Cardinals Big Losers in NFL Week 8 Power Rankings
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals dropped to 2-5 after their Week 7 loss to the Denver Broncos.
Ahead of Week 8, the Cardinals (expectedly) tumbled down various NFL power rankings:
Josh Weinfuss on Kendrick Bourne being the best offseason addition: "The veteran wide receiver, who signed a two-year deal this offseason, has been a reliable third or fourth option for quarterback Jacoby Brissett. That has been especially true after Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded away three weeks ago, as tight end Trey McBride and wide receiver Michael Wilson have gotten a significant amount of attention from defenses. Bourne has 234 yards on 25 catches in seven games. He's on pace for a career high in catches and the third-most receiving yards of his career."
Conor Orr : "Man, the Broncos defense will put you in a terrible headspace."
Pete Prisco : "The high of beating the Rams last week went by the wayside as they were blown out by Denver at home Sunday. They just lack the talent to compete week in and week out."
Nick Shook : "Arizona’s performance in Sunday’s loss to Denver was too predictable. The Cardinals once again became a chuck-and-pray offense on third down, gave up an inexcusable, 62-yard scramble touchdown to Bo Nix, and produced a calamity of errors in the clubhouse leader for worst goal-to-go possession of the year. I feel for Jacoby Brissett, who was brutalized by Denver’s defense. It’s tough to be a Cardinals fan right now."
Mike Florio : "It’s Carson Beck time."
Gary Davenport : "Beck probably isn't the long-term answer at quarterback, but he was a three-year starter at Georgia and then Miami. The Redbirds thought enough of him to spend a Day 2 pick on him.
"And if they're going to get him some game reps, now is the time. After the Cowboys' non-existent defense in Week 8, the Cardinals face Seattle, the Rams and Kansas City.
"This will be a 3-8 team (at best) by the end of November."
Chad Graff on their pass rush being spooky: "The Cardinals have the league’s third-worst passing defense in part because they struggle to generate pressure. The group ranks 27th in pressure rate and 26th in quarterback hits."

title: Cardinals Sign Familiar Face to Address WR Room Injuries
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are bringing back a familiar face.
After losing Jalen Brooks to injured reserve, the Cardinals are signing veteran receiver Zay Jones – who previously played for Arizona for two seasons (2024-25) before not being re-signed this past offseason.
After Brooks was officially placed on IR today following wrist surgery, Jones (who spent time with the Houston Texans in training camp before being cut) was signed to help a depleted receivers room that also lost Marvin Harrison Jr . due to a trade weeks ago.
In related moves today, Arizona officially re-signed offensive lineman Austin Deculus and safety Wydett Williams Jr. to the practice squad and has released safety Jerrick Reed II from the practice squad.
Jones has nine years of NFL experience with over 300 receptions and 3,000 receiving yards. His familiarity with Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort most certainly played a role in helping him get back to the desert.
While current head coach Mike LaFleur doesn't have prior working experience with Jones, former Arizona head coach Jonathan Gannon always sang Jones' praises when asked in press conferences.
“He does his job. He's in the right spot. He can play three spots. He's fast and he's explosive. (He’s a) really good, contested catch guy," Gannon said of Jones last season.
With Jones arriving to a new Cardinals offense under LaFleur, there is some continuity already established with personnel. Jones played with Michael Wilson and Trey McBride previously. Behind Jones, presuming he's eventually worked into Arizona's X receiver role, is fifth-round rookie Reggie Virgil and Simi Fehoko.
LaFleur, asked about replacing Brooks, told reporters it would be done by a committee approach.
“Next man up. I mean, the show goes on, right?" LaFleur said.
"(WR) Reggie’s (Virgil) got a few reps there versus L.A. Didn’t get as many yesterday, but a good week of practice by him. You can do it by committee. (WR) Kendrick (Bourne) can play some X too if we need that. Obviously, (WR) Simi (Fehoko) has done kind of both, but it’ll be by committee.”
The Cardinals, currently 2-5, are dead last in explosive play rates and yards after reception after seven weeks of football. While Jones' presence probably doesn't change those numbers, he does add another veteran presence to a young and overall inexperienced Cardinals' wide receiver room.
Arizona will play the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Jones could potentially be caught up to speed enough to be active for Sunday.

title: 7 Alarming Stats the Cardinals Must Fix Immediately
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 2-5 through just seven weeks of football, and while stats don't always tell the story, it does sprinkle in some context into how a team is performing.
Take for example their latest red zone struggles , which has stalled their offense and overall ability to win games to begin the regular season. Seven weeks is more than enough to gather data and establish a foundation of what a football team is.
While there's a few good things the Cardinals are doing at this point in time, there's several categories where Arizona ranks near the bottom of the league — if not completely alone at No. 32.
Seven alarming stats the Cardinals have to fix, fast:
What it means : The average time quarterbacks spend in the pocket before throwing or moving out.
Why it matters : Jacoby Brissett is getting the ball out at incredibly fast rates, which does keep turnovers and sacks down to a minimum. However, this usually means teams aren't able hit big plays down the field and are often only hitting the first read... which is exactly what Arizona's offense has evolved into with Brissett under center.
What it means : The percentage in which the defensive line is pressuring a quarterback on dropbacks.
Why it matters : The Cardinals have seemingly only been able to manufacture sacks and pressure from exotic looks or blitzes from defensive coordinator Nick Rallis. Great defenses can rush four and drop seven, and Arizona has tried that with little success for far too long. This number only suffers the more time Walter Nolen III misses due to injury.
What it means : The average amount of yards a pass catcher gains after a reception.
Why it matters : If the Cardinals can't hit deep plays down the field, they have to rely on receivers making defenders miss after the catch — which hasn't happened. While Arizona has strong options in Trey McBride and Michael Wilson, neither are exactly known for making defenders miss in the open field. The Cardinals need a spark in their WR room.
What it means : The percentage of explosive plays an offense has. Ten yards for a rush and 20 yards through the air qualifies.
Why it matters : The Cardinals have been forced to dink-and-dunk their way during drives, failing to hit a big play more than any other team in the league. Arizona can't take the top off the defense, make defenders miss after the catch, or block well enough to spring big plays. This falls on a mix of execution and scheme from head coach Mike LaFleur.
What it means : The percentage of drives a defense allows the offense to score on.
Why it matters : The Cardinals' defense is allowing some sort of score on nearly half of their drives, operating in true feast or famine territory. Arizona's defense has unfortunately met low expectations this season by allowing the most amount of points through seven weeks at 208, which is 29.7 points per game. It's basically a coin flip to see if an offense will score against Rallis' unit, and that's not good.
What it means : The percentage of plays where the defense pressures a quarterback on a passing attempt.
Why it matters : Arizona simply isn't getting to the quarterback. Whether it be their defensive line as highlighted above, outside linebackers or whoever else, opposing offenses aren't being pressured nearly close enough  by Arizona's defense to make an impact. Rallis is solid at generating blitzes to manufacture pressure, he just isn't aggressive enough.
What it means : How often a rushing attempt is stopped at or behind the line of scrimmage.
Why it matters: The Cardinals can't run the ball. For what reason remains to be seen, though missing starters along the offensive line doesn't help while LaFleur hasn't found the recipe for success in terms of scheme. Bam Knight's found some success while Tyler Allgeier has been disappointing. Would love to see what Jeremiyah Love can do when he's fully healthy.

title: Cardinals Can No Longer Ignore Their Biggest Problem
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals tried their very best to downplay a problem that now is rearing its ugly head.
The Cardinals enter Week 8 ranked last in red zone efficiency, scoring touchdowns on just 42.86% of opportunities. Arizona has managed to string together long drives, though the difference between three points and seven in the NFL very much can be the difference between wins and losses in a league where over 60% of games come down to one possession.
After going 0-5 in the red zone in their Week 6 loss to the Detroit Lions, LaFleur said the Cardinals wouldn't overreact to one bad week — insisting Arizona had been fine in the red zone previously and the team just needed better coaching and execution.
Week 7 brought another tough week inside the 20s, as the Cardinals went 1-5 in the red zone against the Denver Broncos . Their overall 1-10 outing through the last two games has now tanked Arizona's stats to the bottom of the league, and the Cardinals — whether they want to admit it or not — officially have a problem.
“No, I don’t think it’s a total blowup because up until two weeks ago we were top 10 in goal-to-goal situations. I think we were 13th overall anytime inside the 20, now we’re dead last for obvious reasons," LaFleur told reporters ahead of Week 8.
Data shows the Cardinals were 16th in red zone efficiency at a 61% clip in Weeks 1-5. In the season's totality, Arizona's goal-to-go touchdown percentage (56%) and inside the ten-yard line touchdown percentage (53%) both are ranked second-to-last among NFL teams.
Alarm bells were officially sounded when the Cardinals were at Denver's one-yard line in Week 7, down by 14 with just under two minutes left. Arizona, admittedly altering their approach in hopes to save some clock, struck out on all four attempts to get in the end zone.
"Once we kind of got going a little bit and we were moving it, we weren’t finishing it. Against good teams  — we lucked out the week before because our defense played incredible. We hit six kicks, but you can’t do that every week (and) we know that," LaFleur continued on the red zone struggles.
"It’s like ‘Guys, we’re down there.’ It’s not like we’re not moving the football, but we have to finish. Again, I’ll look in the mirror first and say it starts with me.”
Play-calling changes when you get in the red zone. The field shrinks, and numerous plays/concepts you could normally run are thrown out the window. This places a greater emphasis on not only choosing the right plays, but also execution — which hasn't exactly been a calling card for Arizona's offense to begin the season.
"It’s always going to start with me and the play design. One, the play design and the clarity you’re providing to the guys. Then two, when you’re calling it. It’s always going to start with me," LaFleur said last week. "Then after that, the guys have to go execute it. Sometimes you call the right one and it’s not executed. Sometimes you call the wrong one and guys make a play, but that’ll always start with me.”
It's not as if the Cardinals' offense has been stagnant. They lead the NFL in ten-play drives and are top five in time of possession. They can clearly move the ball.
Yet when it counts, for whatever reason, the Cardinals can't convert field goals into touchdowns. Arizona's strong defensive performance against the Rams was an obvious outlier, one LaFleur and the offensive staff clearly can't rely on.
The Cardinals do know they have a massive problem on their hands, a complex dynamic that doesn't have an easy solution.

title: Cardinals Give Carson Beck Injury Update
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are potentially getting Carson Beck back on the practice field this week.
Beck suffered a back injury that ultimately landed him on last week's injury report. The rookie third-round pick rebounded from a preseason ribs injury that only saw him play one game, and with Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew ahead of him, Beck hasn't played in 2026.
While Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur refused to put a label on Beck's role moving into Week 8, he did say Beck was set to complete a workout today to guage where the Miami product is at.
“Not going to talk about role changes right now, but I’ll know more tomorrow. He’s going to do a workout tomorrow on our off day just to move in the pocket and stuff like that to see where he is in terms of — I guess you could say, ‘rep structure’ starting Wednesday, Thursday (and) Friday," LaFleur said during his Monday press conference.
How did the back injury even happen?
“It just kind of flared up on him honestly. He just had a little bit of a back spasm. Again, when you’re torquing the way these guys torque, that’s not fun. I don’t know if anyone’s ever had back spasms here, but they suck," LaFleur added.
Beck is still awaiting his turn at the wheel of LaFleur's offense, which figures to come down the road as losses continue to pile in Arizona.
When exactly Beck will enter the lineup remains to be seen. The Cardinals won't hand over the keys next week in Dallas after already committing to Brissett despite the team's 2-5 start.
However, we will need to see Beck at some point ahead of a massive 2027 offseason, where the Cardinals just might find themselves in position to take a top-rated quarterback in the draft.
If Beck can convince the Cardinals he's a possible solution at quarterback, Arizona would bypass those opportunities.
Many believe Week 12 is an optimal landing spot for Beck to play, as that would give him multiple games before a bye week and a short stint of easier games to finish the 2026 regular season.
For now, it appears he'll continue to be the team's emergency quarterback on game days. But before any moves can be made, Beck has to be healthy — and it appears we're in line to see him back on the practice field soon.

title: Cardinals' One-Word James Conner Update Raises Questions
full_text:
Arizona Cardinals fans have been wondering where running back James Conner is at in his return to play.
So too has everybody else.
It's been well over a full calander year since Conner went down with a right foot injury (first described as an ankle before eventually corrected by then-coach Jonathan Gannon). Conner, after just three weeks, was ruled out for the season but managed to make a return in 2026's iteration of training camp.
Conner didn't participate in any team drills but did do individual portions through the beginning of camp. He ultimately wasn't spotted at practice in any capacity towards the end of preseason, and he hasn't featured in any sort of game during the 2026 season.
We're now seven games deep into the regular season and Conner has yet to be pulled from his injured reserve slot, which does have a designation to return.
Is Conner going to play at all this season?
"Potentially," said Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur when asked about Conner returning.
"That's all I could give you there."
This conflicts from what Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort told Arizona Sports 98.7 FM last week, where he said Conner is "really close" to a return.
What's going on with Conner?
The veteran running back restructured his contract to stay with the Cardinals this offseason after being labeled as a cut candidate. When Arizona signed Tyler Allgeier in free agency and drafted Jeremiyah Love with the third overall pick, many were curious to see how Conner would fit into the Cardinals' backfield.
There was hope he would be healthy and fully ready to make an impact in LaFleur's new offense, though that's been nowhere close to the case.
While Conner is a coveted locker room leader, Bam Knight's recent surge in play does make Conner expendable. As the league's trade deadline approaches, he's very much a candidate for a deal.
It's also possible the Cardinals would do right by the veteran running back and release him if that's what Conner desires. Teams looking to make a playoff push are constantly looking for players such as Conner for talent and leadership reasons.
The Cardinals, without Conner, have struggled in the run game. Arizona ranks in the bottom ten for team rushing yards per game and average yards per carry this season.
Arizona's been very silent of where Conner stands during his rehab, almost to concerning levels.

title: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love Gets Exciting Week 8 Injury Update
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are getting Jeremiyah Love back to the practice field this week.
Love, who has missed the last two games with an ankle injury, will take the field on Wednesday as the Cardinals prepare to face the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8.
"We'll see as the week goes," head coach Mike LaFleur said at his Monday press conference. "Jeremiyah will be out there at practice on Wednesday, so we'll see how the week goes."
Love, the third overall pick, initially dealt with a different ankle injury during Arizona's preseason. However, up until Week 6, he hadn't missed a regular season game.
The rookie running back has been managing his new ankle injury for weeks before the Cardinals made the call to shelf the Notre Dame product. Arizona said injured reserve, which would require Love to miss at least four weeks, wasn't on the table.
The Cardinals dropped to 2-5 after their Week 7 loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Their backfield has been headlined by Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier. Knight, particularly, has been strong in Love's absence.
"Bam's doing a really good job. He's running the ball well and obviously brought an explosive element to the run game that was needed," LaFleur said when asked if Knight would still have a role. "So yeah, Bam will still have a role, but I'm excited to get Jeremiyah back, particularly at practice this week."
Arizona's rushing offense ranks in the bottom ten of NFL teams for rushing yards per game (96) and average yards per carry (3.7).
There's hope Love's emergence back into the lineup can also add a new layer to the Cardinals' passing attack, where Love's route-running against linebacker matchups should be extremely advantageous for their struggling offense.
We'll get our first injury report for Week 8 after Wednesday's practice, though this is undoubtedly a massive step in the right direction for Love's return.

title: Cardinals' Josh Sweat Trade Rumors Heat Up as 2 New Teams Emerge
full_text:
ARIZONA — Rumors around Arizona Cardinals OLB Josh Sweat continue to materialize as we approach the league's Nov. 10 trade deadline.
Yesterday, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler suggested the Dallas Cowboys were interested in Sweat's services. Today, after Arizona's Week 7 loss to the Denver Broncos, two other teams have been thrown into the mix by NFL insider Jordan Schultz.
"I think we're heading to a very active NFL trade deadline. We could see anywhere from 12 to call it 20 trades. And two teams I'm watching very closely? The 49ers and Bears. I've heard both teams connected to several defensive players including rushers Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack and also DeForest Buckner," Schultz said on The Pivot :
Jordan Schultz links the Bears to Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack and DeForest Buckner + names not necessarily on the trade block. He adds that he’s be shocked if Chicago didn’t make a move before the NFL Trade Deadline. pic.twitter.com/idX357lnLz
The 49ers would be an interesting move, as trading within the division is typically a no-no. However, San Francisco could sweeten that deal by paying a little extra to get Sweat on their team.
The Bears, meanwhile, would complete the foursome of NFC North teams who have former prominent Cardinals on their squad. Sweat, if acquired by Chicago, would see familiar faces in Detroit (Drew Petzing), Green Bay (Jonathan Gannon) and Minnesota (Kyler Murray).
Something both teams have in common? Success. The 49ers are 6-1 while the Bears are 5-2. Both are clearly looking to make a Super Bowl push, which could lead to a potential bidding war for Sweat's services.
Sweat has two sacks on the regular season after a chaotic offseason surrounding the health of his knee, absence in the offseason and reported trade interest/requests after the Cardinals fired Gannon.
Sweat is reportedly hoping to land a new contract, as the final two years of his deal carry no guaranteed money. He also might be looking to jump ship from a 2-5 football team after failing to help build success in the desert.
Speaking with reporters earlier this offseason, Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort shot down any truth to trade rumors around Arizona's top pass rusher.
"I'd say [trade] discussions that come by that, there's always a lot of talk that goes around that. We have no interest in trading Josh. We're excited to have him," he said back in August. "Some of those discussions [we're] going to keep private. But excited to have Josh here, [he] had a great year last year. Excited for more good things out of him this year."
Of course, things can change, especially if the price is right.

title: Cardinals WR Reveals He's Having Season-Ending Surgery
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are set to lose wide receiver Jalen Brooks for the rest of the 2026 season.
Brooks, in an Instagram post on Monday, says he has to get an "emergency surgery" on his wrist and added he, "doesn't need any phone calls, just prayers."
Brooks met with local reporters after the Cardinals' Week 7 loss to the Denver Broncos and appeared to be in obvious discomfort when speaking. He finished his post with:
"I'll be done for the season, God is in control of my next steps much love."
Arizona Cardinals WR Jalen Brooks announces via his Instagram that he's done for the season following an injury to his wrist. pic.twitter.com/Y4jCi3BdTc
This is a big blow for the Cardinals' offense, who was counting on its depth receivers to step up after trading away Marvin Harrison Jr. weeks ago. After scoring under 20 points in back to back weeks, they'll be under an even bigger microscope as injuries accrue across the board, from the offensive line to running backs and now receivers.
Brooks was a productive preseason player who was buried in a Cardinals offense headlined by Trey McBride and Michael Wilson. However, it was Brooks who was propelled into more playing time after Harrison was dealt.
Brooks had a huge catch in Arizona's upset win over the Los Angeles Rams two weeks ago, which helped the Cardinals kick a game-winning field goal just moments after Brooks dropped an open pass.
“How amazing is just having to be resilient in this league?" Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said when asked about Brooks after Week 6.
"... There's always a chance you're going to have to go out there and have to win it. And for him to make that play and Jacoby to rip it in there, it just says a lot about just that Jalen Brooks and his mindset. And it's cool. A lot of good learning moments for for these guys. We can start plugging them in in the redzone and maybe he doesn't get into this situation.”
Brooks will finish his 2026 season with five receptions for 81 yards. Arizona will look to Simi Fehoko and Reggie Virgil as players who can step up in his role. With Wilson and McBride commanding attention, there should be ample opportunity for backup receivers to make plays for the Cardinals.
The Cardinals travel to Dallas to face the Cowboys in Week 8. LaFleur is set to meet with reporters later this afternoon and is expected to confirm the news of losing Brooks for the season.

title: 3 Key Takeaways From Arizona Cardinals’ Week 7 Loss
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals were unable to build on their upset victory against Los Angeles last weekend. Instead, the Cardinals flew back down to earth, falling to the Denver Broncos 30–16 in Week 7.
With this defeat, the Cardinals have now lost 10 consecutive home games.
"It sucks. You hate losing," head coach Mike LaFleur said postgame. "I hate playing not-good football more than I hate losing cause good football can lead to wins unless they make so many plays.
"Credit to them. That is a good football team. It's a well-coached football team. They're going to win a lot of football games, but I know we can play better than that."
Arizona's offense needs to execute better in the red area. Against the Broncos Sunday, the Cardinals went 1-for-5 inside the red zone.
In their last ten red zone trips, Arizona has scored only one touchdown.
"We're moving the ball, and we're not finishing. That's a collective deal with coaching and playing," Mike LaFleur told J.P. Shadrick and A.Q. Shipley on the Cardinals Locker Room Show.
"There was opportunities to make plays. There's opportunities to call better plays. There's opportunities to have some better scheme. So it's a collective deal right now. Again, like I told the guys, we're not going to panic after one week. But now we've had two weeks where we haven't cashed it in."
Due to their recent struggles, the Cardinals now rank last in the league in red-zone scoring percentage (touchdowns only) at 42.8%, per TeamRankings.
Jacoby Brissett is going to need an ice bath after this one. The Cardinals quarterback was under siege the entire afternoon.
Denver's "Orange Crush" defense recorded 13 quarterback hits and a season-high 27 quarterback pressures, per Next Gen Stats.
"He got hit a little bit," LaFleur said to the media postgame. "With their defensive structure, you knew we were going to have to get it over the top. When you do that, you're going to hold onto the ball a little longer."
Coach LaFleur wasn't lying. Brissett 2.82-second time to throw was his longest this season, but it was all for naught. Per Next Gen Stats, the Cardinals allowed a pressure rate of 50.9%. Simply put, Arizona's offensive line was outclassed against Denver's front.
The Broncos didn't come into this week's matchup as an offensive juggernaut. Per Next Gen Stats, Denver ranked 26th in scoring (19.0 PPG), 31st in yards per game (252 YPG), and 32nd in yards per play (4.4).
However, against the Cardinals, the Broncos matched their season high, scoring 30 points. On the day, Denver produced 377 total yards of offense, and 6.7 yards per play.
The Cardinals continue to struggle on defense. They have allowed 30+ points in five of their last six games. Through seven weeks, Arizona's defense has allowed the most points in the NFL.

title: Did Falcons Find their Franchise QB in Michael Penix Jr.? SI's Albert Breer Weighs In
full_text:
It's a popular refrain that the Atlanta Falcons have been in quarterback purgatory since trading Matt Ryan prior to the 2022 season. That's only partially true. Sure, Ryan was the unquestioned starter during his time in Atlanta, but he hadn't had a passer rating above 15th in the NFL since 2018.
The Falcons haven't either.
It's no coincidence that as the Falcons have been poor at the position for the better part of the last decade, the team hasn't had a winning season, and those losing seasons predate the Ryan trade.
The quarterback conundrum was still the biggest question entering the Falcons season under first-year head coach Kevin Stefanski. Between Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa, it was actually a two-part question. Did they have a quarterback who was good enough to be a franchise guy, and could he stay healthy long enough to become that guy?
After seven weeks, the first part of that question looks to have been answered. Penix is having a breakout season under Stefanski and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees. While the second part of the question will take time to answer, Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer thinks the door is open for Penix to lock down the long-term job.
"I’m not sure if Michael Penix Jr. is going to be the Falcons’ starter for (the) next five or 10 years, but that door is certainly opening," Breer wrote on SI . "And Sunday in Atlanta was a really good step in that direction. On the other side was a veteran 49ers defense that had held four of its six opponents to 17 points or fewer through a 6–0 start. A defense that, on this Sunday, was good enough to hold Bijan Robinson to 63 rushing yards on 20 carries."
Breer took note of Penix's numbers this season and was impressed. His passer rating is No. 4 in the NFL among quarterbacks with at least five starts. What he left out, though, is that four out of Penix's five starts have come against teams with a winning record: Packers (4-3), Ravens (4-3), Bears (5-2), and 49ers (6-1).
"That gives Penix a 3–2 record as a starter, following Atlanta’s 0–2 start without him, and this stat line through five games: 96-of-144 (66.7%), 1,157 yards, 9 TDs, 1 INT, 109.1 rating. Which is more remarkable when you consider he’s just two months and two days past his first 11-on-11 practice in Kevin Stefanski’s system, and coming off his third ACL surgery," Breer continued.
It's a far cry from how the season started. Cooper Rush was forced into action after being plucked off his couch at the start of training camp, and the Falcons predictably went 0-2. Tagovailoa couldn't make it to Week 1 without a series of soft-tissue injuries, and Penix was still recovering from surgery.
"At that point, Atlanta looked nowhere at the position. That’s not the case anymore," Breer concluded.
Penix has proven that he's good enough to keep the Falcons from selecting a possible replacement in the first round of next year's draft. Now it's up to him to put the injury concerns behind him and continue playing at a high level.
Scott is an Atlanta-based sports media professional with stints as Director of Scouting of Scout.com, VP of Content Production at Sports Illustrated, and Managing Editor at CBS Interactive / 247 Sports, among others.

title: Falcons Big Winners in Week 8 NFL Power Rankings after Upsetting 49ers
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have already been on a roller coaster season. They began the season 0-2 and look like they're going to be in the running for the No. 1 overall pick in April's NFL Draft. Michael Penix Jr. comes back, and they look like a legitimate playoff threat.
They stumbled against the Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore Ravens team that was beatable, before getting their doors blown off by the Chicago Bears.
So naturally, they beat the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.
I think we can wipe the first two games off the board while the team was playing Cooper Rush after signing him as an emergency quarterback the day training camp opened. If we do that, we see a 3-2 team that has shown signs of being really good with a competent quarterback under center.
So, it's no surprise the national media has been slow to get behind this Falcons team after a big win. This isn't a team that has handled the spotlight very well in the past.
But there are signs this year could be different with talent up and down the offense, and an overachieving defense that will be getting some key players back soon, including edge rusher James Pearce Jr. in two weeks.
NFL Network's Nick Shook is driving the Falcons' bandwagon. He's been a fan of this team from the beginning of the season and has moved Atlanta up from No. 19 to No. 13. He's just as apprehensive as any Falcons fan about the lofty ranking.
"Look, I’m with you: I don’t know who the Falcons are, either," Shook wrote . "They were an inspired bunch on Sunday, outplaying a strong 49ers. Michael Penix Jr. looks very comfortable in Kevin Stefanski’s offense, and Jeff Ulbrich’s defense played with a higher level of aggression. A win like this makes me believe in this team. Hopefully, it doesn't deliver the opposite this Sunday in Tampa."
The Buccaneers are coming off a strange blowout win against the Carolina Panthers. The score was 43-13, and Tampa has 64 passing yards.
SI gave the Falcons the biggest jump in the rankings this week, going from No. 23 to No. 16, first in the NFC South.
"Tommy Rees called one heck of a game against the 49ers, taking Michael Penix’s struggles against secondary blitzes and turning the offense into something that offered plenty of comfort blanket throws while also rolling him out of trouble," Connor Orr wrote on SI .
Pete Prisco may have felt burned earlier in the season after elevating the Falcons after a big win over Green Bay. He had the Falcons at No. 23 coming into the week and moved them to No. 19 after their win over San Francisco.
"Rallying to beat the 49ers is big for this team after losing two straight. The defense made the plays when they needed to be made," Prisco wrote on CBS Sports .
ESPN is the only outlet that doesn't provide any corresponding context for their power rankings. They gave the Falcons the smallest rise, going from No. 22 to No. 19, and they left the 49ers in the No. 1 spot.
The Falcons have seen these ups and downs before over the course of the last few seasons. The arrow is pointing in the right direction now, but in order to make believers out of more people, and more importantly, advance their playoff agenda, they'll need to beat a 2-5 Buccaneers team in Tampa on Sunday.

title: Kendal Daniels Wasn't Only Falcons Rookie with a Dramatic Return vs. 49ers
full_text:
After fumbling twice on special teams against the Chicago Bears, Atlanta Falcons rookie Zachariah Branch received encouragement from his teammates, including running back Bijan Robinson, who prayed with the rookie and helped him regain his confidence heading into the following week.
While linebacker Kendal Daniels got most of the attention for his big game , he wasn't the only rookie who bounced back in a big way on Sunday.
Branch responded exactly how the Falcons hoped, delivering a huge spark that gave Atlanta a much-needed spark in its 29- 20 victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.
Rather than allowing his mistakes against Chicago to define him, Branch returned with renewed confidence and made an immediate impact. His explosive return on Atlanta’s opening possession after San Francisco scored its first touchdown gave the Falcons possession at the 49ers’ 36-yard line. The field position helped set up a 39-yard field goal by Nick Folk, providing an important response.
“Obviously, that big return got us going,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said.
The return was a significant moment for Branch, who remained in the team’s plans despite his costly mistakes the previous week. Atlanta’s coaching staff continued to express confidence in the rookie, allowing him an opportunity to learn from the experience rather than lose his role.
Bijan Robinson praised Branch’s response and talked about his importance.
“That’s how you become the player you want to become if you just keep that faith throughout the week, you keep working hard throughout the week, and then the results will be there when you do everything right,” Robinson said.
That message carried particular weight after Robinson supported Branch during the difficult aftermath of the Bears game. The veteran running back’s encouragement, along with the confidence shown by the coaching staff and teammates, helped reinforce that one bad performance would not determine the rookie’s future in Atlanta.
Branch rewarded that belief against San Francisco. His 61-yard kickoff return helped establish favorable field position, while Atlanta’s kickoff return unit finished with 126 total return yards.
Branch also contributed offensively, recording one reception for nine yards and an eight-yard rushing attempt. Although his offensive numbers remained modest, his impact on special teams demonstrated the explosiveness that initially made him an intriguing addition to Atlanta’s roster.
Special teams coordinator Craig Aukerman and the Falcons’ coaching staff have repeatedly expressed confidence in Branch’s ability to make plays. His speed and versatility give Atlanta a potential difference-maker in the return game, provided he continues protecting the football and making sound decisions.
The Falcons will need that progress to continue. Sunday’s performance was an important step for Branch, who turned a difficult week into an opportunity to help Atlanta secure a statement victory against an undefeated opponent.

title: How Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. Is Beginning to Find His Footing as an NFL Starter
full_text:
When the Atlanta Falcons desperately needed a win, Michael Penix Jr. delivered arguably his best performance as an NFL quarterback.
Trailing the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers 14-3 at the beginning of the second quarter, Penix helped Atlanta spark 23 unanswered points en route to completing a 29-20 comeback in Week 7 on Sunday, Oct. 25.
“Poise, calmness,” said Falcons wide receiver Drake London . “He’s the calmest one out there. He just deals. That’s just MP.”
Penix finished completing 25-of-34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns. It was his second consecutive three-touchdown performance, following last week’s 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears.
“Mike was really good throughout the day,” Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said. “That’s a very good defense; they’re excellent. And they don’t give up big plays. We took our shots when we had them, and when we didn’t, I think Mike saw it really well.”
A large portion of Penix’s successful afternoon was Atlanta’s offensive line play, which was nearly flawless in protection.
And that was against a 49ers defense that entered the game No. 4 in NFL total defense and in the top half of the pass rushing, led by defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, a former head coach of Atlanta.
According to ESPN’s Nick Wagoner, Penix was only pressured three times out of 34 dropbacks.
“It was unbelievable,” Penix said. “To see those guys, the work that they put in every day throughout the week, for them to come out this game, and I don’t get pressured much at all – it’s awesome to be able to see. Those guys work extremely hard, so credit to what they’ve been doing.”
“I don’t remember being hit too many times at all,” Penix added.
After an incompletion on his very first pass, clean pockets helped Penix complete 11 straight completions. Checkdowns, opportunistic shots downfield, and taking care of the football.
“Just making sure we didn’t make any mistakes and go out there and play our brand of football,” Penix said. “We’ve got guys around with the skillset to get open. So for me, I just got to find a way to get them the ball whenever that opportunity is there.”
After basically redshirting his rookie year and then partially tearing his ACL last year, Penix has posted a stat line of 1,157 passing yards, nine touchdowns, and a lone interception. His 109.1 passer rating is fourth in the NFL among quarterbacks with at least five starts this season.
“It’s been great,” Falcons running back Bijan Robinson said when asked about Penix’s development. “I think he’s been growing a lot as a player and doing a lot of great stuff for the offense. He wants to continue to get better. But his process has been really good. And I’m excited to keep playing with him every game coming up.”
Penix now has a full season’s worth of NFL starts at 17. He’s 7-10 as a starter, but more importantly, he's 3-2 this season.
And he’s starting to take command of what this Falcons offense is and what it could potentially be.
“We trust Mike,” Stefanski said. “I know he’s a young player in terms of starts in this league. I get that part. But we trust him.”
The Falcons next travel near Penix’s hometown of Dade City to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in an NFC South clash this Sunday at 1 p.m.

title: Falcons Star Jessie Bates Proves He's the Heartbeat of Atlanta's Defense
full_text:
ATLANTA – The Atlanta Falcons stunned the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. They forced four turnovers and locked down in the second half to win 29-20.
There was plenty to love in the win, but a familiar face led the way.
Falcons safety Jessie Bates III has been a menace to opposing teams since arriving in Atlanta, and he was again on Sunday. He snagged an acrobatic interception that likely kept points off the board for the 49ers, then delivered the game-sealing play in the fourth quarter, punching the ball away from tight end George Kittle to force another turnover.
This interception by Jessie Bates III is UNREAL. SFvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/R4UDkkfGcb
“That interception is as good as it gets,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said. “We needed a play in that moment. The ball skills and the wherewithal and the awareness, the toe-drag swag, that's pretty damn good for a safety. So, really proud of Jessie for just being so aware of that football and making a play and then knocking it out later. I mean, he's playing at a high level.”
Bates’ ability to create turnovers isn't new, but his performance against San Francisco reminded everyone how valuable he can be to Atlanta's defense.
According to Tori McElhaney, only four players have recorded at least six career games with both an interception and a forced fumble. Five of Bates' six such performances have come in a Falcons uniform.
For his teammates, it was little surprise to watch him deliver.
“That’s who he is as a player,” quarterback Michael Penix Jr. said. “Obviously, as a person, he’s great as well. But what we saw out of Jessie (on Sunday) is who he is. That’s who we see every day: just a guy with a nose for the football who makes big-time plays whenever we need them. So it was awesome to be able to see him do that.”
Since 2023, Bates has 14 interceptions, including three returned for touchdowns, and 10 forced fumbles. No player has more combined takeaways in that timeframe.
The production has made Bates one of the NFL's most disruptive defensive backs, but his value to Atlanta extends beyond the raw numbers. He has served as a team captain every year as a Falcon and has been one of the defense's most dependable leaders.
That leadership mattered almost as much as his takeaways on Sunday, with Kendal Daniels wearing the green dot as the defensive signal-caller. The rookie linebacker was an incredible story, but he credited Bates as the calming presence he needed throughout the game.
“Jessie is everybody's role model,” linebacker Josh Woods said. “Just the way he prepares, how smart he is, how he handles himself day in and day out. You know exactly who you're going to get, what you're going to get. If I had to place a heartbeat on our defense, I would say it's Jessie Bates for sure.”
For a team still finding its identity under Stefanski, that influence matters even more, and it extends well beyond his on-field play. His preparation, football intelligence, and consistency have helped establish this standard.
Bates has been doing that since he arrived in Atlanta. Against the 49ers, he reminded everyone why the Falcons' defense keeps running through him.

title: Falcons Sign Former Philadelphia Eagles Tight End, per Report
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are signing former Philadelphia Eagles tight end E.J. Jenkins to their practice squad, per Aaron Wilson , adding another player with ties to the NFC East organization.
Jenkins appeared in all six games for Philadelphia this season, starting two contests. He did not record a reception but contributed on special teams, finishing with two tackles. The tight end played 79% of the Eagles’ special teams snaps and 18% of their offensive snaps before being released.
Jenkins joins a growing list of former Eagles who have found their way to Atlanta.
Jenkins joins safety Sydney Brown, wide receiver Jahan Dotson, defensive back Robert Longerbeam, defensive end Za’Darius Smith, wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus and quarterback Andy Dalton as players with Philadelphia ties connected to the Falcons.
Jenkins entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the New York Jets in 2023 after playing college football at St. Francis, South Carolina, and Georgia Tech.
Originally a wide receiver, Jenkins transitioned to tight end during his professional career. His 6-foot-6 frame provides the size to contribute as a blocker while offering developmental potential as a receiving option.
After the Jets released him during roster cuts in August 2023, Jenkins joined the Eagles’ practice squad. He also spent time with the Las Vegas Raiders’ practice squad before returning to Philadelphia in January 2024.
Jenkins recorded the first touchdown of his NFL regular season career during the 2024 campaign, catching a seven-yard pass from quarterback Tanner McKee in Philadelphia’s Week 18 victory over the New York Giants.
He remained in the Eagles’ organization through their Super Bowl LIX championship season, appearing in eight regular season games and all four postseason contests.
Jenkins has recorded one career regular-season reception for seven yards and a touchdown. His contributions have primarily come through special teams and providing depth at tight end.
The move gives the Falcons another option at tight end while adding depth to their practice squad. Jenkins’ experience playing special teams could be particularly valuable as Atlanta evaluates its roster for the remainder of the season.
His limited offensive production means he will likely need to earn opportunities through practice and his contributions in other phases of the game. However, his familiarity with the Eagles’ system and experience on a championship roster provide additional background as he begins another opportunity.
Jenkins will now look to turn his latest opportunity into a chance to contribute in Atlanta.  For now, the tight end provides additional depth and special teams experience as the Falcons continue building their roster for the second half of the season.

title: Kyle Pitts, Nick Muse Make National Tight Ends Day Count in Falcons’ Win Over 49ers
full_text:
National Tight Ends Day gave the Atlanta Falcons another reason to appreciate their tight end room, but Kyle Pitts Sr. and Nick Muse made sure the occasion came with production on the field.
The Atlanta Falcons defeated the San Francisco 49ers 29- 20 on Sunday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, handing the previously undefeated visitors their first loss of the season.
Pitts and Muse each caught a touchdown from Michael Penix Jr., helping Atlanta overcome an early deficit and secure a statement victory.
For Pitts, National Tight Ends Day is one of the best occasions on the NFL calendar.
“It’s definitely one of the greatest holidays beside Christmas,” Pitts said.
The Falcons tight end backed up his enthusiasm with another touchdown reception, continuing a productive stretch in which he has scored in three consecutive games. Pitts finished with five catches on five targets for 22 yards and a touchdown, while also reaching 300 career receptions.
HAPPY NATIONAL TIGHT ENDS DAY KP! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/CwdtcwKPHk
He became the sixth youngest tight end in NFL history to reach that milestone, adding another accomplishment to his career as one of Atlanta’s primary receiving threats.
However, Pitts was not the only tight end who found the end zone. Muse delivered one of the afternoon’s most memorable moments when he caught his first career NFL touchdown in the second quarter.
Trailing 14-3, Atlanta needed a spark. Penix found Muse on a first-and-goal play from the one-yard line, giving the tight end a milestone he will remember long after Sunday’s victory.
Our MUSE on National Tight End's Day! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/UQNMR1Pvrb
Pitts was thrilled to see his teammate get his opportunity.
“It was amazing,” Pitts said. “I love when the tight end scores, especially on our holiday.”
Pitts added that seeing Muse record his first was special.
“It was pretty cool to see him be his first, and, you know, we’ll cherish that moment,” Pitts said.
The touchdowns highlighted a tight end group that contributed beyond the scoreboard. Austin Hooper recorded two receptions for 21 yards, while Charlie Woerner added a nine-yard catch and continued to provide a physical presence as a blocker.
Their combined numbers were particularly important in a game that demanded Atlanta respond after falling behind early. The Falcons eventually took control, using a balanced team effort to finish off San Francisco and improve their standing in a competitive NFC.
For Pitts, the victory offered the perfect combination of individual achievement and team success. He reached a career milestone, extended his touchdown streak, and watched another member of his position group score his first NFL touchdown.
National Tight Ends Day may only come once a season, but Atlanta’s performance showed the value of having multiple tight ends capable of making a difference when their opportunities arrive.

title: Falcons Defense Sends Clear Message After Beating Undefeated 49ers
full_text:
ATLANTA – The word “identity” swirled around the Atlanta Falcons ’ locker room on Sunday evening. Winless at home this season and, more often than not, outnumbered in their own stands, the Falcons' defense knew the assignment started with them.
“Identity is a good word,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said. “You can talk about it until you're blue in the face, and you can put it on a T-shirt, but we gotta go do it. We gotta go be who we say we are, and I thought today we did that.”
They were tasked with slowing down an undefeated San Francisco 49ers team that, despite a depleted wide receiver room, was loaded with stars. Christian McCaffrey, Brock Purdy, George Kittle, and an overpowering offensive line are more than enough for Kyle Shanahan's wizardry. His unit was third in scoring offense (29.5) and second in EPA/play (+0.16).
“That’s a great offense, great coaches, and a quarterback and team playing as well as anybody in this league,” Stefanski said about the 49ers. “So, you’re not going to shut them out. We understood it was going to be a 60-minute game.”
After the first three possessions, it looked like the Falcons would be just another team the 49ers checked off en route to a playoff run. They raced to a 14-3 lead and piled up 150 yards, with Christian McCaffrey nearly hitting 100 yards on his own.
San Francisco was in full control.
The Falcons’ defensive identity had wavered in recent weeks. Against the 49ers, it held.
“We didn't have the first half that we would like,” defensive lineman Gervon Dexter Sr. said. “To come out and make those adjustments and do some of those things and fix some of those things and come out, that takes a detailed team.”
Atlanta never fully shut down the 49ers, but they punished them for every mistake. San Francisco outgained Atlanta by 105 yards, but the Falcons forced four turnovers, including on both of their final two possessions, plus another turnover on downs. They sacked Purdy twice, defended seven passes, and finished with six tackles for loss.
The Falcons’ defense gave the 49ers everything they could handle.
“We want to get off the field early enough, so we're going to be able to make the big plays, the game-changing plays,” Maason Smith said. “We want to continue on that road throughout the rest of the season.”
And after running for 105 yards in the first half, San Francisco managed just 18 rushing yards in the second. A hampered McCaffrey played a role, but so did this Atlanta defense's mentality.
“They're a team that prides themselves on running the ball, and everything we do is centered around stopping the run,” linebacker Josh Woods said. “They got some leaky yards, whatever. They had some good runs. But it was definitely an identity game. It was a heavyweight fight.”
The Falcons had plenty of heroes, including safety Jessie Bates III and rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels , but this was a total team win for this defense. Woods believes this group earned some of that respect on Sunday.
Now, the challenge is doing that again.
“It’s an identity game every week,” cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. said, “and just being able to go out and do what we practice all week, and just going out there trying to prove us right. Prove we are who we are. So, every week is an identity game.”

title: Falcons Rookie Goes From Scary Injury to Game-Sealing Hero in One Week
full_text:
ATLANTA – Seven days ago, Kendal Daniels was rushed to Grady Hospital following a scary injury at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. On Sunday, the rookie linebacker sealed the Atlanta Falcons ’ Week 7 win over the San Francisco 49ers with an interception and fumble recovery.
Daniels spent nearly 10 minutes on the turf as medical staff tended to him after he took a knee on the helmet. That personnel ultimately immobilized him and carted him off the field. In the hours following the game, media members saw him walking in the locker room, and there was a sense of relief.
What came next is still hard to believe.
He not only recovered, but did so in time to suit up and play against the previously undefeated 49ers. He filled in for Divine Deablo, wore the green dot, led the Falcons in tackles, and recorded two takeaways.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski called it remarkable, and the player called it the craziest week of his life.
“I've never not walked off the field after an injury,” Daniels said after the game. “Mentally, I had to be prepared and going back home and just making sure I was okay mentally more than anything, and not playing timid. I've never not gotten up from an injury. So, being stretched off the field ­– I won't let it happen again. It was a bad feeling, and I'm blessed to be able to play this week.”
Daniels avoided a major injury last week, but he couldn't move his neck in the days after the game. By Wednesday, he was practicing and feeling better each day.
“He’s a dog,” defensive lineman Gervon Dexter Sr. said. “Not a lot of players will go out there and play after something like that happened. He did, and he got all our respect in this building.”
Linebacker Josh Woods spoke with Daniels on Sunday after the “scary” injury, but never doubted that he would be down for long.
“He’s got whatever ‘it’ is,” Woods said. “Everything that he does is pretty dope. Then, for last week to go how it went, and then for him to have the game that he had today, it's a testament to his preparation. He's kind of got that ‘X-factor’, that ‘it’-thing about him.”
That ‘it factor’ showed in the waning minutes on Sunday.
Daniels’ interception snuffed out a 49ers possession that started at midfield and could have put San Francisco in front. The Falcons had just gone three-and-out, and it felt like momentum had flipped entirely in the away team's favor.
Instead, the rookie stepped in front of a Brock Purdy pass and returned it to the Falcons’ red zone. Nick Folk converted the field goal, making it a two-score game.
He recovered a fumble on the next drive, and that officially ended it.
“He put his head down and goes to work every day,” Maason Smith said. “He understands that nothing is given. Everything is earned. When you have size and speed like him, with a mind like his, and you combine both of those things together. Man, there's nothing but excellence waiting to happen.”

title: Winners and Losers from Falcons' 29-20 Win Over 49ers
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons upset the San Francisco 49ers 29-20 in Sunday's Week 7 matchup.
It's the biggest win of the season for a Falcons team coming off a loss to the Bears last week, and it’s now their first home win of the season.
Here are the winners and losers from Atlanta's victory at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Penix delivered an efficient performance against San Francisco, completing 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns without throwing an interception. The Falcons quarterback consistently made the most of his opportunities, helping Atlanta score enough points to secure a nine-point victory.
Penix's three touchdown passes were the highlight of his afternoon. He connected with Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and Nick Muse for scores, spreading the ball around and keeping the 49ers' defense from focusing on one primary target.
Atlanta's passing attack was particularly effective in the red zone, where the Falcons capitalized on their opportunities. Penix also demonstrated improved decision-making by protecting the football and avoiding costly mistakes.
The Falcons managed just 25 yards of offense in the first quarter, making their eventual offensive production even more impressive. Penix helped Atlanta overcome that sluggish start and finish with a winning performance against one of the NFC's top teams.
Smith was one of Atlanta's biggest defensive difference makers, recording a sack, forcing a fumble, batting down a pass, finishing with two tackles for loss and adding a quarterback hit.
His performance demonstrated the impact he can make when he consistently disrupts opposing offenses. Smith affected San Francisco's passing game with his pressure while also making plays behind the line of scrimmage.
The forced fumble was an especially important moment in a game where Atlanta needed its defense to deliver timely stops.
Smith's performance was one of the most encouraging individual developments from Sunday's victory. Atlanta will need that type of production from its defensive line as it moves forward through the season.
Daniels had a memorable afternoon after entering the week with questions surrounding his availability following last week's injury concerns.
The rookie linebacker made his presence felt in Atlanta's 29-20 win, recording three tackles and one assist while contributing to a defense that made several crucial plays.
Daniels also recovered a late fumble to help the Falcons close out the victory. Jessie Bates III punched the ball out, and Daniels was in position to secure the recovery, giving Atlanta possession at a critical point in the fourth quarter.
BOOM! @KendalDaniels__ picks it off! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/7VBExpgNMh
After uncertainty about whether he would be able to play, Daniels' return was an encouraging development. Not only was he back on the field, but he also made an important contribution to a win over a talented opponent.
For a young defender, being available after an injury scare and making a decisive play in a game of this magnitude is a significant moment. Daniels deserves credit for getting back on the field and helping Atlanta finish the job.
Jessie Bates just always seems to be around the football. Bates came through with one of the game's biggest defensive plays, intercepting Brock Purdy in the red zone to prevent San Francisco from capitalizing on a scoring opportunity.
The veteran interception was a momentum-changing play, particularly because it denied the 49ers a chance to add points in a close contest. Bates displayed excellent awareness and positioning to make the takeaway when Atlanta needed a stop.
JB3 in his own league 🔥 FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/1mdXYHdXKY
He also helped seal the victory late in the fourth quarter by punching the ball out and creating the fumble that Daniels recovered.
Bates showed why having an experienced playmaker in the secondary is so valuable. His interception helped prevent San Francisco from scoring, while his forced fumble helped Atlanta regain possession and protect its lead.
In a game where the Falcons needed their defense to make plays at critical moments, Bates delivered twice.
National Tight Ends Day turned into a productive occasion for Atlanta's tight end group, which contributed two touchdown receptions and an important career milestone.
Pitts led the way with five receptions for 22 yards and a touchdown. His scoring reception was one of Penix's three touchdown passes, and Pitts also reached 300 career receptions during the game.
Austin Hooper added two receptions for 21 yards, while Charlie Woerner caught one pass for nine yards. Nick Muse finished with two receptions for two yards and a touchdown, providing another scoring option for Atlanta.
Our MUSE on National Tight End's Day! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/UQNMR1Pvrb
Muse's touchdown was particularly valuable because it demonstrated the Falcons' ability to find production beyond their established offensive playmakers. Pitts also delivered in the red zone, helping Atlanta turn a passing opportunity into points.
The group provided Penix with reliable targets throughout the game, and having multiple tight ends contribute helped diversify the offense.
Pitts reaching 300 career receptions was a notable individual accomplishment, but the entire group deserves recognition for helping Atlanta secure the victory.
Atlanta's kickoff return unit provided an important boost in field position, with Zachariah Branch and Khalil Herbert combining for 126 return yards.
Branch delivered a 60-yard return, while Herbert added a 38-yard return to open the second half. Both plays gave the Falcons opportunities to start drives with favorable field position and helped generate momentum.
Explosive returns can have a significant impact in close games, especially when an offense is working to establish consistency. Atlanta's return unit helped ease some of that pressure by creating opportunities for Penix and the offense.
Herbert's return to begin the second half was particularly important because it gave Atlanta a strong start coming out of the locker room.
The Falcons received a boost from their special teams, and the return unit deserves recognition for helping the team control field position in a nine-point victory.
The Falcons’ offensive line took a lot of criticism after last week’s loss to the Bears. On Sunday, not only did they not give up a sack, but the 49ers weren’t credited with even a hit on Penix.
Atlanta's opening quarter was far from ideal, as the Falcons managed just 25 yards of total offense and punted on both of their first two drives.
Against a San Francisco team that entered the matchup undefeated, the slow start put unnecessary pressure on the defense and prevented Atlanta from establishing an early rhythm.
The Falcons struggled to sustain drives, leaving little room for error against a dangerous opponent. Although Penix eventually settled in and threw three touchdown passes, the opening quarter demonstrated how quickly the offense can stall when it cannot consistently move the chains.
Atlanta deserves credit for adjusting and finding ways to score, but a 25 yard opening quarter is not a formula the team should want to repeat. Against other playoff contenders, a similarly sluggish start could prove much more costly.
The Falcons got the result they wanted, but the early offensive struggles remain an area to address moving forward.
Atlanta's run defense had some difficult moments against San Francisco's ground attack, allowing 123 rushing yards on 23 carries. That amounted to approximately 5.3 yards per attempt, giving the 49ers opportunities to move the chains on the ground.
Kaelon Black led San Francisco with 63 rushing yards on 12 carries, including a 30-yard run and a touchdown. Christian McCaffrey added 39 yards on seven attempts and another rushing touchdown.
