title: What Josh Allen Must Do to Win His Second Career MVP
full_text:
A lot can change from Week 7 to Week 18 in the NFL , but MVP campaigns rely on season-long success.
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen may seem like the early favorite to many, but a recent ESPN poll of NFL execs, coaches and personnel has a different QB atop the ballot.
So, what would Allen need to achieve in Buffalo's final 11 games to bring home more hardware?
According to Cameron Wolfe's poll, 49ers QB Brock Purdy received six out of 16 votes in the exercise.
It's important to note that this was published prior to San Francisco's 29-20 loss to the Falcons, which included Purdy throwing two interceptions and taking two sacks in the team's first loss of the season.
Even so, one AFC assistant GM even said that "Josh Allen is the easy answer." However, their pick was still Purdy "because of impact in that scheme despite all their injuries...His numbers and the way he does it may not be as gaudy as Allen, but he's very valuable."
Allen still finished second in the poll with four votes. An NFC defensive coach said, "It's gotta be Josh Allen right now. He won the game vs. the Rams by himself! Damn he's good!"
Wolfe cited Allen's improbable touchdown to Keon Coleman against the Raiders as a "perfect example of him putting on his superhero cape to save the day in unorthodox and often wild ways."
Third on the ballot was Kenneth Walker with three votes, but this was prior to Seattle holding him to just 57 total yards on Sunday night. Bijan Robinson and Jaxon Smith-Njigba were the other vote getters, illustrating how wide-open the race is through seven weeks.
Through six games, Allen is 114 of 171 for 1,504 passing yards and nine passing touchdowns, while adding 48 rushes for 240 yards and a league-leading eight touchdowns on the ground. His 17 total touchdowns currently lead the league, even after Week 7.
His 17-game pace with these numbers includes 4,261 passing yards, 680 rushing yards and 48 total touchdowns. All of this is within reach since the Bills have the eighth-easiest remaining schedule and a defense that would need drastic measures to suddenly become a viable unit.
For what it's worth, San Francisco has the 12th-easiest remaining schedule, while Purdy is currently on pace for 10 fewer touchdowns. Plus, top wideout Mike Evans is currently dealing with rib and Achilles injuries, making his short-term availability uncertain.
Is it possible Allen keeps the pace mentioned above? Of course. Is it realistic to expect he keeps this pace? Of course not.
Instead, Allen needs to continue leading the most explosive offense in football, and stack wins against premiere opponents. Taking care of a Ravens team that will likely have Lamar Jackson back would be a good start, followed by a chance to hand the Minnesota Vikings their first loss of the season if they defeat the Lions in Week 8.
Buffalo's QB also has the advantage of multiple primetime holiday games, playing the Chiefs on Thanksgiving and the Broncos on Christmas. His performances in those games will be crucial.
Unfortunately, in a social media driven world, the MVP is as much about performance as it is about narrative. Allen has a strong start to his MVP campaign narrative - dissecting a vaunted Texans defense in Week 1, defeating the Lions on Thursday Night Football and carrying the Bills to his first overtime victory in a Monday Night thriller against the Rams are all details that matter in this race.
Only four execs and coaches may vote for Allen now, but he's in pole position to strengthen his legacy with a second MVP award.

title: Bills' Post-Bye Schedule: Five NFL Primetime Exposures vs. Winning Teams Await
full_text:
It's certainly somewhat of a surprise that the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens will not take center stage in a featured NFL viewing window in Week 8.
Instead, the November 1 battle between the two preseason AFC favorites will kick off at 1 p.m. ET alongside seven other games in that time slot.
Following the home game against the Ravens, however, the Bills, led by NFL MVP favorite Josh Allen, will become primetime darlings over the season's final two months.
Five of their final 10 regular season games will be standalone features, and all five opponents currently own winning records. We wrote about how challenging the Bills' post-bye schedule is shaping up to be.
The stretch begins on Monday Night Football against the Minnesota Vikings. The Bills visit Minnesota to close out the NFL's Week 9 slate on November 9. Then, it's back-to-back 1 p.m. kickoffs against divisional foes in Weeks 10 and 11 before returning to the spotlight on Thanksgiving night in Week 12 .
Buffalo, which will also play a standalone game on Christmas , will appear on Sunday Night Football and a special Saturday primetime affair during the month of December.
Date: Monday, November 9 Network: ESPN (8:15 p.m.) Venue: U.S. Bank Stadium
It'll be the Bills' first trip to Minnesota since Josh Allen's rookie year. The Vikings (6-0) are currently the NFL's lone remaining unbeaten. They'll visit the Lions before hosting Buffalo.
Date: Thursday, November 26 Network: NBC (8:20 p.m.) Venue: Highmark Stadium
The Bills have beaten the Chiefs during the regular season in each of the past five years, and the way things look at this point, this Thanksgiving game could wind up determining the No. 1 seed in the AFC. Kansas City is 5-1 after suffering a Week 7 road loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
Date: Sunday, December 13 Network: NBC (8:20 p.m.) Venue: Lambeau Field
This trip to Green Bay kicks off three consecutive weeks of featured games for the Bills. The Packers, who made the playoffs last year, are 4-3 through the season's first seven weeks.
Date: Saturday, December 19 Network: NBC (8:20 p.m.) Venue: Highmark Stadium
The Bills host the Bears and quarterback Caleb Williams for a Saturday night special in Orchard Park. Chicago, which beat the Packers in the playoffs last year, owns a 5-2 record heading into Week 8.
Date: Friday, December 25 Network: Netflix (4:30 p.m.) Venue: Mile High Stadium
It's a rematch of the 2025 AFC Divisional Round that was ultimately decided on the Brandin Cooks catch-turned-interception . The Broncos are 5-2 thus far, only one-half game behind the Chiefs in the AFC West standings.

title: Bills Trade Deadline Tracker: Rumors For Buffalo With Two Weeks Left
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is just two weeks away as we turn the page to Week 8 of the season, when the Buffalo Bills will be returning from their bye .
After a nice rest and a week to make adjustments on the defensive side of the ball, where the Bills have had no shortage of struggles , Buffalo will square off against the Baltimore Ravens this week and are likely to see quarterback Lamar Jackson , who is expected to return from injury after a three-game absence.
It will be yet another test for the Bills, who need to seriously think about making at least one trade on defense.
With a few weeks to go before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, you can follow our tracker below for all of the latest rumors pertaining to what the Bills might do, and players who could be available for Buffalo to trade for.
ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport report that the Colts will look to trade away pieces at the deadline if things continue to go south between now and Nov. 10.
"If (the coming weeks do) not go well, new chief of personnel Ed Dodds, a longtime lieutenant of Ballard, will work in concert with Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon and other members of the Indianapolis brass to deal resources and build for the future," the ESPN reporters wrote.
Among the Colts that could be available, Rapoport and Schefter say, are defensive tackles DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart, and wide receiver Keenan Allen.
As we touched on in our biggest needs section below, wideout is a spot the Bills should consider adding to, and as our Randy Gurzi explained on Monday, bringing in help at D-tackle wouldn't be a bad idea, either.
It certainly wouldn't hurt for the Bills to make an addition at any defensive position group, but the ones most in need are safety, cornerback and inside linebacker .
Maxwell Hairston and Dee Alford have been disappointments and rookie Davison Igbinosun needs more time to develop. At safety, Cole Bishop has only been OK and C.J. Gardner-Johnson hasn't provided the level of play Buffalo needs.
The Bills could use an upgrade over Dorian Williams, and we know Terrel Bernard is a shaky starter because of his injury history, so at the very least, Buffalo needs more depth.
On offense, wide receiver is a position the Bills might explore an addition to. Joshua Palmer is a zero and DJ Moore is battling a shoulder injury that could linger all season.

title: Bills' Week 8 Injury Outlook: Will DJ Moore, Ed Oliver Be Ready to Face Ravens?
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are coming off their bye week with seemingly minimal injury concerns, but there are a few big names to monitor in Week 8.
While wide receiver DJ Moore and defensive lineman Ed Oliver were unavailable last time out against the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18, the rest has likely allowed them to get over their injuries .
Additionally, tight end Dalton Kincaid and outside linebacker Bradley Chubb warrant a check-in due to the fact they both left the Week 6 game in Las Vegas due to rib injuries. Neither issue has apparently lingered into Week 8 as the Bills prepare to host the Baltimore Ravens for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on November 1.
Buffalo will host its first official Week 8 practice and media availability on Wednesday, October 28.
In an extremely rare development, Moore missed back-to-back games heading into the Week 7 bye.
After reaggravating his AC joint sprain against the New England Patriots on October 4, Moore was officially questionable in Weeks 5 and 6 before landing on the game day inactive list.
While Moore likely could have played through the shoulder problem, it seems a different line of thinking won out with the Bills opting to give him uninterrupted time for rest and recovery.
"It [the rest] helped big time," said Moore during a Monday morning radio appearance on WGR 550.
All signs point to Moore being at full strength when the Bills host the Ravens.
Oliver left the Week 4 home game against the Patriots after taking a hit on the left leg in the knee area. He didn't return, and the Bills held him out of practice during Week 5 preparations for the Los Angeles Rams.
With Buffalo holding its Week 6 practices at UC Irvine prior to traveling to Las Vegas for the October 18 game, Oliver missed back-to-back days before finally returning to action, in a limited capacity on Friday, October 16.
Ruled questionable to play, the defensive tackle was ultimately scratched for the second game in a row. More than two hours prior to kickoff in Week 6, Oliver was seen working out on field with trainers at Allegiant Stadium.
Kincaid left the midway through the third quarter on October 18 due to a ribs issue. After a trip to the locker room, the tight end returned to game action as the Bills took possession with 8:01 remaining in the fourth quarter.
Making a 14-yard reception three snaps into the drive, Kincaid was available the rest of the way. He made bye week appearances on the Pat McAfee Show and ESPN's College Gameday, giving indication he's ready to go when practice resumes.
Surprisingly, Kincaid recorded only one TD reception over the first six games, but he's capable of erupting at any moment.
Chubb suffered a ribs injury early during the second quarter against the Raiders in Week 6. He left the game, and the Bills subsequently ruled him questionable to return .
The starting edge rusher was available down the stretch, but Buffalo primarily deployed second-round rookie TJ Parker for the remainder of reps. It appeared as if there was no desire to risk potentially worsening the issue, especially heading into the bye week.
Chubb saw 21 of 66 defensive reps against the Raiders, but he'll likely resume his full-time role in Week 8.

title: 4 Bold Predictions for Panthers vs. Packers That Just Might Come True
full_text:
For the second straight year, the Carolina Panthers will head into the wintry confines of Lambeau Field. For the second straight year, they will do so as underdogs after an abysmal loss in which they allowed 40 points the week prior. It's a little uncanny how that happened.
It should be a fun contest on Thursday night no matter what. Here are some bold predictions that could, under the right circumstances, come true this week.
The Panthers made life difficult on Jordan Love last year, and the defense has more talent this year to do the same. However, without Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, one would expect the Panthers to struggle in coverage.
Akayleb Evans is everyone's favorite punching bag, and sadly, he's likely to be picked on again (assuming he plays after being dinged up on Sunday). But Love is prone to being a little too aggressive at times, so we're predicting that Evans will finally punch back against an opposing offense and snag a takeaway.
It hasn't been a banner start to Jaelan Phillips' Panthers career. He does have 2.5 sacks in 4.5 games, which translates to a full season of over nine sacks. That's not that bad, although it's not what Carolina is paying for.
The Panthers should get Phillips back after missing last week, and the Packers, like the Panthers, have struggled to protect their quarterback. If anyone can make life difficult on that offensive line, it's Phillips, who can break out with two sacks of Love. And if Phillips can't go, then Princely Umanmielen should be able to wreak havoc, too.
Jalen Coker set his career high with 138 receiving yards in Week 1 this year, and the Packers' defense is pretty stout. However, they're allowing the 12th-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers this year.
Coker's been a little slow (not entirely his fault) since returning. A motivated Bryce Young against that secondary should lead to a solid day. Coker, because he will not see as much of Green Bay's best defender, should be able to set another career high.
The Panthers have no business winning this contest, which makes it the boldest prediction of all. They are and should be underdogs, and this is deservedly a game everyone expects them to lose. That was probably true before the Tampa Bay Buccaneers made mincemeat of Carolina as well.
They can't follow the same formula of controlling the game with the ground attack and limiting possessions. That won't work this time. But they do have the aerial firepower to go band for band with Green Bay, and the Packers have lackluster pass protection. There is a path, albeit narrow, to victory.

title: The Panthers Let a Key Player Walk in Free Agency. They Probably Regret That Now
full_text:
When the Carolina Panthers let D.J. Wonnum walk in free agency, I didn't think much of it.
Wonnum was coming off a season with only three sacks, and the Panthers had plenty of other things to worry about. He eventually signed a one-year, $3 million deal with the Detroit Lions, and at the time, I could understand Carolina deciding to move on.
Seven weeks into the season, I'm not so sure about that anymore.
Wonnum already has five sacks in six games for Detroit, which is two more than he had in 16 games for Carolina last season. He even got one against his former team when the Panthers played the Lions earlier this season.
This isn't me saying the Panthers made some terrible decision by letting Wonnum leave. If I didn't think it was a big deal at the time, I'm not going to sit here seven months later and pretend Dan Morgan should've known exactly how this would play out.
But look at Carolina's edge room right now. Jaelan Phillips has been dealing with a hamstring injury, Thomas Incoom is on injured reserve with a calf injury and the Panthers have already had to elevate Nick Hampton from the practice squad.
That's where the $3 million starts to bother me a little bit.
Wonnum wouldn't have come back as someone Carolina needed to build its defense around. He would've been another veteran pass rusher who could give them snaps, get after the quarterback and keep the Panthers from having to dig so deep into their depth when injuries hit.
And it's not like his production in Detroit came completely out of nowhere. Wonnum had eight sacks during his final season with Minnesota and then had four in only eight games during his first year with Carolina. Last season wasn't particularly good, but we've seen him produce when he's healthy.
Maybe things would've played out differently if he had stayed in Carolina. Maybe he doesn't have five sacks right now. There's no way to know that, and that's why I'm not going to call letting him leave some massive offseason mistake.
I just know the Panthers could use another healthy edge rusher right now, and a guy they let walk for $3 million is sitting in Detroit with five sacks.
Yeah, I bet they'd like to have that one back.

title: Fantasy Football Projections for Panthers' Bryce Young, Chuba Hubbard & More
full_text:
It's a short week for the Carolina Panthers as they look to rebound from an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . The 43-13 decimation of the Panthers is raising major questions on both sides of the ball, especially the defense .
As in Week 1 against the Bears, the run defense was atrocious, allowing Tampa Bay was able to score 43 points despite Baker Mayfield throwing for just 64 passing yards.
As for the offense, Bryce Young, Chuba Hubbard, Tetairoa McMillan, and the rest of the roster performed poorly. Despite losing to the Detroit Lions in Week 7, the Packers have played at a high level for the last three weeks.
From a Fantasy Football perspective, Carolina faces another tough test, as the Packers are a top-10 to top-12 fantasy defense in the NFL. That said, Carolina can still put together decent performances. Here are the Week 8 projections for fantasy-relevant Panthers.
Coming off his worst game of the season, Bryce Young should be able to improve on his three-turnover performance. Against the Buccaneers, Young posted just over 5 fantasy points. Now going up against the Packers, don't expect a game-breaking performance, but an average or slightly below average game.
The Packers' defense ranks fifth against QBs this season, which should make fantasy managers a reason to hesitate to start Young on Thursday night. Even so, Young has still posted over 19 points in four of Carolina's six games; he's clearly more reliable than he has been in years past.
Unlike Bryce Young, Hubbard faces a favorable fantasy matchup this week. While the Packers' defense overall ranks in the top half of the league overall, it's currently 27th to 28th against running backs.
This doesn't mean that individually Hubbard will go off on his own, but there's certainly a chance he scores the most points among the Panthers this week.
Hubbard is Carolina's safest starter and has been all season. Through six games, Hubbard hasn't scored fewer than 10 points. That trend won't end on Thursday night, Hubbard is still a high end RB2
Another matchup that should be somewhat favorable. Both Coker and McMillan were ineffective against the Buccaneers, combining for fewer than 10 fantasy points and fewer receiving yards than Darren Waller, who caught one pass.
With Bryce Young having a tougher matchup, the receivers could suffer. Both Coker and McMillan have 30+ point performances, but outside of those games, neither has scored more than 16 points this season.
This feels like a game where both can produce, but not win someone's week for them.
Tetairoa McMillan final projection: 14.4
Jalen Coker final projection: 11.2

title: Pete Prisco's Bryce Young Take After Crushing Loss Shows How Far We've Come
full_text:
Two things can be true at once: the Carolina Panthers got outclassed in every way by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and Bryce Young had his worst start of the season . The two facts are undeniably related, but they're both true statements .
In the past, Young would've been blamed for the disaster. Why did he fumble and throw two interceptions? That's probably why they lost, right?
That was the running narrative for Young's first three years. If the Panthers lost, it was because they didn't have a good quarterback. Now, though, it's abundantly obvious that they do have a good quarterback.
So, while the temptation to blame the quarterback is there, even Pete Prisco, who notably has been slow to praise Young ever, believes it wasn't Young's fault in particular.
Pete Prisco admitted earlier this year that he was wrong about Bryce Young and that he deserved to be in the MVP conversation. It was honestly the first bit of praise for either Young or the Panthers from the CBS analyst in a long time.
Until Sunday's contest, Prisco had picked the Panthers to lose every single matchup. He was wrong this time, so perhaps he'll be back to it, but obviously, he's never been a big fan of the Panthers or Young. Even he can't deny how bad the team failed on Sunday.
"I'm not going to sit here and blame that loss on Bryce Young. The bottom line is that was a team loss." @PriscoCBS #NFLPostgame pic.twitter.com/2fFSJISkvE
Prisco said, "I'm not going to sit here and blame that loss on Bryce Young. By no means was that on him... He didn't play well, he threw interceptions, but the bottom line is, that was a team loss."
The analyst rightfully took aim at the Panthers' run defense, which was once again porous. "You can't play and win playing that style of football," he said.
Young, as Prisco said, was not great, but things got out of hand almost immediately. Bad protection by Robert Hunt led to the fumble returned for a touchdown that made it 17-0. From then on, the Buccaneers knew he would have to pass.
He managed to hit Darren Waller for a 50-yard touchdown to spark some hope, but the special teams allowed a blocked PAT to be returned for two points, deflating things even further.
From then on, the stout Tampa defense knew what the Panthers had to do, so they pinned their ears back and went after Young to the tune of five sacks. By that point, the game was over, so Young's mistakes didn't really cost them the game.
He'll tell you he needs to be better. He does, and he has been this year. But Sunday's ugly showing was more than a QB problem. It was an organizational failure from the top down.
The silver lining to this loss is that it isn't coming with calls for Young to be benched. Everyone seems to be in agreement that of all the things going wrong for Carolina this year, quarterback isn't one. How far we've come.

title: Overreaction? Panthers May Have Shown Who They Really Are vs. Buccaneers
full_text:
I was starting to think I had the Carolina Panthers figured out.
They weren't great, but they were getting better. Bryce Young was playing some of his best football, the defense had settled down after a rough start and Carolina had started winning games. I was starting to buy into the idea that maybe this team had finally turned a corner.
Then Tampa Bay came to town and beat them 43-13.
I'm not going to completely change my opinion of the Panthers because of one bad Sunday. But I'll admit, this one bothered me a little more than a normal loss because there wasn't really one thing you could point to and blame.
Pretty much everything went wrong.
Maybe that's what bothered me most.
Carolina gave up 291 rushing yards against Chicago in the opener, and I remember wondering how you were supposed to win games when you couldn't stop anybody from running the football. Then the Panthers got better. The run defense settled down, and I thought maybe we could finally quit talking about it every week.
Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards Sunday.
Bucky Irving had 106 yards and two touchdowns, Kenneth Gainwell had 88 and Sean Tucker added 52 yards and another score. Baker Mayfield threw the ball just 11 times because, really, why would Tampa Bay do anything else?
That's the number I keep coming back to. The Buccaneers scored 43 points and barely needed their quarterback to throw the football.
I thought Carolina was past games like that. Apparently, I was wrong.
I've defended Young quite a bit this season, and I still think most of it was deserved.
He had been playing better. He was taking better care of the football, making some big throws and looking more comfortable running the offense. I've written plenty about the progress he's made, so I'm not going to make excuses for him when he has a game like this one.
Young went 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He also lost a fumble, giving him three turnovers on the afternoon.
The offensive line didn't exactly do him any favors. Young was sacked five times, and playing quarterback when you're down 33-6 at halftime isn't a situation I'd wish on anybody.
Still, three turnovers are three turnovers.
I'm not suddenly back to questioning whether Young can be Carolina's quarterback because of one game. I do want to see what happens next, though. We've spent the past few weeks talking about him taking a step forward, and now we get to see how he responds to taking one backward.
Usually, even in a loss, you can find something.
Maybe a young player had a good game. Maybe the defense played well enough to win and the offense couldn't get anything going. Sometimes you walk away thinking the Panthers probably should've won.
I couldn't find much of that Sunday.
Carolina turned it over four times, allowed 258 rushing yards and gave up five sacks. By halftime, it was 33-6 and whatever plans the Panthers had coming into the afternoon were pretty much gone.
And that's where I'm struggling with this one.
Were we watching a team get better over the past few weeks, or were the wins making it easier to ignore some problems that were still there?
I don't think it's fair to say none of the improvement was real. Young really was playing better. The defense really had improved, and the Panthers were finding ways to win games they probably would've lost before.
That's why Sunday was so frustrating. Just when I thought I knew what this team was becoming, they gave us three hours that looked a whole lot like the Panthers we thought they were leaving behind.
Six games probably isn't enough to know for sure.
I'm not ready to throw away everything Carolina did before Sunday, and I'm definitely not calling the last few weeks a fluke. One terrible game doesn't get to erase everything that came before it.
But I'm also not shrugging off a 43-13 loss at home.
If Carolina comes back and looks like the team we were watching before Tampa Bay, maybe we chalk this up as one of those Sundays where everything went wrong at once. Those happen in the NFL.
If the run defense gets pushed around again, the turnovers continue and Young struggles, I'm going to look at this game a lot differently.
I was starting to believe the Panthers had turned a corner.
After Sunday, I need to see it again.

He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Why Carolina Panthers Can't Fire DC Ejiro Evero... Yet
full_text:
Defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero has had a very up-and-down tenure with the Carolina Panthers . The highs have unfortunately not been very high, and the lows have been abominably low. Sunday was yet another low.
In Evero's defense, there are a substantial number of injuries on defense. Missing Jaelan Phillips, Jaycee Horn, and Mike Jackson certainly doesn't make life easy on a defensive coordinator. There are, because of that and more, holes in this unit even still.
Additionally, the defensive coordinator doesn't tackle. He doesn't make interceptions. He doesn't cover receivers. He can only do so much, and players not executing is a big part of the equation. Players play, and coaches coach.
Ultimately, though, that doesn't really matter. Coaches are scapegoated all the time, and it's not always the wrong idea. Evero can't tackle, but a consistent lack of tackling under him is problematic. It all reflects on the coaching, even if he isn't out on the field.
And so, after all this time and the ups and downs, we've come to the conclusion that Evero needs to be fired . It may not be his fault entirely, but if anything's going to get better, something has to change. And personnel is a whole lot harder to change at this point.
So, Evero's time should be up. But not yet.
The Panthers can't fire Ejiro Evero. It's difficult to fire a coordinator in-season and promote someone else to the position, but it's almost impossible for anything to happen in such a condensed week.
The Panthers travel to take on the Green Bay Packers on Thursday Night Football. Dave Canales said they essentially had their Monday meeting on Sunday because of the short week. They will have had a total of three days to prepare, not including gamedays Sunday and Thursday.
It is hard enough to prepare for a game in that period, let alone get a new coordinator up to speed, even if it's someone on the coaching staff already (like Peter Hansen, who called plays some during the preseason).
But this short week leads to a long week. They'll play Thursday and then have nine days between gamedays, which is more time to implement changes. So, if the Panthers fire Evero on Friday morning, they'll have plenty of time to change things.
Kaye's Take: I think it's important to point out how bad the talent was on defense in 2024 when the defense gave up the most rushing yards in a season since 1980. But it's also worth pointing out if you take away the 8 occurrences of 200 or more rushing yards in 2024 (which…
It bears mentioning that the same logic applies to any moves. If the Panthers are going to sign Marshon Lattimore, trade for Sauce Gardner, or trade for Josh Sweat, they probably won't do it before Thursday.
Why the Panthers wasted the bye week as it pertains to any of that is beyond us, but they have a second mini-bye coming up that could open the door to the changes we believe are necessary.
Dave Canales has said that he's seen what Evero's scheme can look like, and it can look really good. That is true. But in Carolina, it never has. And after a certain point, it becomes clear that it's not working.
It's not working, and it's time to make a change. Just not yet.

title: NFL Week 8 Odds Reveal Panthers' Chances of Bouncing Back vs. Packers
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers blew a golden opportunity to get two games above .500 and take hold of the NFC South on Sunday. They cannot linger on that very long, though, because they play the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night.
The vibes were so high and the Panthers were favored at home before dropping the egg of all eggs against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Now, a loss puts them below .500, souring what had been a really fun start to the season.
Will they lose? Here's what the early odds say for this primetime bout.
To absolutely no one's surprise, the Panthers are road underdogs against the Packers. Despite beating them in Lambeau Field last year, the Panthers are once again expected to lose this contest.
The spread is 3.5 points per DraftKings . The Packers are -115 to cover, and the Panthers are -105 to cover. The over/under is set at 47.5 points, with the over at -112 and the under is -108.
The Panthers are +160 to win outright, and the Packers are -192 on the moneyline. The oddsmakers don't have a lot of faith in the Panthers, despite both teams coming off a loss.
Essentially, the oddsmakers believe the Packers will win with a final score of 26-22. Somewhat surprisingly, it's not expected to be a bigger blowout for the Packers.
The Panthers just can't get healthy. Taylor Moton went down shortly after returning, and they're still without Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn. Meanwhile, the Packers are adding players. Josh Jacobs just returned from the Commissioner's Exempt List.
He probably shook the rust off, which is bad news for a Panthers defense that now has two games allowing 250+ rushing yards to opponents under its belt.
So, unfortunately, there are plenty of reasons to expect the Panthers to lose, and it's unlikely they can replicate last season's magical upset. The same formula simply won't work, and the Packers will likely not underestimate them this time.
Both teams are in desperate need of a win, but the Packers are better, more trustworthy, and healthier than the Panthers. That is reflected in the game odds.
The only potential silver lining is that the Panthers scored 32 and beat the Detroit Lions with most of the same injuries, while the Packers just lost to the Lions after scoring 17, so perhaps the Panthers have enough firepower to surprise people.

title: Dan Morgan Can't Escape Blame for Panthers' 43-13 Disaster
full_text:
There are plenty of people who deserve blame for what happened to the Carolina Panthers against Tampa Bay. Bryce Young turned the ball over three times, the defense gave up 258 rushing yards and the offensive line allowed five sacks.
Dan Morgan deserves some of that blame, too.
I've liked a lot of what Morgan has done since taking over as general manager. The Panthers have more talent than they did when he got the job, and he's made some good moves trying to clean up a roster that needed a lot of work.
That doesn't mean I have to agree with every decision he's made. Sunday exposed a few areas where I think Carolina could've done more with its roster, especially once injuries started piling up.
This is the one I've had the biggest problem with because the Panthers have known for weeks that they were going to be without their two starting corners.
Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson have been on injured reserve since late September. Carolina brought Robert Rochell back to the practice squad and moved forward with Will Lee III, Akayleb Evans and Chau Smith-Wade on the active roster.
I would've liked to see Morgan add another veteran.
That doesn't mean there was some obvious trade sitting there for Carolina to make. We don't know what other teams were asking for, which players were actually available or what conversations Morgan had around the league.
But from the outside looking in, I thought the Panthers needed more help at the position.
Carolina didn't need another No. 1 corner. Even somebody who could come in and give the Panthers dependable snaps while Horn and Jackson worked their way back would've made me feel better about the group.
Now Evans is dealing with an injury, too, leaving Carolina even thinner at the position.
Maybe Morgan believed the Panthers had enough to get through this stretch until Horn and Jackson returned. If so, I understand not wanting to overpay for what could've been a temporary fix.
I still would've added somebody.
I'm not blaming Morgan because players got hurt. No general manager can control that, and Carolina has had some bad luck there.
Jaelan Phillips couldn't play against Tampa Bay because of a hamstring injury, while Thomas Incoom was placed on injured reserve with a calf injury. Carolina elevated Nick Hampton from the practice squad before Sunday's game.
At that point, you're getting pretty deep into the roster.
That's where I think it's fair to question whether Carolina has enough proven depth available at the position right now. Once the injuries started piling up, players who weren't necessarily expected to have major roles were suddenly being asked to play more.
That's going to happen during an NFL season. Nobody has starters sitting on the bench waiting for somebody to get hurt.
But the drop-off has been noticeable, and Carolina hasn't gotten enough from its remaining edge group to make up for what it lost.
The injuries aren't Morgan's fault. I do think it's fair to question whether the Panthers were prepared well enough to handle them.
This is probably where I'm most frustrated with Morgan because I agreed with what he was trying to do.
Protecting Young had to be a priority. We had already watched what happened when Carolina put him behind a bad offensive line, and there was no reason to keep doing that to a young quarterback the franchise was trying to evaluate.
Morgan invested heavily in fixing it. Robert Hunt and Damien Lewis signed deals worth a combined $153 million in 2024, making it pretty clear how important rebuilding the interior of the offensive line was to Carolina.
At the time, I thought it was exactly what the Panthers needed to do.
That's also why watching Young get sacked five times against Tampa Bay was so frustrating.
I'm not putting every sack on the offensive line. Young can get rid of the football quicker on some plays, and sometimes the guy on the other side simply wins. That's going to happen.
What shouldn't happen very often is an offensive line with this much invested in it getting overwhelmed for an entire afternoon.
Carolina didn't spend all that money just to be a little better up front. The Panthers made those investments because protecting Young had become one of the biggest issues on the roster.
Sunday wasn't close to good enough.
I'm not going to look at one 43-13 loss and suddenly decide Morgan has done a bad job. I still think he's made this roster better, and there are moves he's made that I would make again.
But part of being the general manager is deciding where you need more help and where you're comfortable with what you already have.
I thought Carolina needed another corner before Sunday, and I still do. The injuries at edge have shown how quickly the depth there can be tested. Morgan also put significant resources into an offensive line that didn't come close to playing well enough against Tampa Bay.
None of that means Morgan is responsible for everything that happened Sunday.
The players still have to play. Dave Canales and his staff have plenty to answer for, too. A general manager can't control turnovers, missed assignments or what happens on every snap.
But Morgan built the roster those coaches and players are working with.
If we're going to give him credit for helping make the Panthers better, it's fair to question some of his decisions when the holes in that roster show up this clearly.
After what happened Sunday, I think he's earned some of the blame.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. title: Panthers Were Praised for Offseason Signing, But It Hasn't Worked Out At All
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers had a reality check on Sunday afternoon, getting completely obliterated by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . The 43-13 beatdown was embarrassing for both sides of the ball, especially the defense, which surrendered 258 rushing yards.
Many thought that this game would be ugly, but ugly for both sides, not just for Carolina. Tampa Bay won by 30 points, with QB Baker Mayfield throwing for just 66 yards and no touchdowns.
The last time a team won with their QB throwing for fewer than 50 yards was Christmas of 2025, when the Vikings beat the Lions.
So yes, the defense is the number one problem from Sunday's debacle. However, it wasn't the only major issue.
Panthers QB Bryce Young was pressured on over 68% of dropbacks against the Buccaneers, the most in any of Carolina's six games this season.
What's even more alarming is that this isn't the first game of the year where Young was pressured on over 60% of dropbacks. In Week 3, against the Browns, Young was pressured on over 63% of dropbacks.
Both alarming performances from the offensive line, a unit that was revamped in the offseason through both the NFL Draft and free agency.
On Sunday, one of Carolina's biggest offseason signings was dreadful, making the offseason praise now look foolish.
Not only was Walker abysmal on Sunday against Tampa on Sunday, but he's been underwhelming all season.
ESPN's Mike Kaye pulled up Next Gen Stats to put Walker's struggles in perspective.
#Panthers LT Rasheed Walker, according to @NextGenStats , has allowed a team-leading 34 QB pressures (including four sacks) on 257 pass sets. Seven pressures (including three sacks) came against Tampa Bay.
The lack of production thus far is beyond the worst-case scenario when Walker was signed in free agency. What's even more baffling about it is that Walker was really good as a pass blocker in 2025 for the Packers.
In 2025, Rasheed Walker played 986 snaps, and only allowed five sacks for the entire year. Furthermore, Walker posted a 93.8 pass-block rate in 2025, which ranked 11th in the NFL.
Now, less than halfway through 2026, Walker has already allowed four sacks, three of them in a single game.
Bryce Young was awful against Tampa Bay. Giving up points or giving up exceptional field position is always a QB problem, but it sure doesn't help that the left tackle, who protects Young's blindside, is giving pass rushers free sacks.
The other big problem is that Carolina has to stick with Walker moving forward, because Taylor Moton  suffered a fractured fibula in the game against Tampa Bay on Sunday. If Moton were healthy, then he could start at right tackle, and Walker could compete for reps with rookie Monroe Freeling.
Now thats not an option, as it hasn't been for most of the season anyway. If there's no improvement moving forward, then Carolina could explore outside options as the trade deadline approaches.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: Apparently, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Still Own the Carolina Panthers
full_text:
Cue legendary Pro Football Hall of Fame coach Vince Lombardi.
It was the classic “what could go wrong, did go wrong” game for the first-place Carolina Panthers. And that was just the first half on Sunday afternoon at Bank of America Stadium.
Dave Canales’s team trailed 33-6 at intermission, and by that time the team’s offense, defense, and special teams contributed to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ point total.
Calijah Kancey sees the open field on the Buccanneers' scoop and score 💥 pic.twitter.com/YH7gyTwIbv
Carolina’s defense surrendered 147 yards rushing and three offensive touchdowns in the first 30 minutes of play. Canales’s club turned over the ball three times before intermission. The Panthers were down 17-0 early in the second quarter after Buccaneers’ defensive tackle Calijah Kancey scooped up a Bryce Young fumble and returned it 32 yards for a touchdown.
Something you NEVER see: A blocked PAT turns into Zyon McCollum's 2-pointer. pic.twitter.com/p268pVNAky
And just after the Panthers finally woke up from their cat nap, things got a little crazier. Young found tight end Darren Waller for a 50-yard touchdown less than two minutes later. However, the PAT was blocked and Tampa cornerback Zyon McCollum returned the prize for two points and a 19-6 lead. The Bucs tacked on two more touchdowns and took a 27-point advantage into the locker room.
Tykee Smith gets the INT off of Bryce Young #WeAreTheKrewe #TBvsCAR pic.twitter.com/srgCceuI63
When it was all said and done, the final verdict was an ugly 43-13 home loss by Canales and company. Young came into the game with only a pair of interceptions. On Sunday, he was picked off twice and lost a fumble that was returned for a touchdown. In fact, after giving up the football just four times during their 3-2 start, the Panthers committed four turnovers in the stunning 30-point loss.
Yes, Carolina remains the only team in the NFC South that does not have a losing record. However, Sunday’s loss was a little reminder that while the Panthers unseated the Bucs last season as division champions, their recent history in this rivalry can’t be ignored.
Bucky Irving with his SECOND touchdown of the day 🔥 TBvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fz7kxCXD6Y
Dating back to the start of this decade, the Panthers dropped to a disappointing 2-11 in 13 meetings with the Buccaneers. The clubs will renew acquaintances in Week 12 on a Monday night at Tampa, a place that Carolina hasn’t won at since 2017 (the Panthers defeated Tampa Bay, 37-26, at London in 2019 in what was a home game for the Bucs). And it’s safe to say that Young has had his hands full against Todd Bowles’s defenses.
In seven games vs. the Buccaneers, the four-year pro has completed just 126-of-217 throws (58.1 percent) for 1,393 yards, eight touchdowns and four interceptions. He has been sacked a disturbing 20 times (3 times by Tampa defensive tackle YaYa Diaby on Sunday), lost two of his six fumbles and the team is 1-6 in those contests.
Canales and his club don’t have much time to feel sorry for themselves. The Panthers will be at Lambeau Field on Thursday night to face Matt LaFleur’s Green Bay Packers.
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: Why Bears Must Respond to Seahawks' Quenton Nelson Trade, 49ers' DeForest Buckner Deal
full_text:
The Chicago Bears front office cannot continue collectively sitting on their hands as the rest of the NFC is making moves.
Tuesday was a major day for the conference on the trade market, and both players dealt could've helped the cause in the Windy City.
The Seattle Seahawks landed eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts in a trade for a 2027 third-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round draft pick. Indianapolis continued selling off pieces following a 2-5 start, dealing defensive lineman DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick.
Seattle lands a star in the interior offensive line to spruce up a lagging running game that's ranked No. 31 in the NFL through seven games, just in time for a Monday Night Football matchup with the Bears in Week 8. Chicago had interest in acquiring Nelson before the trade was completed. Regardless of whether that was a position of need with Joe Thuney and Jonah Jackson is a good question, but the Bears now face off against a player they were unable to land in a deal.
The Niners, meanwhile, get interior help on the other side of the ball to directly respond to the Seahawks' big move. Chicago did have a need there alongside Grady Jarrett, but again, failed to meet the Colts' asking price.
If this season doesn't end in a deeper run than last season, you could pinpoint the exact day the front office's ambitions weren't meeting the moment.
GM Ryan Poles is who's been with the Bears the longest of the key figureheads. Chicago has already gotten a good return on Ben Johnson's offensive system and Dennis Allen's defensive schemes in a year-plus of their regime, but Poles had some bumps in the road during the early years.
The depth chart he's built has been good enough to start 5-2, even with Caleb Williams missing two games. We don't know if this is a playoff-ready roster, though.
There are clear needs in the defensive interior, while another outside corner could be handy. Left tackle could be a need too, depending on who you ask. Linebacker and defensive end could use some temporary depth after injuries to T.J. Edwards and Dayo Odeyingbo.
If any of those positions prevent the Bears from winning the NFC North, or fail to go on a deep playoff run, it's on Poles.
We'll see what Poles does to rectify the issues before November 10.
Andrew Hughes is a freelance journalist based in Austin, Texas, who has bylines across ON SI and The Sporting News. His work has been featured in The Miami Herald, Bleacher Report, and Yahoo Sports. Andrew graduated from Brooklyn College with a degree in journalism in 2017 and has been a sports fan since 1993.

title: Apologetic Montez Sweat Offers Little Clarity After Reinstatement
full_text:
It was a costly two-week suspension for Bears defensive end Montez Sweat but it didn't cost the Bears much in terms of losses or even a pass rush.
Sweat returned to practice on Tuesday after his performance enhancing drug policy suspension had ended and expressed how much it hurt being out while the Bears beat Atlanta and New England.
"It was devastating," Sweat said. "I'm just happy to be back in the building with my teammates. I think that's what I missed the most, just being in the locker room around my guys."
According to details of his contract reported by Spotrac.com and Overthecap.com, Sweat is forfeiting about $2.3 million from this year's salary for the two weeks without playing. He also has voided the remaining guarantees on his contract. That comes to about $12.7 million which now is not guaranteed should he be cut or the team trade him.
Chicago’s Top 3 Highest Paid Defensive Players: 1. Jaylon Johnson - $24,502,380 2. Montez Sweat - $22,766,472 3. Grady Jarrett - $18,925,000 46% of the total defensive salary cap. Lol.
Sweat signed a four-year $98 million deal with about $20.4 million in signing bonus shortly after he came over in a trade with Washington for a second-round draft pick prior to the 2023 deadline.
Stressing he has never been fined or penalized in this way, Sweat recognized he's paying a steep price for being out.
"Yeah, it's definitely something I got to live with my career," he said. "I never want to cheat the game, and I would never do it intentionally, but what happened happened and I'm moving forward."
Sweat deemed the incident triggering the penalty an accident but wouldn't detail what it involved.
"It was a surprise, but you take a lick on the chin and keep moving forward," he said.
"It was tough. Nobody wants to go look someone in the eye after you've done something detriment like that to the team, but I mean, those are the things you have to do to move forward." Montez Sweat on his conversation with Ben Johnson: ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/7gyZndzoTK
No doubt the Bears will need Sweat's defense against run and pass rush moving forward, but they did find a way to get past the shock of not having a former Pro Bowl edge in the lineup. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen simply moved around personnel and also blitzed more with slot cornerback Kyler Gordon now back in the lineup. Gordon has four sacks in two weeks.
“It’s great," Sweat said. "As long as he gets on the field, he’s going to make plays, so it’s been amazing watching him pass rush.”
Daniel Hardy was shifted from his normal heavy allotment of special teams reps to playing more edge rush and had 1 1/2 sacks against the Patriots.
"Big shout out to Daniel Hardy," Sweat said. "He’s been carrying his weight and creating a lot of opportunities for himself. He’s done great. Book. All the guys. They’ve been doing an awesome job.”
There's no doubt the Bears could improve themselves in this regard in the trade market. Khalil Mack's name keeps popping up. Getting Sweat back to go with this new blitzing approach could add the combination of pass rush and run defense they need to challenge Minnesota in the NFC North.
On a more personal note, Sweat wanted to express to fans and teammates how bad he felt with the positive test.
"I take the responsibility full upon myself," Sweat said. "It was nothing with the nutritional staff here or the training staff here. It was things I was doing on my own. Yeah, take that on the chin and move forward."
He added that he has something to prove as a result.
“Just that I’m still the player that I am," he said. "One positive in my career doesn’t define my career.”
Considering Sweat's contract situation and his sack production, his future in Chicago could be determined by the way he finishes out this season. The Bears obviously will also look to bolster their defense in the draft next year, as well.
The DT I'm trading for Jeffrey Simmons instead of DeForest Buckner for this reason: Have to pay him, but Simmons is the long-term solution for the D-Line. 29 and in his prime. Also played with Montez Sweat at Miss St. Buckner would help, but only would be a short-term rental.

title: 49ers Trade For DeForest Buckner: Who Are Bears' Other DT Options on Trade Market?
full_text:
The DeForest Buckner dream for the Chicago Bears is dead.
According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , Buckner is headed to the San Francisco 49ers in a trade that will nab a 2027 fourth-round pick for the Colts.
"Reunion! The Colts are trading three-time Pro Bowl DL DeForest Buckner to the 49ers for a 2027 fourth-round pick, sources tell (The Ringer and Netflix Sports).," Pelissero wrote.
The Bears and 49ers were both mentioned as teams "connected to" Buckner by NFL insider Jordan Schultz. It isn't clear just how involved the Bears were before Buckner went to San Fran, but none of that matters now.
With the Bears still in need of defensive tackle help and Buckner now off the board, here's a look at a handful of other options Chicago could explore before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
Buckner's now-former teammate, Stewart doesn't offer the kind of pass-rush punch Buckner does but he is a solid run-stuffer who can plug gaps up the middle.
Stewart has posted a respectable Pro Football Focus pass-rush grade of 67.0 and has 0.5 sacks and five pressures, and a better-than-average 60.4 run defense and eight run stops.
With Buckner costing just a fourth-round pick, it's conceivable Stewart could be had for a sixth-rounder, or maybe a fifth in a trade that involves Day 3 pick swaps.
Sitting at 1-4-1, the Washington Commanders are on the road to nowhere, so it's very possible they'll be sellers at the deadline and Payne is a clear trade candidate, as he's on the final year of his contract .
Payne is an even better run defender than Stewart, as evidenced by his 67.9 PFF mark in that area, which ranks 22nd among fellow interior defensive linemen.
Payne is also a better pass-rusher and has tallied three sacks or more in each of the last six seasons, including 11.5 in 2022, and four in 2023 and 2024.
We could see Payne fetching a fifth-round pick for Washington.
Sieler is by far the best pass-rusher on this list given his superior history of sack production with 5.5 or more in each of the past three seasons, including a whopping 10 in 2023 and 2024.
Sieler took a step back in 2025 with 5.5, but that's still very good sack production for an interior defensive lineman.
Sieler's run defense has been badly lacking this season, but he has traditionally been solid in that area, with PFF grades of 60.7 or better in every season of his career but one before this one.
The veteran would likely cost no more than a fourth-round pick.
This is the home-run swing.
It isn't clear if the Tennessee Titans would even trade their franchise player, but we know Simmons has grown more and more frustrated with all of the losing in Nashville over the years, so he could request to be moved.
Simmons is the elite of the elite at his position. He's a top-notch run defender with his 70 PFF grade ranking 17th, and he's one of the best interior pass-rushers in the NFL after tallying 11 sacks last season and four through seven games in 2026.
It would probably cost a first-round pick just to get the Simmons trade conversation started, but with the kind of impact Simmons could make, and with the Bears in win-now mode, it's worth considering such a blockbuster deal.
The Bucs are a dreadful 2-5 and could consider selling off pieces at the deadline as a result, although being in the putrid NFC South might make them think twice.
If they do sell, Vea could be on the move after the two sides had a contract dispute during the offseason that led to Vea getting a band-aid extension he'll surely want to re-visit in 2027.
Vea only has one sack through seven games this season, but he has shown he can do better than that with 4.5 or more in each of the past four seasons, including a career-high seven in 2024.
The veteran has not been good in run defense in 2026, but, again, that's another area where he has traditionally performed better with grades north of 60 in all but one season before this one.
We'd estimate a fifth-round pick being the cost here, although it's possible Tampa Bay could fetch a fourth if they send back a late-round pick.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Is Ben Johnson Running Up Against a Coach He Can't Outstrategize?
full_text:
The X's and O's matchup for Monday Night Football between Bears coach Ben Johnson and Seattle coach Mike Macdonald is one largely untested, as they've only met up twice in the past.
Neither occurred with both as a head coach, so it's largely a journey into the strategic unknown. The past has some elements to contribute to this discussion of who wins between pre-eminent football minds from opposite sides of the line of scrimmage.
Both past encounters occurred when Johnson was offensive coordinator in Detroit and once was before Macdonald came to Seattle as head coach in 2024. Both had very different results, so it's difficult to judge much.
What can be ascertained is the Lions defense really suffered an embarrassing day once and the other time Seattle just couldn't keep up with Johnson's attack.
In 2024, Macdonald was in his first year as head coach after he served as Baltimore's defensive coordinator. His Seahawks faced the Lions coming off of an NFC championship game appearance in 2023, and a 2-1 start to the 2024 season. Detroit went on to a 15-2 season before losing in the first round of the playoffs to Washington, but Johnson's offense was roaring all day against Macdonald's defense.
The Lions won that Week 4 game 42-29 in Detroit, as quarterback Jared Goff had a perfect day passing. He was 18-for-18, passing for 292 yards, and the other Lions pass was completed by Amon-Ra St. Brown for 7 yards. This NFL record flawless passing effort by Goff was the last time Johnson went up against Macdonald.
The Seattle Seahawks just held Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs to THREE POINTS. Now Caleb Williams is next. Seattle limited Mahomes to 165 passing yards, zero touchdowns and one interception while holding Kansas City to only 213 total yards. Caleb’s biggest… pic.twitter.com/Bh08yg8hR1
It was quite different the first time they played when Macdonald was Baltimore's defensive coordinator and Johnson Detroit's offensive coordinator. The Lions started 5-1 that season and on Oct. 2 when to Baltimore with Johnson's offense dominating opponents. Macdonald's Ravens defense shut down the Lions in a 38-6 Baltimore home-field win.
Johnson's offense came out firing blanks. They trailed 35-0 against Lamar Jackson and the Ravens before finally getting their only score in the fourth quarter on Jahmyr Gibbs' 21-yard touchdown run. It was 28-0 by halftime. Johnson's offense and the Lions defense were completely humbled.
Ben Johnson is Mike Macdonald of offense https://t.co/lYlrASY2kE
What this says for the Bears game with Seattle isn't much. It's different personnel, different teams, coaches in different roles in some cases.
However, it does say is both coaches have shown their ability to scheme up a big day against the other in the past.
No other defense so thoroughly snuffed out Johnson's Lions offense in the 2023 season. The six points was a season low and the next closest thing was when Matt Eberflus, Justin Fields and Co. beat the Lions 28-13 at Soldier Field on Dec. 10, four weeks after they had given away a game to Detroit at Ford Field when leading by 12 with three minutes remaining.
We are going to need the game of Ben Johnson’s life against this Seahawks defense… My goodness Mike MacDonald is insane! pic.twitter.com/TKrlwL6Plc
The 42 points Johnson's 2024 Detroit attack scored on Macdonald's first Seattle defense was a season high scored by a Seahawks opponent. Seattle's own offense piled up a season-high 516 yards against Detroit but couldn't get in the end zone enough to keep pace with Johnson's offense in that one.
The picture this paints for Monday night's game is two fighters who can land haymakers on each other. Which comes out of the ring doing it best in the third matchup is anyone's imagination, but both are coming in off outstanding showings. Seattle looked more like a defending champion in dominating Kansas City on Sunday night, while the Bears on Thursday beat Seattle's opponent in the Super Bowl, the same team the Seahawks barely survived 13-10 in this season's opener.
One unknown element might be the dynamic force Caleb Williams brings to the game as a QB capable of doing damage as a runner or passer, although Seattle QB Sam Darnold isn't exactly a stature. The other is that for the first time, both are the head coach of their teams.
This could be Johnson's biggest test this season with Williams as his quarterback, as the blowout loss at Green Bay earlier came without being able to lean on his starting QB.
Mike McDonald vs Ben Johnson pic.twitter.com/ba5E7YVxU0

He also has worked a prep sports writer for Tribune Newspapers and Sun-Times newspapers.

title: Kyle Monangai Tuesday Injury Update, Bears' Roster Move Are Bad Signs for RB's Week 8 Status
full_text:
The Chicago Bears were back on the practice field on Tuesday ahead of their Week 8 game against the Seattle Seahawks and there was bad news for running back Kyle Monangai.
According to The Chicago Tribune's Sean Hammond , Monangai was not spotted at the portion of practice open to the media, so he's seemingly not ready to take part yet after missing the last three games and not practicing in that span.
We won't be getting an injury report on Tuesday to confirm, though, as the Bears don't have to release one until Thursday because their Week 8 contest is on Monday night .
"The Bears returned to practice Tuesday at Halas Hall, but will not release an injury report until Thursday," Hammond reported. "During the open portion of practice, we did not see RB Kyle Monangai or CBs Malik Muhammad or Tyrique Stevenson."
This is obviously a bad sign for Monangai's chances of suiting up in Week 8, as is the roster move Chicago made before practice.
The Bears announced they have promoted running back Zavier Scott from the practice squad to the 53-man roster while also releasing cornerback Nick McCloud.
As ESPN's Courtney Cronin said, Scott, who has been serving as the team's RB3 behind D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson with Monangai sidelined, was out of practice squad elevations and is viewed as a valuable special teams member, so that might be behind why the Bears made this move.
"The Bears signed running back Zavier Scott to the 53 as he was out of practice squad elevations," Cronin wrote. "Scott played well on special teams and could give the Bears depth in the backfield amid Kyle Monangai’s prolonged absence (missed the last three games with turf toe)."
On Monangai, Cronin noted that "it's an important week regarding his availability," while also saying that if he can return to practice, it "would be a sign of moving in the right direction" for his availability.
Well, as we know, Monangai was not back at practice on Tuesday, so there's that.
The Bears haven't kept four backs on the 53-man roster all season long because of how top-heavy they are with Monangai and Swift.
That roster move, combined with the fact that Monangai still isn't practicing, has us thinking he's is trending in the wrong direction for Week 8.
It would be at least somewhat surprising if Monangai doesn't go this week. After all, the Bears opted not to place him on injured reserve at the outset of his injury, which we assumed meant Monangai wouldn't miss more than three games.
Well, he has now missed three games, hence our previous optimism he would return this week.
Perhaps that optimism was misplaced. We'll have a better idea of where things stand with Monangai when Chicago drops its first injury report of the week on Thursday.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Bears Surprisingly Showed Interest in Quenton Nelson Trade Before Seahawks-Colts Deal
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have been linked to a few edge rushers and an interior defensive lineman in early trade rumors , which was to be expected because Chicago has clear needs at those spots.
What we weren't expecting was the Bears to be linked to a guard, but here we are.
That's right, the Bears were listed among the teams to have interest in now-former Indianapolis Colts All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson before he was traded to the Seattle Seahawks .
Along with the Bears, the Green Bay Packers and Philadelphia Eagles were also interested, but neither of those teams are surprising because both have clear needs at guard.
"The Packers, Bears and Eagles were among teams that showed varying levels of interest in Quenton Nelson, per source. His market was strong," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported.
The Bears are well-stocked at both guard spots with Joe Thuney and Jonah Jackson, and both are under contract through 2027.
It's hard to say what the plan would have been had the Bears made a trade for the eight-time Pro Bowler. Maybe they would have moved Thuney to left tackle? We can't say for sure.
Perhaps this was just the Bears doing their due diligence, but it's hard to imagine Fowler would be reporting a simple check-in.
It is worth noting that, as good as Jackson and Thuney are, neither one is as good as Nelson, who is arguably the very best guard in the league.
Having an opportunity to acquire a player that good doesn't come around very often, so it's possible Chicago considered pulling the trigger, regardless of how little they needed to.
One position the Bears do need to address is the interior of the defensive line, where the Gervon Dexter trade has proven to be a mistake because nobody other than Grady Jarrett has stepped up.
Now that we see the Colts are willing to move their best players, Buckner, who is on the final year of his contract like Nelson is, becomes a much more realistic option for Chicago.
And, we've already seen rumors connecting the Bears to possible interest in Buckner. NFL insider Jordan Schultz named Buckner as one of three players to watch for the Bears, along with Khalil Mack and Josh Sweat.
"Two teams I'm watching very closely are the 49ers and Bears," Schultz said on The Pivot on Monday . "I've heard both teams connected to several defensive players, including rushers, Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack. Also, DeForest Buckner, along with some names who aren't necessarily on the trade block."
Bucker would be perfect for what the Bears need, which is a good pass-rusher and run defender. Hopefully Chicago can get a deal done for the former Pro Bowler, and sooner rather than later.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Quentin Nelson Trade Should be Green Light for Bears to Take a Big Swing
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is exactly two weeks away and two teams are already on the board with a big move. The Indianapolis Colts are sending six-time All-Pro guard Quentin Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero .
By trading Nelson, a captain and leader of their offense, just one week after they fired general manager Chris Ballard , the Colts are signaling to the league that they're officially trade deadline sellers, and the Chicago Bears should take that as a green light to take a big swing on another long-time Indianapolis Colt: two-time All-Pro defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.
A two-time All-Pro and three-time Pro Bowler, Buckner has been the heart and soul of Indy's defense since he was traded there from San Francisco in 2020. He's past his prime at 32, but his start to the 2026 season has shown that he still has plenty left in the tank. Buckner has already racked up four sacks in seven games, and his 91.2 impact grade from Pro Football Network is the fifth-best mark for all defensive tackles.
In short, Buckner is exactly what Dennis Allen's defense is missing. While this unit has shown general improvement from last year, it's still hard to trust this defense to help carry the Bears on a Super Bowl run. Sure, there's been injury issues, but injury issues happen every year to every team. That shouldn't stop the Bears from making an aggressive push to add an All-Pro caliber defender to a defensive line currently lacking serious firepower.
In case you needed any perspective on how little juice exists on Chicago's defensive front, cornerback Kyler Gordon is currently the team leader in sacks with four, and he missed the first five games of the season. There's a reason why all three of my top trade candidates for the Bears were defensive linemen.
It doesn't get more simple than this: the Colts have what the Bears need and they're willing to sell it. The Bears just need to pony up the draft compensation necessary to add a proven veteran who could help take them on a Super Bowl run. What the Colts would desire in a trade for Buckner is unknown, but I wouldn't imagine it'd be higher than what they got for Nelson.
If a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick would be enough to pry Buckner away from the Colts, then general manager Ryan Poles should already be on the phone making that deal. It's not like his track record with third-round picks is worth writing home about.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: Bears' D'Marco Jackson Might Actually be Team's Best Linebacker
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have an interesting situation brewing at the linebacker position.
D'Marco Jackson had the best game we've seen from a Bears linebacker this season against the Patriots, finishing with six tackles and coming down with an end zone interception in the team's 30-24 primetime win.
Aside from being rested (along with the rest of the defensive starters) for one fourth-quarter drive against Atlanta, he's played every defensive snap for Chicago since T.J. Edwards suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 5 matchup against Green Bay.
Jackson made a strong case to remain a lineup fixture since taking over the starting job. In fact, he might be their most well-rounded linebacker.
Edwards and Devin Bush both make $10 million per year. Meanwhile, Jackson makes $3.75 million per year. You wouldn't know it by watching how they've all performed this season.
Bush has been solid in coverage (although he's also dropped two easy interceptions), but he struggles near the line of scrimmage. Meanwhile, aside from a standout performance against Philadelphia, when he snagged an interception and knocked down two more passes (one of which was a dropped INT of his own), Edwards hasn't shown much promise against the run or the pass.
The linebackers have struggled in run support , which is a major reason safety Dillon Thieneman has nine more tackles (47) than the second-place player (Bush). He's been an eraser on the back end and has routinely tackled opposing ball-carriers eight yards past the line of scrimmage because the linebackers have gotten locked up.
The LB position is unique, as linebackers usually relay the play-call to the rest of the defense. With them being in the middle of the defense, the all-important "green dot" duties are almost always tasked to 'backers.
That often creates situations where starting 'backers are not earned via a meritocracy. The green dot duties often go to someone with the most knowledge or experience, regardless of whether a better player is waiting in the wings.
When healthy, Edwards has worn the green dot for Chicago's defense. However, Jackson has taken over those duties during his absences in both of the last two seasons. That would let them seamlessly make the switch to Jackson if they want to go that route, which they should want to do .
. @bears run defense has been excellent these past 2 weeks with lots of new faces; @jamreekromah @TheShemarTurner @JordanvandenB12 @DMarcojackson20 Maybe that Cignetti staff @JMUFootball @IndianaFootball know what the heck they are doing💯💯💯 #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/qib5JDxYNc
Whether it be against the pass or the run, he's simply better than Edwards at this stage of his career . He proved that last season, too, showing strong playmaking ability after starting four games for Edwards (and Tremaine Edmunds) late in the season.
Over those four games, he had 30 tackles, a sack, an interception, and two pass deflections. He was all over the field, and you could make a strong case that he shouldn't have left it after Edmunds returned to the lineup late in the season.
Going back to Edmunds probably helped Chicago save money on Jackson, whom they signed to a two-year, $7.5 million deal this offseason. However, they shouldn't make the mistake of taking him off the field again.

title: Alontae Taylor is the Answer the Bears Are Searching For at CB
full_text:
Cornerback Alontae Taylor has fallen out of favor with the Titans. He was a healthy scratch for the team's Week 6 matchup with the Colts and didn't see any playing time against Cleveland on Sunday.
Many have speculated whether Taylor, who signed a three-year, $60 million deal with Tennessee this offseason, could be dealt ahead of the November 10 trade deadline. He clearly isn't a great fit for Robert Saleh's defense and is already being phased out.
Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen knows Taylor well from his days in New Orleans. They drafted him in the second round of the 2022 NFL Draft, Allen's first as Saints' head coach.
With the Bears' secondary struggling to hold up in coverage, some believe his familiarity with Allen's scheme could make Chicago a likely destination for Taylor. After all, they almost pulled the trigger on a move that would've brought him to the Windy City last year
The Bears' secondary would probably be their biggest potential Achilles heel. Coby Bryant will be back in December to hopefully provide a similar boost to the safety room that Kyler Gordon has provided at nickelback, but Tyrique Stevenson and Jaylon Johnson have been terrible this season .
They don't have a contingency plan there. Clark Phillips III and Nick McCloud are no saviors. Taylor was expected to be that for the Titans, but he's unfortunately fallen well short of those expectations through the first half of the season.
He is, however, one of the most promising reclamation projects among all cornerbacks that might be available ahead of the deadline. He looked like a rising star for the Saints over the last four seasons prior to the 2026 campaign.
Considering his familiarity with Allen's scheme and the low cost to acquire him, he would be a worthwhile dart throw for Chicago. There's really only one caveat to the deal...
Alontae Taylor's contract might be a poison pill that prevents another team from making a move (or the Titans from pulling a trigger). With him guaranteed $20.5 million next season, it might be difficult for them to find a taker.
However, if both teams can find common ground in the draft capital department, then a trade could make sense for both parties. Another team would probably have to give up a higher-round pick (probably a third-round selection) if they wanted Tennessee to take on his guaranteed money. Alternatively, if another squad would take on the brunt of his salary next season, he could probably be had for a late-round selection. They'd be doing the Titans a favor.
Another potential holdup for Chicago is whether Allen would view Taylor as an outside cornerback, as he played both in the slot and perimeter during their time together in New Orleans. If they do, then a move might make sense, as that's where their most glaring issues have been. Kyler Gordon has fortified the slot since returning from Injured Reserve, and they probably aren't interested in taking him off the field for Taylor on the inside.
Meanwhile, Johnson and Stevenson have both played replacement-level football this season. The latter is slated to hit free agency this offseason, and cutting ties with Johnson would save $16 million.
If Allen believes Taylor can fill the void on the outside, they might be willing to take on his contract (and get him for dirt cheap) for a boost over the stretch run. That would also make it easier to move on from Johnson's contract next offseason.
