title: Bears NFL Power Rankings For Week 8: Chicago Standing on Doorstep of No. 1 Spot
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are riding high going into Week 8 and they are getting plenty of respect in the NFL power rankings of experts.
The Bears knocked off the New England Patriots with a strong showing in Week 7, and now they turn the page to Week 8, when they'll be tested yet again versus the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on Monday night.
Pretty much everything is going right for the Bears. Caleb Williams is taking that next step in his career and the defense has been better than expected, even at less than 100%.
Chicago will be getting at least one reinforcement this week, as Montez Sweat will return from suspension and Kyle Monangai might make it back from injury after a three-game absence.
But before we look ahead, let's see where the Bears are landing in the NFL power rankings of experts going into Week 8.
No change for the Bears here from Orr, who has the Minnesota Vikings and Seattle Seahawks leaping over Chicago instead.
"The NFL is trying to penalize Caleb Williams for wearing cleats that may help reduce non-contact injuries (a dubious claim, but in a sport where confidence in the unknown matters, I’ll allow it)," Orr said. "The cleat brand is paying the fines. Williams won’t stop wearing the cleats."
The Bears will play the Seahawks this week and a win should allow Chicago to leapfrog them in Orr's power rankings next week.
The Bears are on the doorstep of the No. 1 spot in Davis' power rankings this week, with only the San Francisco 49ers ahead of them.
"QB Caleb Williams has been lights out since his return," he said. "But after failing his Week 2 test against the Vikings, he'll try to pass this week's against Seattle's equally formidable D − and on the road this time."
With three impressive showings in four games this season, the Bears quarterback is ascending toward elite status just the way Chicago hoped he would.
He is no doubt giving the Bears that green light for an extension Ryan Poles talked about during the offseason.
ESPN's Courtney Cronin was posed the question: who was the Bears' best offseason addition?
Her choice was first-round pick Dillon Thieneman.
"Thieneman and fellow rookie DB Malik Muhammad II have nearly identical stat lines this season, but the No. 25 pick gets the nod here for how he has handled the highest snap percentage of any Bears defender (97.58%). Thieneman is No. 1 or tied for the team lead in total tackles (47), passes defensed (five) and interceptions (one). He also has 1.5 sacks and three QB hits. Thieneman has had his share of learning moments, but the stability he has provided can't be overstated for a secondary that has dealt with moving parts since the start of training camp," Cronin said.
No argument here. Thieneman has been as advertised. The only new addition who approaches what he has done is linebacker Devin Bush, but we agree the answer is Thieneman.
Ranking: 8 | Last week: 13
Prisco gives Williams love, but he rightly points out how well the defense has been playing, even at less than 100%.
"Caleb Williams is playing the best football of his career right now. But the best news for this team: The defense has made strides," Prisco wrote.
Both are very important developments, of course.
Chicago would have no shot to compete for a Super Bowl if Williams didn't take the step forward he is right now, and the defense's improvement only increases the Bears' chances.
Now, we'd love to see Poles make that final trade or even trades on defense to put this team over the top. He can do that by adding a starting interior defensive lineman and/or an edge rusher.
Thankfully, based on rumors , it appears Poles is at least considering doing so.

title: NFL Analyst Makes Bold Claim On Stellar Bengals Cornerback
full_text:
DJ Turner II has quietly asserted himself as one of the NFL’s best cornerbacks, and not many people have woken up to that.
Last season, despite the Bengals experiencing a down defense, Turner held his own, extinguishing several fires on the year, compiling a stellar 78.1 PFF coverage grade, good enough for sixth-best among 114 qualifying cornerbacks.
Across last season, Turner totaled 40 tackles, two interceptions, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. The former Michigan standout allowed an opposing QB completion rate of just 47.6%.
All of last season’s stellar outputs has since led to a stalled contract negotiation, as Turner is yet to put pen to paper beyond his rookie contract, which ends at the conclusion of the 2026 season, putting an end to his four-year rookie deal.
“...DJ Turner is the most underrated player in the NFL. Because we don't talk about them enough. Like it just a criminally under-discussed player who I don't believe has received All-Pro or Pro Bowl accolades up to this point in his career, it's wild to me,” opened ESPN's Field Yates earlier this month.
My vote for most underrated player in the NFL: Bengals CB DJ Turner. pic.twitter.com/dUhFywH2y0
Turner was selected with the 60th overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, after breaking out in the Wolverines’ 2021 season
“That cornerback market exploded this offseason, right? The likes of Christian Gonzalez, and Devon Witherspoon, and Derek Stingley [Jr], and Pat Surtain II, amongst others, making crazy, you know, great money, $30 million-plus per year.”
Turner’s rookie contract with the AFC North side was valued at just $6.16 million at signing .
“DJ Turner belongs in that conversation. I mean, that is just ridiculous what he has done. That's a hard assignment.”
“Like, we're not talking about him just holding down big, physical perimeter wide receivers. You've got guys playing in the slot, smaller and twitchier guys, bigger, more physical guys. Shoutout to the most underrated player in the NFL.”
Through the 2026 season so far, Turner has put together 12 tackles and five pass breakups. Turner’s PFF grade sits at 62.7 overall, including a 64.2 pass coverage grade and a 58.6 run-defense grade.

title: Zac Taylor Calls Bengals QB Joe Burrow the Most Accurate Passer in the World
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals had their most dominant performance of the season in their 35-13 win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 7.
Well, maybe their most dominating half of football since the team was held scoreless in the first half. Coming out of the locker room, the Bengals were on a mission on the offensive side of the ball, scoring 35 unanswered points on the way to their fourth win of the season.
Leading the offensive onslaught was quarterback Joe Burrow. Burrow tossed four touchdown passes in the second half comeback and finished his day 22 of 30 with 292 passing yards. It was a very efficient day for Burrow, and head coach Zac Taylor knows the work his quarterback puts in to deliver such accurate passes on Sundays.
"I don't know," Taylor jokingly answered when asked about Burrow's accuracy. "Watching how he works in practice between reps. Watching how he works in pre-practice, watching how he throws in pregame, watching his body movements... It's really impressive."
Taylor also said that he has never been around another player as detailed as Burrow, calling him the most accurate passer in the world. To hear Taylor's praise of Burrow, check out the clip above this story.
It's obvious to anyone who has watched at least one Bengals game this season that this team is going to go as far as Burrow can take them.
The second half performance in Baltimore is a strong indicator that this offense can light a defense up quickly, and that it hasn't even hit its full potential.
Taylor's comments about the Bengals star being the most accurate passer in the world are supported by the numbers. Excluding Jaxson Dart and Drew Lock, who have only played two games this season, Burrow leads the NFL in completion percentage at 71.7.
The win over the Ravens was massive for this team. Now, the Bengals have a chance to really separate themselves in the standings with November approaching.
Next up, a matchup with the Tennessee Titans. No game is an easy game in the NFL, however, the Bengals can't allow the one win Titans to get the upper hand. This is a game the Bengals have to come out quick with hopes of putting the Titans to bed early.
Following this game, the Bengals have the Atlanta Falcons and a rematch with the Pittsburgh Steelers on the schedule. There's an opportuntiy to come out of that stretch 3-0. Especially wiith Burrow playing at his current level.

title: Bengals Snapping Uniform Combo Drought for Ring of Honor Game
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals will wear one of their most successful uniform combinations Sunday when they pay tribute to two of the franchise’s great players.
The Bengals will wear black jerseys with white pants, orange stripes and black socks for Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans, which will feature the induction of James Brooks and the late Bob Trumpy into the Ring of Honor at halftime.
Trumpy’s induction will come one day shy of the one-year anniversary of his passing on Nov. 2, 2025, at the age of 80.
Sunday will mark the seventh time the Bengals have worn the black-white-orange-black combo – officially.
They’ve actually worn the combination eight times, but one of those instances was in Week 17 of the 2022 season when the Buffalo Bills’ Damar Hamlin suffered a medical emergency on the field and the game was canceled.
The Bengals are 4-2 in the six previous games wearing black-white-orange-black, with the most recent coming all the way back in the 2023 finale against the Browns, making it one of the longest combo droughts among all the options since the team unveiled their new uniforms in 2021.
This will be just the second time the Bengals have worn black jerseys this season, and the first since Week 4 against Jacksonville.
It will be the third time they have worn black socks, which have turned into a good-luck charm for the team.
They’re 2-0 this year while wearing black socks and 8-2 in their last 10 dating back to the Week 6 win on Monday Night Football against the New York Giants in 2024.
Here is a list of the previous seven times they wore the black jersey, white pants, orange stripes, black socks combo:
Week 18, 2023: Bengals 31, Browns 14
Week 14, 2023: Bengals 34, Colts 14
Week 2, 2023: Ravens 27, Bengals 24
Week 17, 2022: Bengals vs. Bills, canceled
Week 14, 2022: Bengals 23, Browns 20
Week 7, 2022: Bengals 35, Falcons 17
Week 5, 2021: Packers 25, Bengals 22 (OT)

title: Bengals Fear Season-Ending Injury for Erick All Jr. Amid Flurry of Roster Moves
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals placed Erick All Jr. on injured reserve on Tuesday after the tight end suffered a knee injury during Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens. The injury is believed to be a torn ACL according to NFL insider Ian Rapoport . Cincinnati hasn't officially announced a diagnosis, but the report raises the likelihood that All's season is over after just seven weeks.
If confirmed, the injury would be a painful setback for a player who only recently returned from a lengthy recovery. He tore his ACL in 2024 and missed the entire 2025 season. He made it back onto the field this year, only to leave Sunday's game with another injury.
All's absence also leaves the Bengals thinner at tight end. The team had already placed Tanner Hudson on injured reserve earlier this month. Now, Tuesday's moves involve four tight ends, with the Bengals bringing back a familiar face to fill the opening on its active roster.
The Bengals also announced they signed Cam Grandy from the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad. Grandy originally joined Cincinnati as an undrafted free agent from Illinois State in 2024 and spent his first two NFL seasons with the team.
Cincinnati waived Grandy after this summer's training camp — and he spent the first six games of the regular season on Minnesota's practice squad.
Grandy gives the Bengals someone who has spent time in its offense as it adjusts to All's injury. However, his return comes under difficult circumstances.
Cincinnati also placed tight end Josh Kattus on the practice squad injured list. Kattus signed with the Bengals' practice squad on Oct. 20.
To fill that opening, the Bengals signed Caden Prieskorn to the practice squad. The former Ole Miss tight end spent time on the practice squads of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Cleveland Browns in 2025. He was with Cleveland and Carolina this offseason before the Panthers waived him at final cuts.
Rookie Jack Endries will take on a bigger role with All and tight end Tanner Hudson (torn pectoral) likely out for the remainder of the 2026 season.

title: 'Stats Don't Mean Anything' - Boye Mafe Focused on Winning Tendencies Amidst Great First Bengals Season
full_text:
Boye Mafe is worried about wins, not numbers, during the 2026 Bengals season. The young edge rusher has been everything fans could ask for so far after being the top free-agent signing for Cincinnati this past offseason.
Mafe is one of the best quick-pressure rushers in the league this season (12th in total QB pressures among all players). He has a Bengals-defense-best 88.2 Pro Football Focus grade entering Week 8.
"I don't really care about my stats. My stats don't mean anything," Mafe said on Sunday. "At the end of the day, I want to win a game. I'm here to play football. At the end of the day, I want to celebrate my teammates and be around my teammates."
Mafe was lights out against the Ravens, notching five tackles and 1.5 sacks (five pressures). He's had four-plus pressures in every game but one this season.
"I feel confident. I feel comfortable. The coaches trust me," Mafe noted about how the defense is coming to him right now. "There are some things that I have to clean up, and [there are] some things that I have to do better. I want to play back a couple of plays myself, and I always strive to do better. At the end of the day, I'm not really worried about like the stats or anything like that. I just want to be able to play the best ball that I can and show the player that I can be."
Cincinnati stayed calm and responded when Mafe and his teammates entered halftime down 13-0.
They smoked Baltimore 35-0 after that.
"Yes, and it's trust in each other. We know on the offensive side of the ball what they can do and who they are. They know on the defensive side of the ball who we are, too. So, just trusting each other and just knowing that we're going to figure it out. At the end of the day, we have enough playmakers to make it happen," Mafe concluded.
Mafe and the rest of the Bengals return to practice on Wednesday as they keep building momentum entering the thick of the 2026 season.

title: Bengals Could Cement 'Fairytale' Trade Idea Ahead of 2026 Deadline
full_text:
While the Bengals' defense has fared better this season, flaws remain in the unit even after the team's offseason injection of talent. Now with the NFL Trade Deadline drawing near, another trade idea has surfaced involving the Bengals: Adding All-Pro safety Derwin James from the Chargers.
Pro Football Focus revealed their top-ten fairytale trade ideas involving star players from teams that have underperformed to start the season, listing James as a fit in Cincinnati.
"While the Chargers’ offense has sputtered in 2026, the team’s defense has actually been largely effective, Ironically, James — long one of the game’s foremost safeties — hasn’t contributed as much as usual," Pro Football Focus wrote. "Playing in only three games due to a hamstring injury, James has mustered a 60.9 overall PFF grade, and his coverage mark sits at a 50.8, however, he’s only a year removed from a 78.8 overall grade, including 80.1 in coverage as well as 34 total stops."
Even after signing Bryan Cook this offseason, the Bengals safety room still ranks 29th overall on PFF. Cook dealt with an injury early this season, forcing Jordan Battle to step up and show growth and leadership, but that has not materialized.
Across five games, Battle has missed 19.4% of his tackles, continuing his string of unreliability. The team signed Kyle Dugger later in free agency this offseason to provide further veteran depth behind Cook and Battle. However, he also dealt with an injury at the start of the season and is only now returning to practice following the team's bye week.
Adding James would give Cook the perfect partner at safety in the Bengals' secondary. While Cook has built his career on his physicality and open-field tackling, James has made a name for himself as a consistent big-play threat.
Last season, he had three interceptions, one forced fumble, and missed only 9.1% of his tackles. On top of that, he has consistently shown a knack for turnovers, with 12 interceptions, six forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, and 19 sacks.
While James has excelled in his hybrid-safety role throughout his career, he is 30 years old and on a contract that is not team-friendly beyond this season.
The Bengals would inherit the remaining $7.7 million of his base salary this season if they acquired him after Week 6. That alone is extremely appealing for someone of James' caliber; however, in 2027 his $17.5 million salary is fully guaranteed, and in 2028 his base salary is $24.6 million.
That means the Bengals would likely have to agree to a new contract with James after the trade. Extensions for key players in D.J. Turner and Dax Hill would also become increasingly difficult and would likely force the team to let one or both walk in free agency.
James has also dealt with a hamstring injury early this season, which has reduced his production; specifically, he has missed more tackles, with a 16.7% miss rate.
Everything considered, while trading for James would bring excitement to the Bengals, it would come with great risk. At age 30 and with a soft-tissue injury, it feels like a move the front office would oppose.

title: Bengals TE Mike Gesicki Thinks 'The World Knows' What Kind Of QB Joe Burrow Is
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals picked up an impressive 35-13 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. However, the scoreboard doesn't tell the entire story.
Going into halftime, the Bengals were down 13-0. It looked like the narrative of this game was going to be another blown opportunity. The team got the message during the break and put together their best half of ball this season, scoring 35 unanswered on their division rival.
Quarterback Joe Burrow tossed four touchdown passes in the second half to lead the charge. Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki was on the receiving end of one of those touchdowns, and had plenty of great things to say about his quarterback after the game.
“We know what we have in Joe," Gesicki said when speaking with CLNS Media's Mike Petraglia after the game. "I think the world knows what kind of quarterback Joe is. I said since I got here, best quarterback in the league. He proves it time and time again."
The second half of Sunday's win in Baltimore was the exact performance this fan base has come to expect from their quarterback. It's also the reason why the expectations are so high for this team.
The Bengals' offense has so many weapons, and Burrow is using them all. For instance, look at the Gesicki touchdown. Gesicki wasn't even the number one tight end option on Sunday, but Burrow found him to get the scoring started in the third quarter.
Burrow found four different options on his four touchdown passes, which included Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Drew Sample, and Gesicki.
Sure, the Ravens were down their best player with quarterback Lamar Jackson missing another game due to his ankle injury. However, Jackson doesn't play defense. The Bengals managed to turn things around in the second half, and a lot of that is on the shoulders of Burrow.
It can't be overstated how important this win is for the Bengals. The rest of the AFC North has no desire to lose at the moment, so the Bengals have to take these head-to-head matchups.
Now, the Bengals can control their destiny with another important AFC North battle on the horizon. Matchups with the Tennessee Titans and Atlanta Falcons are next, but that second meeting with the Pittsburgh Steelers will be here before you know it.
The next three weeks could tell the story of the 2026 Bengals. There's nothing better than getting the chance to watch important football.

title: Bengals Are on Pace for Historic Season After Dominating Win Over Ravens
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals earned their second straight victory this season with a convincing 35-13 beatdown of the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday.
While the final score is what everyone is talking about, things didn't look good at halftime. The Bengals were shut out in the first half before ripping off 35 straight points to win a pivotal divisional matchup.
Joe Burrow and the offense found their rhythm, and so did the team's defense. The performance on Sunday continues to put this version of the Bengals on a path that could make them one of the more special teams in the franchise's history.
Paul Dehner Jr. shared that the Bengals' point margin this season is the third-highest since 2000 and fifth in the NFL.
After Sunday's win, the Bengals have a +41 point margin this season. The Bengals have scored 163 points this season and have allowed 122.
Taking a closer look at the franchise's history, the 2005 Bengals have the best point margin at +71, with the 2015 team in second at +60.
There's still a long way to go if the 2026 Bengals want to make history, but Sunday's second-half performance proves this team has what it takes.
It's clear this Bengals offense can score in bunches. Burrow tossed all four of his touchdowns in the second half on Sunday.
The offense is averaging 345 yards per game, but on Sunday, the team flew by that number, finishing with 359 yards. Yes, the offense is what moves the needle, but what about the defense?
Al Golden's unit should get a tip of the cap for keeping the team in the game in the first half, allowing the Ravens only 13 points. But their second-half shutout deserves just as much praise as the offensive onslaught.
The Bengals had four sacks on Sunday, putting them at a tie at the top of the chart for most sacks in the NFL with 21. This front office had a mission to make the defensive line better, and did just that with the additions of Boye Mafe and Dexter Lawrence.
This team has shown flashes of brilliance. The next step is putting it all together for four quarters. Statistics continue to show the Bengals are one of the best all-around teams in the league, they just haven't hit their full potential. That should put the rest of the league on notice.

title: Zac Taylor Updates Injury Timelines For Erick All, Kyle Dugger Entering Titans Week
full_text:
The Bengals had two injuries pop up during Sunday's thrilling comeback win against the Ravens . Erick All (knee) and Kyle Dugger (quad) got knocked out of the game, and Bengals head coach Zac Taylor updated their outlook for Week 8 on Monday.
All's already had that right knee operated on multiple times this decade, causing him to miss the entire 2025 season.
Still, there's no confirmation on the severity yet as Cincinnati signed Cam Grandy to the roster in the mean time. Dugger is out at least for this week with his issue.
"He'll definitely be out this week, and we'll get more information on his quad," Taylor said before touching on when they'll know more surrounding All. "I'm not sure. It could be in the next day. I'm not positive on that."
All did sound optimistic about the outlook after the game. The fact he talked to any media at all is a good sign.
Both players are important for Cincinnati's depth on either side of the ball.
All played a season-high 33 snaps last week and was pacing towards close to that on Sunday, while Dugger posted a season-high 54 in Week 3 before getting injured and returning to play 11 snaps on Sunday.
Cincinnati got great impact from the rest of the roster to still win without them.
"Yes, I think we know who we are. At the end of the day, from a personnel standpoint, I think no matter who we're going against, we know who we are," Orlando Brown Jr. said after the win. "We know what we're capable of, which is fortunate, from the way that this team is built from a talent standpoint, the type of characters that we have in here and [with] the type of men in here. So, at no point in time would I tell you that we weren't going to stay the course. We had to come together at the end of that first half, make a commitment to one another to be more physical and violent and be able to go out there and finish."
Cincinnati should be getting names like Andrei Iosivas and Jalen Davis onto the practice field and off of injured reserve soon. They are continuing to knock on wood with great health as we head toward the midway point of the 2026 season.
Taylor and the rest of the roster have Tuesday off before returning for a normal three-practice week on Wednesday. They battle the Titans at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.
Spoke with Erick All Jr. at his locker postgame. Had street clothes on but no brace. Was standing and smiling. Said he’ll know more Monday but he’s hoping and praying for encouraging news.

title: Report: Bengals Signing Familiar Tight End Ahead of Titans Matchup
full_text:
The Bengals added another new name to the 53-man roster on Monday. WLWT's Charlie Clifford reported the team is signing tight end Cam Grandy for this week and beyond.
The team is back to a full roster. They plucked Grandy off of the Minnesota Vikings practice squad in what could be a sign of Erick All's injury fallout.
"The Bengals are signing tight end Cam Grandy off the Vikings practice squad to their 53-man roster, a league source tells WLWT. Grandy played a role in Cincinnati in 2024 & 2025 and is now back," Clifford posted on X.
Grandy has appeared in 13 career games with seven catches for 35 yards. All of those appearances have been with the Bengals from last season and 2024. He did not appear in any 2026 games so far.
Cincinnati is fresh off a massive AFC North win over Baltimore.
They flipped a 13-0 halftime deficit into a 35-13 win.
"[In the] second half. The first half was about third downs. We did a poor job on both sides of the ball on third down," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said on Sunday. "We didn't convert more than, like, a third-and-1. I think Ja'Marr [Chase] caught one early, but we didn't convert on the three main drives we had. Defensively, I don't know what the stats were in the first half, but I know they converted [almost] every one of them. Now, we did a good job limiting them to some field goals on two of those drives, which was key. But we just never really got in a rhythm. And [during] halftime, we came in here and took a deep breath. I thought guys really handled themselves well, and we came out and scored five straight touchdowns in the second half. [The] defense got five straight stops, and that's how you have to do it.
"That's how you go on the road and win. We had the turnover plus some fourth-down stops that count as more. I don't know how many. So, I'm just really proud of the way the guys responded, just took a deep breath, kept their composure, led, and went out there and put together as good a second-half performance as I've ever seen."
Cincinnati and Grandy are preparing for Tennessee at home this week.

title: Browns May Have Found Football’s Next Dynamic Duo in These Two Rookies
full_text:
Coming into the 2026 NFL Season, the Cleveland Browns were in desperate need of wide receiver help.
Luckily for the organization, they were able to draft KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston in this past year's NFL Draft.
Seven weeks into their young careers, Concepcion and Boston are already proving that they are poised to be the NFL's next dynamic duo.
KC Concepcion is currently on pace for 73 catches for 800 yards Denzel Boston is currently on pace for 50 catches and 900 yards Just fantastic production from your two rookie wide receivers #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/FvyDtjQAJh
In the first seven weeks, each receiver has put up some big-time performances for the Browns.
For Boston, he leads all rookie receivers in touchdowns with three. Meanwhile, Concepcion is coming off a dominant game where he had eight receptions for 129 yards.
The two receivers rank second and third in total receiving yards, only behind the first receiver drafted, which was Carnell Tate.
Looking at the pace, both guys are projected to get close to that 1,000-yard mark. If they keep up the production they have had, there is no doubt they could both reach quadruple digits in their first season.
As long as the injury bug doesn't come around too often or severely, Cleveland has their wide receiver room set for the foreseable future with the two rookies and second year man Isaiah Bond.
It's all just a matter of who the quarterback is.
If the Browns can find a top-tier guy, they will have the chance to put together a team that can win lots of games, go on playoff runs, and maybe just try and compete for that coveted championship.
Regardless, having multiple great receiving options means whoever does inevitably take over the offense will have help. It does not fully matter if the Browns have a top quarterback or not.
Outside of Boston and Concepcion, the Browns have had back to back phenominal draft classes.
Some other big names the Browns have drafted in the past two season are:
If the Browns can figure out a quarterback that can take them to the playoffs in the near future, they can capitalize on all these star players being on their rookie contracts.
It's also a good time to note that they just traded for Jared Verse, who was drafted in 2024 and won DROY after his rookie campaign.
While Deshaun Watson has been winning games, how sustainable is the injury-prone 31-year-old? Now more than ever, Cleveland truly is a quarterback away.
After the 2025 NFL Draft, I thought the Browns had to have just gotten lucky by getting so many great players. Then, they clearly did it again.
Something has changed in the front office, and Andrew Berry is seeing prospects clearer than ever.
Now is a great time to be reminded that Cleveland has 11 picks in the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft . Not only do they have two first-round picks, but over the past two seasons have been known to trade up and down and move all around the board while collecting more and more assets.
What if the Browns have another winning draft?
The future is clearly bright for a team with such a dark past. Cleveland, it's time to get excited.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: Denzel Ward Reached a Major Career Milestone in Browns Win Over the Weekend
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns improved to 5-2 over the weekend , which is tied for their best start since 1999, and the game was an offensive explosion for the Browns. Cleveland totaled 491 yards on the day (308 passing, 183 rushing), easily their highest mark of the season so far.
Deshaun Watson was tossing the rock to almost everyone on offense, leading to breakout games from KC Concepcion and Harold Fannin Jr. primarily. While the attention should be on the offense for shattering through, on the other side of the ball, there was an achievement that should not go unnoticed.
Denzel Ward picked off Tennessee quarterback Cam Ward (no relation) in a pivotal spot of the game in the second quarter. The Titans had just gotten the ball off a Fannin fumble at the Browns' 44-yard line, and on the first play after the turnover, Ward stepped in front of Elic Ayomanor to snatch it right back. The Browns then drove down 78 yards and capped it with a Quinshon Judkins touchdown to level the score at 14.
This interception was Ward’s 20th career pick , passing Joe Haden on the Browns all-time list up to spot 15. Only 14 other Browns players have amassed that 20-pick mark, but as we know, when you are as good as Ward is on the outside, teams will avoid him.
That avoidance doesn’t stop Ward from racking up other key defensive statistics, as he is Cleveland’s all-time leader in passes defended with 110, a feat he achieved last season, and is also top 10 in solo tackles with 309.
Ward has kept up his Pro Bowl-level play throughout his career; in his ninth season in the league, he is the highest-graded cornerback in the NFL this season, per PFF.
While the Browns have shipped away notable players like Myles Garrett on defense and parted ways with others in free agency, Ward has been the mainstay who was worthy of the fourth overall pick. His five Pro Bowl selections are the most by a cornerback in Browns history, and his play this year is calling for a sixth.
Cleveland recognized that in the offseason, keeping him home with an extension until 2029 . One of the franchise’s best cornerbacks still plays like he is trying to earn a spot each and every week, though. He continues to be the leader of that secondary, which is putting up another great season defending the pass, as they rank in the top 10 of the NFL in fewest passing yards allowed per game (201.7) and per play (5.5).
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: Andre Szmyt is Forcing Browns Ownership To Put Their Money Where Their Mouth Is
full_text:
Andre Szmyt has done his job.
On Sunday, Oct. 25, the Cleveland Browns took down the Tennessee Titans on the road at Nissan Stadium 27-24 , with Szmyt kicking his third game-winning field goal this season. Now, on the campaign, he has been directly responsible for sending the Browns home with wins against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football, the Baltimore Ravens and the Titans.
Since Post-1999, Szmyt now ranks second in Browns game-tying or go-ahead field goals in the final two minutes of a contest, trailing just legendary kicker Phil Dawson with 10.
Szmyt, himself, has a total of five.
Across the last two seasons, Szmyt hasn't just been clutch, but also consistent. He has made 38 of his 43 attempts, good enough for an 88.4% completion rate , while also knocking through 36 of his 38 attempts on PATs.
Post-1999 #Browns game-tying/go-ahead FGs in final 2 minutes: 🔸Phil Dawson (10) 🔸Andre Szmyt (5) 🔸Dustin Hopkins (4) Owner Jimmy Haslam called Szmyt a "cornerstone player" this past offseason. Right he was 🥹 (h/t @DanielOyefusi ) #DawgPound https://t.co/TsFWl0tx7X
But with how good Szmyt has been, it is surprising to see how weak a contract he is currently playing on.
This past offseason, the 28-year-old signed a one-year, $1.1 million extension to stay with the organization. After an impressive rookie season, one in which he booted 24 field goals and 25 extra points, one would expect him to see a bigger deal come across the table.
And surprisingly, Browns owner Jim Haslam talked as if he would make the big bucks.
When reflecting on the roster the team built in 2026, a group that was built on youth and first-year players, Haslam spoke highly of Szmyt and many others.
"I think what is important to understand about our rookies, though, and you will see them, you all know them, [is that] they are not only really good players, but they are also really good people," he said. "They will be the cornerstone with which we will build and grow and develop this winning team."
If Szmyt is really a long-term cornerstone for the team, and the front office just wanted to see him come out and continue the 2025 success into 2026, now is the time to put the money in front of him.
Consistent and clutch kickers are hard to come by, especially in today's game, so being able to secure one is incredibly important. The Browns, who have routinely gone through kickers since Dawson left the organization back in the early 2010s, should know this better than anyone else.
Szmyt has made as many game-winners as field goals he has missed. If the Browns don't see how valuable that is, other teams will. He has arguably one of the league's most valuable legs.
And if he enters the open market this offseason, some team is going to pay him a hefty sum.
The Browns better hope that they can get to him before then and lock him down as a cornerstone in The Land for the next few years.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns' 5-2 Start Raises a Major Question About Quarterback Position Future
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns’ season was supposed to be all about which quarterback to draft in 2027, but that was flipped upside down after a 5-2 start and sitting in first place in the division.
Deshaun Watson has led the offense to five game-winning drives, and the offense will continue to improve in the last 10 games. The Browns will have too many wins to be able to draft a top quarterback, and their other first-round pick from the Los Angeles Rams is expected to be outside of the top 10.
All the winning is fun now, but it leaves the future of the quarterback position in limbo.
They can move on from Deshaun Watson next season, but if he leads the team to the playoffs, then it will be difficult to justify replacing him. He threw for his first 300-yard passing game last Sunday and the offense looked smooth. If he can continue to put up big numbers and elevate the young players, then the Browns should seriously consider extending him.
However, Watson has not been consistent. Extending him would take into consideration his entire body of work with the Browns, which is incomplete. During his first season in Cleveland, he came off a year-and-a-half gap without playing and could not practice with the team while his suspension was in effect. He then had an unprecedented shoulder injury, led the offense for the Ravens, and two Achilles injuries.
If the Browns feel that he is a long-term solution, then he will cost a lot of money as the price for the position continues to grow. The roster is filled with rookie contracts, so the Browns can afford a new contract next season, but they will need the cap space starting in 2028 to extend their draft picks.
Shedeur Sanders is also the backup, and he was in a competition with Watson for the starting position in training camp. He has been able to observe how Watson prepares and learn Todd Monken’s offense without getting rushed into action. He is on a rookie contract, but the Browns need to figure out if he has enough talent to be able to replace Watson .
The roster is showing that they are ready to win now, and the team cannot take a step back next season because of poor quarterback play.
If they move on from Watson, Sanders may not be the automatic replacement . They activated Dillon Gabriel from the injured reserve list this week, meaning that he has to take a roster spot. The team is 5-2 and the defensive line depth has performed well in addition to special teams. A player will have to be cut to make room for Gabriel.
He has been praised for understanding the offense, but his physical limitations may be too much to overcome. Gabriel was not considered for the starting position at any point this season and does not seem like a viable option to elevate the offense next season.
The Browns drafted Taylen Green in the sixth round, and his physical tools are immeasurable. He is considered very raw for the position and will not be ready to take the keys to the offense next season. His future in the league may be at a different position where his speed can be utilized.
A mid-to-late first-round pick may be an option, but it has to be a quarterback that Todd Monken believes can win. There could also be reclamation projects that can step in for a year or two, but that will not solve the long-term future of the position.
Monken gets a lot of credit for reviving Watson’s career and putting him in good positions to exceed. He is winning with this roster, which nobody expected when he was named the starter. The answer for the position’s future is muddy, but Monken is proving that he should be trusted with the solution.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Even After an AFC North-Leading 5–2 Record, Not Everyone Has Warmed Up to the Browns
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns’ 5-2 AFC North-leading record with all five victories occurring in a come-from-behind fashion have impressed many in and around the NFL.
More than a few outlets are still skeptical that Cleveland can continue this brand of tight, play-from-behind, overall-point-deficit brand of football all the way to the team’s first division title since 1989 in the extinct AFC Central, despite five remaining games against teams with losing records, including three clubs at 2-5.
Projections to win the AFC North, according to ESPN Analytics: 🏈 Bengals (4-2): 68.3% 🏈 Steelers (5-2): 15.7% 🏈 Ravens (4-3): 10.5% 🏈 Browns (5-2): 5.5%
For example, ESPN Analytics has Cleveland with the worst chances among all four teams at just 5.5 percent, and Cincinnati as heavy favorites (68.3 percent) after Week 7 action.
Squawka has even less faith, putting the Browns chances at just 4.9 percent. That’s pretty far off from where they currently see the Bengals, at 59.9 percent.
And CBS Sports has a slightly better number for the Browns, at 8.6 percent probability of winning the division, but still lagging behind the other three clubs.
So…. @CBSSports still has the Browns having the lowest chance to win the AFC North despite’s wins over BAL and PIT pic.twitter.com/WBAf8xnIWQ
The Athletic’s Playoff Simulator is a bit more generous with the Browns after their Week 7 win, putting their chances at a division title at 17 percent, while parking Cincinnati’s odds at 45 percent. This model has the Browns basically tied with Baltimore, also at 17 percent, just below the Steelers’ 21 percent. Cleveland’s upcoming game is a road match at Pittsburgh, who they haven’t swept in a regular season since 1988, so a win on Sunday could surely flip the script for the Browns.
Where the Browns have made impressive gains is in the betting markets, where they started the season off at +2100. Even before Sunday’s game, Cleveland was being listed in the +1000 to +1800 range, but after beating the Titans in a hard fought battle on the road, the Browns’ odds have improved to the +585-+700 range, depending on the sportsbook.
For starters, Cleveland is carrying a -13 point differential , the only team in the division in the red after Week 7. Meanwhile, the Bengals are operating at +41 on the same stat. When push comes to shove, will the Browns be able to manufacture enough points to keep on winning down the road?
Then, there’s the four remaining divisional games on deck. Cleveland has yet to face the now heavy favorites Bengals, which they will do in Weeks 13 and 18. And, presumably, the Ravens will have Lamar Jackson back from injury in time for their Week 16 rematch.
Of course, next week’s test at Accrisure Stadium will be a big one, as the Browns face off against the Steelers for the second time this year after a tight win on a Thursday night. Remember, sweeps occur in the AFC North at a much lower rate than what league-wide averages show.
Then, of course, there’s the question of how long do you expect to continue to win on the games’ last drive , a model that’s been proven unsustainable over the long run over and over again.
The Browns cleaned up a number of things this Sunday against the Titans , but keep in mind it was a 1-5 opponent still looking for its first home win in eight tries on the other side of the field.
There’s no denying that Cleveland has been playing with fire, so it’s logical for so many to still be skeptical about the Browns until they prove they can win without the late-game drama.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Browns Rookie Spencer Fano Is Already Changing Cleveland's Offensive Line
full_text:
As the saying goes, “football is won in the trenches,” and that remains true for the Cleveland Browns.
The Cleveland Browns have struggled offensively throughout the 2026 season. Before the Titans matchup, the Browns ranked 28th in points per game and 29th in yards per game. That changed against Tennessee. The Browns exploded for 491 total yards and 27 points, driven by strong performances from multiple key skill players.
Quinshon Judkins with a big run to pick up the first down 🏃 CLEvsTEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TZiyT6cL3n
While many will focus on Deshaun Watson’s 308 passing yards or Quinshon Judkins’ 96 rushing yards and 2 rushing touchdowns, a budding star on the offensive line was also key to the Browns' victory.
The Cleveland Browns selected Utah offensive tackle Spencer Fano with the ninth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, signaling high expectations for his future. Despite playing right tackle during his final season in college, the Browns expected Fano to flip to the all-important blindside left tackle position, which he had experience with earlier in his career.
Fano has started every game at left tackle for the Browns this season, and while it hasn’t been all positive , Fano had a true breakout during the Browns' most recent matchup against the Tennessee Titans.
Spencer Fano earned his highest PFF grade of the season during the Browns' Week 7 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Fano received an initial grade of 92.2 , making him the highest-graded offensive player for the Browns in their 27-24 win.
Fano’s breakout came against a strong Titans defensive line that features star names like defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers, making his performance more impressive despite the Titans' now 1-6 record.
Love to see this. KC - orbit motion decoy (holds BS LB) Fano - down block on Simmons (All-Pro) Boston - crack block on PS safety Barber - counter kickout Fannin - counter pull for PS ILB Judkins - tight course, make CB miss Every key player mentioned here is 22yo or younger. pic.twitter.com/XW4Xue6x7h
Fano has shown flashes of greatness in his young career, but this is his most complete NFL game yet. If Fano can continue to build on performances like this throughout his rookie season, the Browns may have their left tackle for many years to come.
While the Titans' defensive front is no slouch, the next challenge comes against one of the league's best, the division rival Pittsburgh Steelers. While history is not on Cleveland’s side, the Browns haven’t won in Pittsburgh during the regular season since 2003. If Fano can build on this performance against a Pittsburgh defensive front featuring T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith and Cam Heyward, the sky may just be the limit for the young tackle’s career.

title: 5 Winners, 2 Losers From Browns Win Over Titans
full_text:
The Browns are now 5-2 seven weeks into the 2026 NFL season, to absolutely no one's surprise, after winning another game in the final seconds against the Tennessee Titans. Cleveland was down two touchdowns early in the game, but battled back in a huge way that ended up being their strongest offensive showing of the season.
There are a lot of points to note from the win, so let’s start off with the winners from Sunday.
Believe it or not, Watson’s 308 passing yards vs. Tennessee were the most in his Cleveland career, and the first time that he has thrown for 300+ since January 3rd, 2021, also against the Titans. His previous high with Cleveland was 289 in 2023, which came against, you guessed it, the Tennessee Titans.
Apart from the interception, Watson was very efficient in the passing game, getting the ball to the playmakers and giving them a chance to run with it. His rushing touchdown from nine yards out also gave Cleveland the cushion in the fourth quarter to leverage the game their way. Watson has now led the Browns to five game-winning drives this year, and is just the third quarterback since 1970 to have a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of a season, joining Troy Aikman in 1990 and Matthew Stafford in 2016.
Sunday was a breakout day for Quinshon Judkins; he rushed for 96 yards on 17 carries for two touchdowns. Those 5.6 yards per carry were the second-highest of his career so far, and it was because the offensive line was creating space for him. According to Next Gen Stats, Judkins averaged 2.3 yards before contact per carry, which was a season high and the first time this year he was over 1.0+ yards before contact.
Dylan Sampson was at last back in the backfield as well, and he showed off his speed totaling 77 yards on just nine touches, averaging 8.5 yards per touch.
What a breakout game it was for Concepcion; KC caught eight passes for 129 yards, and 82 of those yards came after the catch. Those 82 yards after the catch were a season-high for him, and his 55 yards after contact were the most by a wide receiver this season (NGS). He also was able to help in the run game, breaking an 18-yarder on an end around.
Might as well put the entire passing game on here, huh? Fannin was another guy who excelled after the catch, as 59 of his 91 receiving yards came after the catch. His 36-yard catch put Cleveland and the next winner right where they wanted to be.
While Szymt did miss a 43-yarder early in the fourth quarter, he stepped up when it mattered yet again, nailing a 32-yarder for a walk-off win. Szmyt now has four field goals that won Cleveland the game through seven weeks.
It is difficult to find losers for Cleveland from this game, but there are a couple.
Tony Pollard has Cleveland’s number as the Titans running back had another career day vs. the Browns, putting up 155 total yards and three touchdowns. The Browns are now 20th in the league in rushing yards allowed per game at 116.4, something that will hopefully get cleaned up later in the season.
Ward showed some flashes, hitting multiple slant routes to rookie Carnell Tate and second-year guy Elic Ayomanor for some nice gains. Apart from those throws, though, there wasn’t a ton of flashes, as he notably missed a touchdown on their final drive to Daniel Bellinger.
Ward is far from the Titans' first problem, but with the team at 1-6 and his stats are what they are, it may be alluring for Tennessee to look at those top QBs in next year’s class.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: If The Browns Keep Winning, Will Deshaun Watson Land a Big Deal?
full_text:
It is no secret that Deshaun Watson has been great this season for the Cleveland Browns . Through seven weeks, he has led the NFL in game-winning drives with five.
Looking forward, the Browns can absolutely keep winning games with Watson at the helm. There may even be a chance for a division title and playoff push.
But after the 2026 season is all said and done, what is in store for Watson? This is the final year of his previously historic five-year contract .
Let's look at three options for the Browns.
Understandably, if Watson takes the Browns to the playoffs, he will most likely get an extension.
Realistically, even if he were to get injured and miss the remainder of the season, Cleveland has seen enough to most likely pay the former first-round pick.
At this moment in time, Watson getting a new deal is the most likely situation.
Patrick Mahomes         Deshaun Watson - 5-1 record                    - 5-2 record - 1,474 pass yards       - 1,482 pass yards - 9 pass TD                    - 7 pass TD - 4 INT                             - 3 INT - 64.9 comp%               - 64.8 comp% - 71 rush yards… pic.twitter.com/vhQoVvPj5O
However, one fact stands out.
Deshaun Watson isn't getting any younger. At 31 years old with a deep injury history, there definitely is a risk when offering a new deal.
Additionally, with Shedeur Sanders patiently waiting his turn, does another contract drive him out of town? Let's look at the options if Watson is done after this season.
In a given situation where the Browns decide to move on, Shedeur Sanders is slated to be the next guy in line for Cleveland.
When was the last time the Browns had the chance to develop a quarterback behind one that was consistantly winning games?
Unless Sanders gets impatient and wants to find an opportunity elsewhere, he will have plenty of experience seeing the system executed when he gets his chance to step in
Before the 2026 season began, many fans thought the Browns would be looking forward to the 2027 NFL Draft with a top pick by this part of the season.
Still, Cleveland has the option to draft a quarterback, develop him behind Watson for a year, and trade Sanders.
This option may actually make the most sense for the Browns. Not only does it allow them to go after a first round talent, but they can also bring back Watson for another year or two to develop their draft pick and trade Sanders.
Who knows, maybe there is another team that has been eyeing Sanders from a distance and will give up a decent package for the young quarterback.

title: Where Browns Got it Right, Where Browns Got it Wrong vs. Titans
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns went into Nashville and rocked the Tennessee Titans to improve to 5-2 and maintained first place in the AFC North. The Browns once again relied upon a game-winning field goal against the lowly Titans, but the numbers tell a different story. The offense got plenty right in the road win, but there were also some aspects of the game that they got wrong.
Deshaun Watson had his first 300-yard game in his career with the Browns. Receivers were open and the ball was placed in a position to allow them to run after the catch. KC Concepcion shined in that role, amassing 129 receiving yards by juking, spinning, and breaking tackles. Watson got Harold Fannin Jr. involved and he made an incredible play to put them into field goal range at the end of the game. He had 91 receiving yards and he has to be a contributor on offense for the unit to play up to its potential.
The Browns welcomed the return of Dylan Sampson and utilized his speed on screen passes to gain crucial first downs. Watson threw an interception early in the game, but otherwise he protected the football and was only sacked one time.
The defense got eaten alive last season against the Titans’ running game, resulting in a loss. The defensive line has a new play style this season with more depth, but they again lacked to control the line of scrimmage. Tony Pollard averaged over five yards per rush on his way to 129 rushing yards. He started the game with a 36-yard rushing touchdown for an early lead.
The Browns have been feast or famine in stopping the run this season as they also had a lot of tackles for loss. When they were not hitting Pollard in the backfield, there were holes big enough for him to get to the secondary. The rushing defense’s potential was on full display during a goal line stand by getting a turnover on downs at the one yard line.
Grant Delpit and Emmanuel McNeil-Warren have been fantastic at playing near the line of scrimmage and helping the defensive line get pressure. But when they are not there, the holes have to be covered up.
The offense finally got their top-two running backs in the huddle for the first time this season and the attack looked greatly improved. Quinshon Judkins averaged 5.6 yards per rush on his way to a season best 96 yards. Sampson also had six carriers for over 7 yards per rush. The offense converted five-third downs in part to solid rushes on first and second downs.
Todd Monken even used Concepcion to rush the football , and he had a long run, setting up the offense. The successful rushing attack opened up the pass game as the Titans could not blitz Watson as often.
The Browns dominated in every statistic, except they lost the penalty battle. They had eight penalties for 48 yards. The yards were not much, but the timing was critical. The defense forced the Titans to punt late in the game on a critical drive, and they were relying on their place kicker to boot the ball. The special teams unit came out with 12 men on the field and a penalty was called, resulting in a first down for the Titans.
At both the end of the first and second halves, the offense found a way to score. At the end of the first half, the Browns marched down and Monken kept calling plays with time dwindling. He got the ball out quick and to the sidelines, and the Browns kicked an easy field goal to close out the half.
The offense got the ball back with around a minute left in the game and they got chunk plays to cruise down the field. They used the clock masterfully and the offense methodically got a chip-shot field goal to win the game. All five of their wins have come in game-winning fashion .

title: Biggest Takeaways From Browns Victory Over Titans
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns took down the Tennessee Titans 27-24 in their Week 7 matchup.
While the Brown and Orange walked away with the win, there are some major positives and negatives that we saw in the game.
Let's break down some of the biggest factors we saw out there on the field.
Maybe Tony Pollard has a grudge against the Browns' defense and pulls out his best performances when facing them. Regardless, the defense did a terrible job stopping the league's worst offense.
Coming into the game, the Titans ranked dead last In offensive yards per game, with 263.3. Against the Browns, they put up 322.
Time after time, Pollard would break down the Browns' run defense, which led to Cam Ward dicing up the secondary with quick passes and slant routes.
While there were some great plays made at times, it was very unsettling to see the Browns continually struggle against one of the statistically worst offenses in the entire NFL.
DESHAUN WATSON GO AHEAD TUDDY pic.twitter.com/KuhyT1ebzs
You could really argue that Deshaun Watson had two game-winning drives in this matchup.
He started by leading the Browns down the field and finding the end zone with his legs to take a late lead. After the defense gave up a touchdown, he once again marched Cleveland down the field and into field goal range with no time remaining.
At some point, it feels like the juice has to run out with these game-winning drives.
However, it is great to see the Browns finally getting the quarterback they traded for four years ago. As long as he can keep up the production, the Browns will keep winning games.
One of the statistics the Browns actually took advantage of was the fact that Tennessee allows the 21st most rushing yards per game in the NFL.
For the first time this season, Quinshon Judkins was able to produce for the Browns as he did in his rookie season.
On the game, Judkins finished with 96 rushing yards on 17 carries (5.6 yards per carry) while finding the endzone twice.
By far, the Browns run game looked the best it did all season. As a whole, Cleveland had 183 rushing yards on offense.
Week after week, the Browns can't seem to stay out of their own way.
Averaging nine penalties per game on the season coming into the game, Cleveland got flagged one shy of their mark to be at with a total of eight flags.
Still, multiple drives were halted and ruined thanks to simple mistakes.
One example to think about is Zion Johnson getting two holding penalties in the span of three plays. That surely has to be some sort of record somewhere.
No matter how ugly, a win is still a win.
While it would've been much nicer to see the Browns play better against a team they probably should've blown out, they still got the job done .
A lot of credit in this game has to go to Todd Monken. No matter what happened, good or bad, he kept his guys focused on the game and managed to come away victorious.
Cleveland truly has found their guy with Monken, and he continues to prove it week after week.

title: Dallas Cowboys Insider Pours Cold Water On Troy Aikman-Front Office Pipe Dream
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are riding high after cruising to victory over the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, but there is another storyline that has been running rampant.
In the days leading up to Monday Night Football and in the aftermath, there has been discussion about three-time Super Bowl champion Troy Aikman one day teaming up with Jerry Jones and taking a role in the front office.
The conversation began amid the ongoing drama between Aikman and his broadcasting partner Joe Buck at ESPN, and Aikman added fuel to the fire by saying he would be open to any conversations with Jones about a role with the team .
Jerry Jones has even said he would not rule out the possibility of adding Aikman in a front office role if that's the direction he decides to go with his career. However, not everyone is buying into the hype.
One longtime Cowboys insider and former ESPN reporter, Ed Werder, recently stopped by the Dan Patrick Show to share his thoughts on Aikman and Jones working together , and he's not willing to buy in. In fact, Werder appears confident that Aikman would never return to Dallas to work under Jones.
"Troy played for Jerry as a GM... Troy thinks he had half a career because Jerry wasn't a good GM." — @WerderEdNFL doesn't see Troy Aikman and Jerry Jones ever working together. pic.twitter.com/Q4GwyPBjff
"[Troy and Jerry] had a lot of disagreements about the way Jerry operates the franchise. And so Jerry said again this morning he'd be open to the idea of Troy joining, but I just don't see it. I mean, Troy played for Jerry as a general manager," Werder said. "Troy thinks he had half a career because Jerry wasn't a good general manager. And the thing he's done poorest of all as a general manager is hire coaches. We've seen Troy be involved as a consultant, hiring coaches and the general manager in Miami. And my thought at the time was, why isn't Troy doing for Jerry or for Miami what he should be doing for Jerry?
"I just don't think they're philosophically compatible. So I don't think it'll ever happen. I don't think... I don't think Jerry wants somebody else to get football credit if this team wins. Like he's spent 30 years on that crusade, and now he's going to hire Troy Aikman. And if they win from that point forward, Troy's going to get all the credit. Well, Troy's exceptionally close to Jimmy Johnson, closer to Jimmy than he is Jerry. And so for all those reasons, I just don't think this works."
While the thought of a franchise legend coming back to America's Team to help spark the franchise turnaround and help lead the Cowboys back to the promise land is great, it really is pretty unrealistic.
We know that Jerry loves a good bargain, and you aren't going to get Aikman for cheap. There will be a bidding war for his services if he chooses to continue his broadcasting career and parts ways with ESPN. And if he wants to get involved in a front office, his mind is something several franchises will want to bring in.
AIkman will be highly sought after, so Jerry Jones won't be bidding against himself, which as we've seen in the past, likely means that he will be losing out on another bidding way.

title: Stephen A. Smith Claims Dallas Cowboys Are Losing Confidence in Dak Prescott
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys put together an impressive effort on the ground in Monday night's 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Cowboys running back Javonte Williams finished with 25 carries for 155 yards and a touchdown, as Dallas had one of its best rushing performances since the Ezekiel Elliott era in a game that the franchise needed to win.
But through the air, Dak Prescott made some impressive throws when he needed to and proved to be the difference in Dallas cashing in drives for touchdowns instead of settling for field goals and keeping a wounded Eagles offense in the game.
His first two touchdown passes to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both came on third down, plays that ultimately swung the game in Dallas' favor. He finished 15 of 27 passing for 212 yards, three touchdowns and no picks.
But despite another solid day at the office for Prescott, Stephen A. Smith isn't letting that stop him from unleashing some foolish hot takes on his beloved Cowboys.
After getting cozy in the suite at Lincoln Financial Field with Jerry Jones on Monday night, Smith wasted no time making comments Tuesday morning that he would have never said in front of Jones.
During the latest episode of ESPN's First Take, Smith claimed that the Cowboys no longer have "supreme confidence" in Prescott and that the front office is "not satisfied." He made sure to emphasize that this is only his interpretation.
"This is my interpretation, I believe there's a lack of confidence, supreme confidence in Dak Prescott," Smith said. "You believe in him, you're paying him, but in the same breath, you're understanding the importance of having that balanced running attack. Because when you just have him dropping back the pass that football, you're not satisfied with the level of production that you're getting."
There's no doubt that Prescott hasn't been at his best this season, at least compared to the elite standards that he's set for himself.
"I believe there is a lack of confidence in Dak Prescott." — @stephenasmith on the Cowboys' offensive woes 😳 pic.twitter.com/HfLTB8U8yx
But to say that the Cowboys are losing confidence in their franchise quarterback after a few below-average games is another attempt by Smith to generate negative attention around Dallas -- as if there wasn't enough already.
In back-to-back losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers, Prescott finished with just two touchdowns and four interceptions. In his defense, both picks against Tampa Bay came off tipped passes, though the film from the Packers game is something Prescott will want to forget.
Smith is better off saving his foolish comments unless Prescott has consistent struggles throughout the rest of the season.
Until then, the Cowboys will have to live with the unfortunate reality that they might be one of the worst teams in the NFL if not for the presence of Prescott.

title: Why Cowboys Cut Reserve RB Following Week 7 Victory Over Eagles
full_text:
After moving on from Jaydon Blue following a disappointing preseason, the Dallas Cowboys brought in former TCU running back Emari Demercado . The fourth-year back gave the Cowboys something they didn't have in their backfield, which was game-breaking speed .
He was never able to put that on display, however, as Demercado appeared in just two games and had 15 yards on five attempts. Now for the second time this year, Demercado has been waived by the Cowboys.
Demercado had been surpassed on the depth chart by Tyler Goodson, who had 10 rushing attempts for 38 yards in their win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Goodson's ascension isn't the only reason Demercado was released, though.
Demercado was waived, along with backup tight end D.J. Rogers , to open up two spots on the 53-man roster. That's a good sign for two defenders who have been on the IR, but recently had their 21-day practice windows opened.
Outside linebacker Marist Liufau suffered a fractured forearm in the preseason finale against the New Orleans Saints and has yet to play this season. His practice window was opened during their prep for Week 7, but he didn't make the trip to Philadelphia.
Safety PJ Locke suffered a torn plantar fascia in their Week 2 win over the Washington Commanders. Like Liufau, he returned to practice last week but did not make the trip with the team for the Monday Night Football matchup.
Getting Locke back could be huge since the Dallas pass defense has been suspect. They've also been dealing with multiple injuries and could use Locke, who has experience working with defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
There's also an outside chance Jalen Thompson could be returning soon, although his practice window has yet to be opened.
A third-round pick out of Notre Dame in 2024, Liufau has been a traditional linebacker throughout his career. Once Parker took over, he was moved to the edge, where Parker believes he can use his speed to cause problems in the offensive backfield.
He's also one of the top special teams players on the roster, which is where he will make his biggest impact. The Cowboys have had issues in coverage, and were hit with multiple penalties during their win over Philadelphia.
Adding an experienced player such as Liufau could be a major boost for this struggling unit.

title: Jerry Jones Isn't Optimistic About Cowboys' Chances of Making Trade to Improve Defense
full_text:
Back in training camp, Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones made it very clear he's open to making moves .
And that has continued to be the case during the 2026 season, even after the blockbuster deal with the Pittsburgh Steelers for cornerback Joey Porter Jr.
However, being open to making a big trade and actually being able to pull one off are two very different things. It takes two to tango and Jones not only has to find something that makes sense and can make a big impact, but the price has to be right, too.
On Tuesday, Jones was once again asked if he'd be open to making another trade to add to the Cowboys' defense.
He reiterated that he is, but he noted that it's "unlikely" Dallas will be able to pull something off.
"If we could do it where we sit right now, I would add to it," Jones said on 105.3 The Fan (H/T Tommy Yarrish of DallasCowboys.com ). "But the adding to it is a big statement. It's unlikely we'll get the opportunity from outside coming in. But if it's there, I'll do it."
Smaller trades will likely be available for Jones, but the Cowboys' defense needs something significant to try and fix what is a very broken unit — and even then that might not be enough.
This defense is more than just one player away. There are so many issues and defensive coordinator Christian Parker's play-calling is among them, which leaves little faith Parker will actually be able to maximize whoever Jones brings in.
The biggest need the Cowboys have comes at edge rusher. Dallas' group has just 3.5 sacks, with Donovan Ezeiruaku leading the way with 1.5, followed by Rashan Gary and Malachi Lawrence each having one. Von Miller has been a total zero , both literally and figuratively.
The problem is that the Cowboys need to add an elite edge rusher and those guys are rarely available. Maxx Crosby has been a name often mentioned for the Cowboys, but with the Las Vegas Raiders not being as bad as expected, it's possible he's going to stay.
There should be options on the next tier, with guys like the Arizona Cardinals' Josh Sweat and the Los Angeles Chargers' Khalil Mack likely to be among the best options out there, but the Cowboys have to compete with several other teams in the market for an addition and Dallas' stockpile of draft picks is low.
Knowing all of that, Cowboys fans need to seriously temper their expectations for what Dallas will do at the trade deadline.

title: Jerry Jones Leaves No Doubt About Desire to Add Troy Aikman to Cowboys' Front Office
full_text:
With Troy Aikman seemingly on his way out at ESPN, many have wondered if his next job might be with the Dallas Cowboys.
Aikman's contract is about to run out after this season and there is no sense that ESPN is going to extend him. That would mean the Hall of Famer will be a free-agent broadcaster, but might he be interested in a front office role instead?
The only semblance of a front office role Aikman has ever had came with the Miami Dolphins, when he was hired as a consultant for their general manager search. However, we know Aikman has a wealth of football knowledge and it certainly wouldn't hurt for the Cowboys to add some new blood after 30 years without a title.
When asked if adding Aikman is a real possibility, Jerry Jones told 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday he absolutely would do it.
"Yes, I could and would," he said (H/T Patrik Walker ). "It’s that simple because I do think that much of him and his command of NFL knowledge and football. He is qualified to do anything.
“Don’t rule it out. It is very possible.”
The topic has been broached before, but it came up yet again on Monday night after Aikman and Jones were spotted on the field talking for about 10 minutes before Dallas' Monday night game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
We don't know what was said, but the internet immediately ran with the idea they were talking about a front office role, which probably wasn't the case but is fun to consider.
We know Jerry is down, but what about his former quarterback?
Aikman has already touched on this subject before and made it clear he would at least "look at" joining the Cowboys if a position was offered to him.
"I would welcome any conversation with Jerry, and quite honestly I don't know if there ever would be an opportunity," Aikman said to Mike Fisher.
"But if Jerry came to me and felt in his heart that I could lend some services that would help make them better, I'd have a hard time not taking a good look at that," Aikman added.
What's important for a possible Cowboys-Aikman union is what he is actually looking for. If Aikman simply wants to be a consultant with a minor, advisory role, then we can see it happening.
But if he's looking to get his hands dirty and have the ability to make significant decisions, like a general manager would, for example, we can't envision Aikman joining the Cowboys.
That's because Jerry isn't going to give up his power, something Aikman knows full well. If Aikman wants a front office role with significant power, he'd have to go elsewhere, unless Jerry is looking to fire himself after 30-plus years.
We aren't holding our breath for that.
It appears ESPN has no desire to renew Aikman's contract and will simply let him walk, and Aikman is now realizing that this might be it for him as a broadcaster.
"As I'm into my last year at ESPN, I'm realizing that this is something that could very well be taken away from me," Aikman said to Fisher. "For the first time, I'm realizing how much I really do – I've always enjoyed it. I've always known that. But until you risk having something taken away from you, I think sometimes you tend to maybe take things for granted."
With Aikman's tenure at ESPN and quite possibly broadcasting in general winding down, that has created some beef between himself and his broadcasting partner , Joe Buck, with the two reportedly having a heated exchange a few weeks ago before the Monday Night Football game on Oct. 12.
“It nearly got physical off air,” a source told In Touch Weekly . “They were very close from coming to blows.”
It remains to be seen if Aikman, who has been one of the top NFL broadcasters for several years now, will get another gig after his ESPN contract runs out.
If not, an NFL front office job could be in his future, whether that's with the Cowboys or another team.

title: Cowboys Legend Troy Aikman Gives Brutally Honest Take Following Week 7 Win
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys pulled off a 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7. That ended a two-game losing streak and keeps them alive in the NFC East .
Still, they're just 3-4 on the season and there are plenty of reasons to be concerned. That includes the fact that their Monday Night Football win wasn't nearly as easy as the score indicates. Dallas eventually pulled away by scoring the final 18 points, but they were trailing 21-20 in the second half to a beat up Eagles team.
With Tanner McKee filling in for Jalen Hurts, the Eagles offense still had its moments. They might have had even more if Philly had DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks in action, as there were multiple drops by their reserve wideouts. Dallas also couldn't stop Saquon Barkley, who was in obvious pain as he played through a hamstring injury.
That's why Cowboys legend Troy Aikman isn't ready to change his tune. Aikman, who called the game for ESPN, was asked by Scott Van Pelt if this result changed his perception on Dallas. Aikman was brutally honest, saying this didn't move the needle for him.
"Not really. I mean, not really. And I don't mean that as a negative. Not really. I mean, this is a beat-up Philadelphia team. I mean, to come in here and win tonight. I mean, let's not get carried away. You know, they kind of did what you would expect them to do. I did think the Eagles defensively would put up a little bit more of a fight than what they did," Aikman said.
Scott Van Pelt: "Does tonight kind of change the way you see [the Cowboys]?" Troy Aikman: "Eh, not really. Not really. And I don't mean that as a negative... This is a beat-up Philadelphia team. To come in here and win tonight, I mean, let's not get carried away." 🏈🎙️ pic.twitter.com/kZrwflNWQy
"But, you know, it'll bear itself out as we move forward as to what, this team's capable. Defense did some good things. They've still got a ways to go. But that's going to be the key to this team is how far along can this defense come between now and when the playoffs roll around, if they get in."
Aikman has never been shy about criticizing his former team, even calling out the wide receivers for their route running after Week 6. Fans typically appreciate Aikman's honesty, and they also would love for him to take an active role in fixing the organization, something we recently wrote about after Aikman said he would be open to such a thing .
Unfortunately, Jerry Jones is unlikely to bring in anyone who would try and change the way they operate, which is exactly what someone such as Aikman would do.
Dallas has two more games coming up that they should be able to win. In Week 8, they host the 2-5 Arizona Cardinals and in Week 9, they visit the 2-5 Indianapolis Colts.
Of course, no win is easy in the NFL, and the Cardinals are a team that has upset Dallas frequently. Still, this is the best stretch of the season for them to turn things around and begin to build some confidence. We just have to see if they can remain focused and take advantage.
