title: 5 Risers, 3 Fallers After Detroit Lions First Division Win
full_text:
The Detroit Lions handled business and earned a win over the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 of the NFL season.
While it wasn't the cleanest effort, the Lions overcame some of their self-made adversity and ultimately secured a divisional victory in their first NFC North clash of the season.
Here are risers and fallers following the Lions' Week 7 win over the Packers.
Branch was somewhat limited in his return from a torn Achilles, as he played 45 snaps. However, head coach Dan Campbell stated that they took the restraints off at halftime, as he proved to be acclimating well after missing the first five games of the year.
The Alabama product recorded an interception, which was his first since the 2024 season, and provided a spark for the defense. Moving forward, the Lions will continue to increase his workload and he will likely be a difference maker for a secondary that has struggled in his absence.
After a sluggish start to the season, Williams has been finding a groove . He has scored twice in each of the last two games, and has had at least 90 yards in two of the team's last three games.
Williams is the team's bona fide No. 2 option behind Amon-Ra St. Brown, and will continue to be relied upon to produce at a high level. Though the start to the season caused some concerns, Williams appears to be fully out of that funk and should be consistently contributing moving forward.
Viewed as exclusively a special teams contributor, Dorsey got some opportunities on defense and delivered in a big way. Detroit's secondary has been much maligned, and for good reason, through the first five games, but Dorsey delivered a spark in the win over the Packers.
In 14 snaps, Dorsey earned a Pro Football Focus defensive grade of 87.7 and allowed just one completion for five yards on four targets. He earned a shoutout from Campbell in the postgame, and should be a bigger part of the rotation moving forward.
The Lions signed the journeyman Carter after the season-ending injury to Tom Kennedy, and he showed why he's been coveted throughout his career. Carter averaged 26 yards on his two kick returns, and had a 15-yard punt return that he nearly sprung for a huge gain.
Detroit has been angling to get more production out of the return game, and Carter appears to be suited to deliver in that aspect of the game.
With the injury to Devin White, there were opportunities available for a third linebacker in Detroit's defense. It was Nowaske who received the most snaps in that role behind Jack Campbell and Derrick Barnes.
Though it was only 14 snaps, Nowaske showed that he is capable of contributing. He's become a very valuable part of Detroit's linebacker rotation, and appears to be climbing the depth chart midway through his fourth professional season.
Mays got off to a slow start in his Lions debut, as he had a role in two costly turnovers. First, he accidentally punched the ball out of the hands of Jahmyr Gibbs on a late drive in the first half where the Lions appeared poised to extend their lead before halftime.
After halftime, a miscue on a snap between Mays and quarterback Jared Goff resulted in a fumble and subsuquent score on the ensuing drive from the Packers. Mays could certainly shake off the rust and bounce back, but with how well Juice Scruggs was playing he will certainly face some scrutiny.
LaPorta made plenty of headlines with his comments regarding the ongoing contract situation. He addressed the situation and made legitimate claims as to why it's important, but didn't make a huge impact in Sunday's game.
After a strong start to the season, LaPorta was kept in check by the Packers' defense. Part of this was due to the Lions targeting St. Brown and Williams on a majority of passes, while it also had to do with the Packers having a good plan for him.
LaPorta had just one catch for 18 yards, which was his lowest output of the season and the first time he's been held to just one catch in his career since Week 7 of the 2024 season.
Izien did not record any defensive snaps for the second-consecutive game. The former Tampa Bay Buccaneer was limited to exclusively special teams duty, with rookie Keith Abney logging 34 snaps even after Branch returned.
As Branch continues to acclimate, the Lions will increase his workload. At this juncture, it looks as though Abney is ahead of Izien, which means the veteran may continue to be kept out of the defensive rotation unless an injury occurs.

title: 3 Things We Learned About Detroit Lions After Win Over Packers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions recorded arguably their biggest win of the 2026 season on Sunday, defeating the NFC North rival Green Bay Packers, 20-17.
It was a gritty performance from Dan Campbell's squad which did not play its cleanest game, but still did enough right in order to secure the Week 7 victory.
For starters, Kelvin Sheppard's defense, aided by the return of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch, stepped up big time in the divisional affair.
It limited Green Bay signal-caller Jordan Love to under 300 yards passing and kept the Packers’ pass-catching duo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden in check. Both receivers were held under 60 yards and out of the end zone.
Plus, the Lions’ run defense delivered a strong effort, holding Green Bay to just 60 total yards on the ground on 19 carries (3.2 yards/carry).
And Branch had his fingerprints all over the standout performance from Sheppard's unit.
In his first taste of action since tearing his Achilles in Week 14 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys, the defensive back made his presence known.
He logged four total tackles and a pass defensed, and came through with a crucial interception of Love to start the fourth quarter. It wasn't an easy pick to come up with, either.
On the play (third-and-21), the Packers were backed up deep in Lions territory and Love decided to heave the football. It landed past the 50-yard line, where Branch high-pointed the ball and grabbed it out of the air, beating Watson for the 50/50 ball.
BRIAN BRANCH IS BACK GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/F1Pa2vK3fI
It was a prime example of Branch's next-level athleticism and the immense impact he can make in the back-end of Detroit's defensive backfield .
“You go through an injury like that; the amount of rehab and things that go into all of that to get back to where you're ready to play at a high level in the NFL," Lions head man Dan Campbell said of Branch after the game. "You get back to some of what you are, and he's not even fully back yet as far as just the rust. Every rep he takes he's going to get better and better. It's not an easy road. That was a huge play. Everybody loves (Branch) because he's a great teammate and a productive football player. He can just find the ball.”
Campbell & Co. direly missed the Alabama product, and there's no question he played an integral role in the Lions securing the win in the divisional tilt.
Undoubtedly, the defense is leaps and bounds better with Branch healthy.
On Sunday, it also became evident that Cade Mays was not quite ready to anchor the line.
Playing in his first game since being acquired by Detroit this offseason, Mays had a hand in two turnovers: a Jahmyr Gibbs fumble to close the first half and a botched snap in the opening seconds of the second half.
Meanwhile, on a positive note, it became apparent the Lions’ offense can afford to be less than perfect every so often.
Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing's unit was just good enough against Green Bay, and that was more than fine in the Week 7 divisional clash.
Veteran signal-caller Jared Goff threw a ball or two that could have been picked, and the ever explosive Jahmyr Gibbs was contained fairly well by the Packers for most of the game. Yet, it didn't matter on Sunday.
Goff still came through with big-time throws to the likes of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams when it counted the most, and Gibbs ran out the clock in the fourth quarter, setting up Jake Bates for the game-winning field goal as time expired.
Refreshingly, in the Week 7 contest , the Lions’ offense did not have to lead the way and score 30-plus points in order to get into the win column. Instead, the defense took on the protagonist role, allowing Petzing's unit to take a much-deserved backseat.
It was a perfect example of the complementary football that Campbell often preaches about – a winning brand of football that the best teams play on a consistent basis.
And if the Lions want to rise to the top of the NFC, they'll need to play a lot more of that type of football moving forward, including in Week 8 against the undefeated Minnesota Vikings.
Simply, it's the only way Detroit will be able to make a Super Bowl run in 2026.

title: Lions Provide Key Injury Updates: Will St. Brown, Rakestraw Miss Practice?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions had two players with minor injuries, following the teams Week 7 contest against the Green Bay Packers.
Head coach Dan Campbell, speaking to local reporters, updated the minor ankle injuries to wideout Amon-Ra St. Brown and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw.
Both are not currently expected to miss the Vikings game, but could miss one single practice on Wednesday.
Rakestraw played 31 percent of defensive snaps against Green Bay, as Detroit's secondary rotation was effective in limiting the explosive plays in a 20-17 home victory.
If Rakestraw has any setbacks, Roger McCreary, Khalil Dorsey and Keith Abney both have the opportunity to step in during his absence.
Detroit's former second-round pick was urging coach Campbell to play even more in the first half in his first game returning from a torn Achilles tendon.
"I asked for God just to have a clean game and we all had a clean game," said Branch. "We executed. We still left a lot of plays out there again, that comes with it. But we all played a hell of a game and I'm just proud to be a part of the secondary. We done been through a lot and now it's time to hit the ground running now."
He added later, "Just telling him when I get out there, my adrenaline going, so I'm ready to go. The plan was to pitch count. I kind of didn't like it, but they were smart for doing it and I just thanked them because they were looking out for me.”
Branch earned his first interception of the 2026 season. He expressed, "Oh, it felt good. Just to grabbing the pick the first game out, that's nothing but God.”
With each performance since the Bills loss, the team's defense has steadily gained confidence.
"Shepp called a hell of a gameplan, put everybody in the right spot," said Branch. "And again, once we execute it's wraps and that's all we got to do moving forward is execute his game plan.”

title: Everything Lions QB Jared Goff Said After Win Over Packers

The 32-year-old has led 18 game-winning drives as a Lions player (26 in career) and became one of only four signal-callers in NFL history to throw one or more touchdowns and zero interceptions in each of the first six games of a season. The others include Russell Wilson, Alex Smith and Milt Plum.

The pass rush is still what it is. It's fun to watch, man. It really is. And they're getting us the ball back, and we got to do better in some of those situations to extend that lead, but they kept us in it.”

And we wanted to get the first down but wanted to get down and (Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs) Gibby knew that, but he didn't want to get dragged into the end zone if he got too close. So, we ended up in that third-and-1 situation, which we really should have gotten the first down and things would've been maybe a bit easier, but end of the day we got it done, got them to jump offsides before that and made the field goal, so all good.”
“Yeah, massive, massive. And I thought our guys did a great job of not responding to some of the stuff that was going on and just staying in it, staying disciplined and doing our job and that was good.”
“No, I don't think it's - because to us, we're just running the play that's called. It's hard on the sidelines, certainly. And I thought that was as good as it gets at clock management from how much time we had, like four minutes. And then knowing we don't want to give them the ball back. A lot of teams probably take a field goal there with 30 seconds and they have a chance, but we didn't want to do that, and we handled it really well and did everything we wanted to and the kicked it with no time left.”
“Of course. Yeah, of course. If it was the last play of the game and if there's 10 seconds left, maybe he can score, but we didn't want him to .”
“Did he block it? Awesome, amazing. Yeah, I didn't know he blocked it. That's awesome. That's a huge individual effort. The field goals from there typically are pretty high percentage, and to be able to get the ball back, to miss that fourth down conversion and get the ball back with no harm, no foul. Again, hats off to our defense and DJ there with the block.”
“Cade was great. Cade was really good and getting his feet back underneath him and making the calls. They did a lot of stuff defensively that was different when they had (Packers LB Zaire Franklin) 44 out of the game. They changed a little bit of what they were doing with the front pressures and whatnot, and I thought he handled it really well.”
"I came out a little early, I’ve got to stay in there.”
“No, I don't think so. I think you guys know it's cyclical. It comes and goes, and I think what makes our group so special is (WR Isaac) TeSlaa is a huge third-down conversion that was his only catch of the game. (TE) Sam (LaPorta) has the huge two-minute drive catch-and-run and the other one on top of that. That was two massive plays in the game. These guys were staying in it, staying in it, staying in it, and doing their job even when the ball's not coming to them.”
“Yeah, he's good. He started catching stride, and it's dangerous for defenses for sure.”
“Yeah, and he actually drew some coverage. I was talking about it with (Tom) Brady there after the game. He did. The linebacker went to him, and it allowed (WR Jameson Williams) Jamo to be open, and he did exactly what he was supposed to do; ran exactly to the spot, and he was ready for it too. And he told me after, he's like, 'If you were going to throw it to me, I was ready for it.' And I would've if the linebacker didn't go to him and ended up working out great with Jamo.”
“They all count the same. They all are the same. If we play this game now or later in the year with the division on the line. Of course, we know it's a division game. We know it is important to win these ones, but we treat them all the same. They all count the same, and the division ones are maybe slightly more important, but they all count the same.”
“Yeah, I don't know. Play good in the first quarter next week, that would be the answer. I don't know. I thought we did a good job of trying to, even with the Bye week, pull back some of that momentum in practice this week that we had in Arizona and build that into the game. And I think it starts up front with the O-line. Thought they had a great game, they really did. And moving the line of scrimmage and giving me a nice pocket when those guys do that, man, certainly in the first drive , like you're asking, we can do anything.”

title: Packers-Panthers Tuesday Injury Report: Time Near for Micah Parsons, Kevin Zeitler?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – As is typically the case for a Thursday night game, the Green Bay Packers will be a banged-up bunch for their game against the Carolina Panthers.
The Packers held a walk-through practice on Tuesday. If they would have practiced, they would have been down four starters. One of them was Travis Glover, who has started the past four games at right guard.
More on that and the injury report in a moment. But first, there was a potential big update on the status of Micah Parsons.
The Packers didn’t designate Micah Parsons for return this week because the team doesn’t actually practice this week, which would mean one-third of his 21-day return-to-play window would have been wasted.
“I sure hope so,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Wednesday evening.
There was a touch of optimism there, though LaFleur was quick to remind that it will be a medical decision before the superstar pass rusher returns to practice.
“I’m itching for it, though, for sure,” LaFleur said.
Glover is dealing with a knee injury and didn’t play particularly well against the Lions. If he’s not ready, will Kevin Zeitler make his long-awaited debut?
“You shall see,” LaFleur said.
Zeitler was inactive against Detroit and has played only on special teams in his two appearances.
“If we need him, absolutely,” LaFleur said when asked if Zeitler is ready to contribute on offense. “I think he's done a nice job. Here's a guy that came in and didn't have an offseason, didn't have training camp, and he's kind of gradually working his way back into it.”
Linebacker Zaire Franklin would not have practiced due to the shin injury sustained at practice last week and will not be ready for Thursday, LaFleur said. That means a secon consecutie week for Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper.
Receiver Matthew Golden (shoulder and foot) did not practice. Along with Christian Watson, Golden is the driving force in the passing game. Without him, the Packers would be incredibly shorthanded in terms of passing-game playmakers.
“I sure hope so,” LaFleur said when asked about Golden’s availability, “but we're still kind of working through it. You're not getting any real reps. Everything's pretty much walk-through. We will have a short indy [individual drills period] tomorrow, but to move guys around and see how they look, but certainly hopeful for him.”
The fourth and final player to not practice was center Sean Rhyan, who suffered a high-ankle sprain early in the loss at Detroit and will miss “at least” four games , according to Matt Zenitz of CBS.
LaFleur wouldn’t say if John Williams would get the start after playing well in his first career snaps from scrimmage. The other options are Jager Burton and Donovan Jennings.
“We'll see. We're kind of working through everything right now,” LaFleur said.
There was some good news, though. Defensive tackles Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and Anthony Campbell (ankle) would not have practiced on Monday but would have been limited on Tuesday. Campbell was one of the standouts against Detroit.
Same as with Green Bay, four Panthers starters would not have practiced on Monday: defensive tackle Bobby Brown III (hand), cornerback Akayleb Evans (triceps/knee), left guard Damien Lewis (knee) and outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips (hamstring). Brown and Coker, though, moved to full participation on Tuesday.
Still a DNP was Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract in free agency this past offseason. He has 2.5 sacks in five games but was inactive last week against Tampa Bay.
“We’re [going to] try to get him back for this game but, again, the recurring same hamstring,” Panthers coach Dave Canales told reporters on Monday. “It’s still that kind of a tight window, so it'll be close on that one.”
Evans started three of six games and has two pass breakups. Brown is the 332-pounder in the middle of Carolina’s defense.
Not on the injury lists are the starting offensive tackles, left tackle Ikem Ekwonu and right tackle Taylor Moton. They are on injured reserve. Former Packers starter Rasheed Walker has struggled in place of Ekwonu. According to Pro Football Focus, he’s tied for the NFL lead with 26 pressures allowed.
Quarterback Bryce Young was full participation for a second consecutive day as he handles an ankle injury.
This will be Green Bay’s third game against him, late in his rookie season in 2023 and again last year.
“It's been pretty remarkable to watch him,” LaFleur said. “The one thing that jumps off tape is just how he anticipates, and he is not scared. I mean, he'll stand in there, he'll get blasted, he'll get rid of the ball, but he throws into tight windows with a lot of anticipation, and he's got people to throw to.”
Did not participate: LB Zaire Franklin (shin), RG Travis Glover (knee), WR Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot), C Sean Rhyan (ankle).
Limited participation: G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), edge Brenton Cox (quad), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle).
Full participation: CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring).
Did not participate: CB Akayleb Evans (triceps/knee), LG Damien Lewis (knee), OLB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), G Torricelli Simpkins (ankle).
Limited participation: None.
Full participation: DT Bobby Brown III (hand), WR Jalen Coker (shoulder), QB Bryce Young (ankle).

title: Packers-Panthers Matchups: Can Green Bay Take Advantage of Huge Weakness?
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers dropped to last place in the NFC North with a mistake-laden 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday.
They have very little time to lick their wounds thanks to another home date on Thursday night, this one against the Carolina Panthers, who beat the Packers at Lambeau last season.
The Packers had their three-game winning streak snapped by Detroit and are 4-3. The Panthers are 3-3 and lead the NFC South. They are coming off a 43-13 loss to Tampa Bay.
Both teams need a win. How do they get it? Here’s our look at the weekly matchups.
Carolina’s passing offense is a bit of a one-man band. Tetairoa McMillan leads the team in targets, receptions and yards. He’s 11th in the league with 511 yards even while playing one fewer game than most teams. He’s second on the team in touchdowns behind field-stretching tight end Darren Waller.
McMillan caught just four passes for 46 yards last year against Green Bay, but was one of the top rookie receivers in football as he won the Offensive Rookie of the Year Award. The one blemish on his season is that while he’s only dropped one pass, he’s fumbled twice.
Carolina’s passing game starts with Bryce Young, who has been solid if unspectacular this season. He’s thrown 12 touchdowns to just four picks but has been sacked 17 times. He ranks 14th in the league in passer rating.
According to Next Gen Stats, old friend Rasheed Walker leads the Panthers in giving up 34 pressures and four sacks. He allowed three sacks against Tampa Bay on Sunday.
The Packers could have potential for a bounce-back game. Their pass rush was largely nonexistent against the Lions’ Jared Goff, and their coverage suffered as a result.
The combo of Young and McMillan, however, is not exactly the Lions’ offense on turf against Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam LaPorta. The Packers should have a good chance to control the passing game.
Jonathan Gannon probably would have signed up for giving up just 119 yards on 29 carries to Jahmyr Gibbs in Sunday’s game against the Lions.
The Packers have done a good job at controlling opposing ground games save for one disastrous performance against Bijan Robinson on a Thursday night against Atlanta. They’re ranked 17th in the NFL with 115 rushing yards allowed per game.
The Panthers are 21st in yards gained per game on the ground. The question in this matchup will be the health and availability of Green Bay’s defensive line. Anthony Campbell and Devonte Wyatt were estimated non-participants in practice. The Packers got a boost to their depth last week with Jordan Riley returning from last year’s Achilles injury, but are starting to run thin on healthy bodies up front.
As poor as Carolina has been in some games against opposing offenses, its pass defense is pretty good. It ranks sixth in the NFL with just 195.7 passing yards allowed per game and eighth with an opponent passer rating of 83.9.
The defensive backs have yet to get their hands on an interception, as its leading man in that department is linebacker Devin Lloyd with two.
One potential game-changing dynamic this week in this matchup will be the availability, or lack thereof, for the Panthers’ star rusher, Jaelen Phillips. Phillips wrecked the game against Green Bay last year when he was playing for the Eagles. According to PFF, Phillips had eight pressures and two quarterback hits as the Eagles held Jordan Love and Co. to just 10 points. He has 2.5 sacks in five games this season.
Last week, the Packers piled up yards but could not find their way into the red zone. Their offense inside the red area was putrid, going 1-of-4, which included a failed fourth down and a missed chip-shot field goal by Trey Smack.
The drops are becoming obscene. Matt LaFleur can continue to say that it’s just football and those things happen. He’s right to some degree, but they need to find a solution. Matthew Golden, Bo Melton and Josh Jacobs were culprits last week. All three cost them big plays, including a potential game-winning score from Jacobs.
There will be some shuffling on the offensive line. The question is how much? John Williams played most of last week’s game at Detroit after starter Sean Rhyan suffered a high-ankle sprain and backup Jacob Monk sustained an injured quad. Rhyan will miss at least a few weeks and Monk is on injured reserve. Presumably, Williams will start, but don’t discount the possibility of Jager Burton getting the call.
Right guard Travis Glover is on the injury report with a knee injury. Left guard Aaron Banks, the former starter, was active last week but sat on the bench in favor of Laken Tomlinson.
Regardless, they need to protect Jordan Love better than they have the last two weeks against Ejiro Evero’s defense.
The potential for big plays always makes the Packers a threat, but the lack of consistency pushes this matchup to a draw.
As it turns out, Josh Jacobs was not enough to save the Packers’ run game from the depths of hell it continues to descend into.
The Packers remain 32nd in the league in rushing, with their 59.9-yard average right in line with the 60 yards gained against the Lions.
Perhaps some good news is on the way? The Panthers have the worst rush defense in the league, giving up a league-worst 153.2 rushing yards per game and a league-high 5.16 yards per carry. They also lead the league in rushing touchdowns surrendered with 11.
“Just be quicker,” Jacobs said on Tuesday. “Just stuff that come with playing ball. I would also say just keep try to encourage the guys and make the O-line right when it’s opportunities. That’s the only thing I would’ve been preaching really this whole week, just telling guys to finish straight up on guys and allow me to be me and allow me to make them right, so just trying to have that trust.
“Obviously, this week we have a different group of guys up there, so it’s going to be a feel-out process. But we’ll see how it goes.”
The Panthers were clobbered by Chicago in Week 1, when D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai ran for more than 100 yards. Quarterback Caleb Williams added another 65. Overall, Chicago carried 39 times for 291 yards and averaged 7.5 yards per carry.
Sunday’s blowout loss against Tampa Bay was pretty similar. The Bucs averaged 5.3 yards per carry, piling up 258 yards on 49 attempts.
The Packers’ run game should have some opportunities this week, but you don’t have to look that far into the past to see another game where they should have had chances to get moving. Dallas was the worst run defense in the NFL when it came to Lambeau a couple weeks ago, and the Packers’ leading rusher had 28 yards.
Maybe Jacobs changes things this week as he’s more acclimated, but until there’s any improvement that is seen on the field, it’s impossible to give the Packers the benefit of the doubt.
One of the biggest reasons the Panthers were able to knock off the Packers at Lambeau Field last year was Brandon McManus missing a field goal.
McManus’ struggles last season culminated with a disastrous performance in the postseason. As a result, the Packers traded two draft choices to grab Trey Smack in the sixth round.
Smack has shown off a big leg. He’s 2-for-2 on kicks more than 50 yards this season. The problems have been for the more makeable field goals. Smack is 5-of-9 on kicks between 30 and 49 yards. He’s also missed two extra-point attempts. In the three-point loss to Detroit, he missed a 26-yard field goal and had a 35-yarder tipped at the line for another miss.
This is the rollercoaster ride the Packers chose to get on when they gave a rookie kicker unlimited runway, like they did with Anders Carlson during the 2023 season. That year, predictably, ended in disaster with Carlson missing a key field goal in the team’s postseason loss to the 49ers.
We’re a long way away from Smack deciding a playoff game, should the Packers even qualify.
For now, however, he’s the single biggest reason that special teams goes in the direction of whoever Green Bay is playing.

title: Week 8 Consensus NFL Power Rankings: After Big Rise, How Far Did Packers Fall?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers lost 20-17 in Motown on Sunday, but they weren’t driven off a cliff in our Consensus NFL Power Rankings.
First, what are the Consensus Power Rankings? We take eight sets of national power rankings and turn them into one turbocharged power ranking.
With a three-game winning streak, the Packers rose from 24th to 12th in our rankings . After the three-point loss to Detroit, they fell back three spots to 15th.
Here is a closer look, with more information and full rankings available by clicking on the links.
The Packers slipped six spots in Conor Orr’s rankings .
“I’m not sure why – maybe it’s because Jordan Love had a two-week stretch where he played like the Madden quarterback of our dreams – but I am more interested in Green Bay at the trade deadline than any other team in football. I’m still not letting go of Super Bowl aspirations for this team.”
Pete Prisco dropped the Packers only one spot in his rankings.
“Their winning streak came to an end against the Lions in what was a sloppy game. The injuries on the offensive line are a big concern.”
Mike Florio dropped the Packers five spots and offered a word of warning. “They can’t let one loss become two on Thursday night.”
The Packers are down four spots in ESPN’s rankings , which are voted on by their team beat writers.
This week’s theme is best offseason addition. Rob Demovsky selected defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon, who has kept the defense going without Micah Parsons on the strength of takeaways.
“They lead the NFL in forced turnovers (13) and interceptions (nine). They've already topped their interception total from all of last season (seven) and nearly matched their takeaway total (14). Two years ago, the Packers had the fourth-most takeaways with 31, including 17 interceptions. … Gannon has also used disguises and blitzes to manufacture pressure without injured edge rusher Micah Parsons.”
Nick Shook kept the Packers at No. 15 after they lost due in part to Trey Smack’s two missed kicks.
“I can’t dock the Packers for losing a close divisional game on the road, but I can suggest they start exploring other kicking options. … Looking ahead, I am curious to see how much of a difference Josh Jacobs can make for Green Bay’s largely inept running game.”
The Packers were dinged only one spot in Frank Schwab’s rankings. He focused on the officiating – including Xavier McKinney’s reaction. But:
“Officiating or not, the Packers made key errors. Josh Jacobs was good in his return, but he dropped a pass in the end zone in the fourth quarter. Trey Smack missed two short field goals, one that was partially blocked right after Jacobs' drop. Matt LaFleur passed on a field goal to go for it on fourth-and-4 in the first half. Green Bay put up only 17 points on a bad Lions defense. And the officiating didn't help, either.”
Josh Kendall and Chad Graff dropped the Packers three spots in their rankings.
This week’s theme is something spooky, and they chose Green Bay’s NFL-worst rushing attack.
“Josh Jacobs returned to the lineup in a move that should have helped lift the league’s worst rushing attack (based on EPA per attempt). Instead, he managed just 36 yards on 11 carries. Jacobs was better in the passing game (five receptions for 55 yards and a touchdown), but it’s tough to run an offense without a respectable rushing attack.”
Instead of inching up close to the top 10 , Ralph Vacchiano backed the Packers up four spots in his rankings.
“The Packers were a couple of missed kicks away from beating the Lions … but they just couldn’t make the big stop or the big offensive play when it mattered most. QB Jordan Love is still playing well, and he’s got RB Josh Jacobs back now to boost their rushing attack. And their defense is playing sneaky good too. So, the Pack has it all … except that they’re 4-3 and that puts them in last place in their tough division. So, they remain in the middle of the pack for now.”
The Panthers are 19th in the Consensus, with individual rankings ranging from 16th to 22nd. They plunged from 18th to 13th in Frank Schwab’s rankings at Yahoo.
“Every team is allowed a mulligan or two over a long season, but what happened Sunday was atrocious from the Panthers,” he wrote. “They trailed 43-6 at home to a Buccaneers team that had just one win beforehand. Carolina turned it over four times. It even had an extra point blocked and returned for 2 points. Bryce Young had by far his worst game of the season.”
Schwab pointed to Carolina’s horrendous run defense. Well, can the Packers take advantage?
Sportsbook odds aren’t part of our rankings, but they do provide one more perspective on the state of the league. In Packers-related odds at FanDuel Sportsbook :
The Packers, who were +2000 to win the Super Bowl before Week 1, plunged to as low as +6000. They rebounded to +3000 with their three consecutive wins, but fell back to +3500 after losing to Detroit. While the odds changed since last week, they remain 15th on the board.
Among NFC North teams, the Bears are +1400, the Lions are +1700 and the Vikings +1800.
Green Bay opened the season ranked seventh in the NFC playoff odds at -112, fell to as low as 12th at +250 after the win at Tampa Bay, rebounded back to -118 with their winning streak but fell to +126 after losing to Detroit. That is eighth on the board and last among the NFC North teams (Minnesota is -520, Detroit is -270 and Chicago is -255).
Quarterback Jordan Love is rising fast in the MVP race. He opened at +2200 but bottomed out at +10000. He rose to +3300 after their three-game winning streak and moved to +2500 after the Detroit game. That’s tied with Jared Goff for eighth on the board. Buffalo’s Josh Allen (+150) is the heavy favorite.
The Packers are last in the NFC North standings and far back in the back in the division odds at DraftKings. Minnesota is -105, followed by Detroit at +300, Chicago at +315 and Green Bay at +1125.

title: Sean Rhyan Injury Update, John Williams’ Opportunity and Packers Roster Move
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – John Williams went from the end of the bench to front and center for the Green Bay Packers in the blink of an eye.
Williams, a seventh-round pick in 2025, hadn’t played a single snap on offense in his career. Until Sunday. With starting center Sean Rhyan and backup Jacob Monk injured within the first 10 plays, Williams wound up playing 58 snaps against the Detroit Lions on Sunday.
The job, presumably, is his now.
Rhyan suffered a high-ankle sprain during the opening series against Detroit when running back Josh Jacobs was tackled and fell into the back of Rhyan’s leg. He will miss “at least” the next four games, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz.
Testing has confirmed that #Packers center Sean Rhyan has a high ankle sprain that will likely sideline him at least a month, sources tell @CBSSports . Not currently expected to undergo tightrope surgery but currently viewed as likely that he’ll miss at least four weeks. pic.twitter.com/P8mqaYnajh
With Monk suffering an injured quad during that same series and landing on injured reserve on Monday, Williams could be the team’s starting center for the next month. The other option is rookie Jager Burton, who was inactive for the third consecutive game.
With Monk on IR, the Packers promoted Mekhi Becton from the practice squad. The 11th pick of the 2020 draft, he had started 59 games during his first six seasons. The Packers signed him after the Week 3 disaster against Atlanta . He spent the past few weeks working at right guard and right tackle while getting acclimated after offseason surgery.
“Got a lot of confidence with what he’s been able to display on the practice field. So, 100 percent,” coach Matt LaFleur said recently.
Becton is an enormous individual at 6-foot-7 and 357 pounds. He was a first-round bust with the Jets, where he played left tackle, but his career changed when the Eagles placed him at right guard in 2024. That’s where he played for the Chargers last season.
“Mekhi is a big guy; big physical guy,” said Packers left guard Laken Tomlinson, who played with the Jets in 2022 and 2023. “He’s a people-mover. I played with him with the Jets. He’s a physical freak. Definitely excited to have him on the squad.”
Including Rhyan, the Packers have 11 offensive linemen on their roster.
The projected starting five after training camp consisted of left tackle Jordan Morgan, left guard Aaron Banks, Rhyan, right guard Jacob Monk and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele. For most of the game against Detroit, only Morgan was on the field.
Williams was an excellent left tackle at Cincinnati. The Packers drafted him in the seventh round last year, but he missed his entire rookie season following back surgery aside from three weeks of practice late in the season.
This year, he spent the offseason practices and the start of training camp at center before bouncing out to left tackle. In fact, all 93 preseason snaps came at left tackle.
However, with Rhyan and Monk injured and Burton inactive, Williams was thrown into the fire at Detroit, where he was challenged by a strong defensive line and incredible noise. PFF charged him with one pressure allowed on 43 pass-protecting snaps.
“I can’t say enough about the job John Williams did, coming in in a hostile environment and just handling the operation, the communication,” coach Matt LaFleur said after the game. “To lose two guys at center that quickly in the game, it was a little bit terrifying, but I thought he did a really good job.”
Williams majored an aerospace engineering , so his ability to handle the mental aspects of the game are not in question.
“He’s so intelligent. He’s got great command, understands all the calls, why we’re doing what we’re doing,” LaFleur said. “Again, I commend him for the job he did stepping in a tough situation.”
After the game, quarterback Jordan Love laughed when asked if he’s ever taken snaps with Williams. After all, Love is the starting quarterback and Williams was an end-of-the-depth-chart player.
“Not much,” he said. “I think it’s one of those things where we always talk about that next-man-up mentality. Early on, losing Sean and losing Monk, I think John did a great job being able to step up. He hasn’t taken many reps at center, let alone with the ones.
“I think for him, that’s just a great job of being ready, being able to come in, be able to make these calls in a position where he hasn’t played too much. We talk about it all the time – that next-man-up mentality – but I think he did a great job tonight, and it’s going to be another short week for him to get ready. We’ll see what those guys’ status is. It’s a tough situation losing two guys early, but I think John did a great job.”

title: Latest NFC Playoff Standings, Projections Are Double-Whammy for Packers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers are in last place in the NFC North but are clinging to a spot in the NFC playoff field following their loss to the Detroit Lions.
With a 4-3 record, the Packers are in seventh place in the NFC. If the season were to end today, they would be – you guessed it – the No. 7 seeds. That was their spot in the playoff field each of the last three seasons.
Making matters worse, their first-round opponent would be the 49ers, who knocked the Packers out of the playoffs in 2019, 2021 and 2023.
Here’s where things stand, along with the latest playoff projections.
The Packers are in seventh place in the NFC. They have the same record as the Seahawks but have a better conference record.
Talking about the state of the team, quarterback Jordan Love said after Sunday’s game:
“Man, I just think looking at tonight, just taking today into consideration, not good enough. I still think there’s so much more out there for us as a football team in every area.
“I think just looking at the offense, we’ve made some strides. There’s still a lot of plays out there where we can really be dominant, but we’ve got to be able to come out here and finish these drives, put up points and just execute at a higher level. I still think there’s a lot out there for us.”
The Packers are one game ahead of the Falcons, Rams and Cowboys. The Packers lost to Atlanta, beat Dallas and will play Los Angeles.
2. San Francisco 49ers, 6-1
12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 2-5
13. New Orleans Saints, 2-5
14. Arizona Cardinals, 2-5
15. Philadelphia Eagles, 2-5
16. Washington Commanders, 1-4-1
Here are the Packers’ playoff chances, according to various playoff simulators. Their playoff hopes took a significant hit following Sunday’s loss to the Lions.
Using The Athletic’s playoff simulator , the Packers have a 40 percent chance of qualifying for the playoffs. It was 53 percent before the game. Their NFC North odds are only 5 percent with a less than 1 percent chance of winning the Super Bowl.
Their playoff chances would bounce back to 48 percent with a victory over NFC South-leading Carolina on Thursday night.
At NFL.com , the Packers have a 42 percent chance of reaching the postseason, down from 54 percent last week. That ranks ninth in the NFC, with Seattle and Dallas ahead of the Packers even while behind them in the standings.
At Playoff Status , the Packers have a 50 percent chance of reaching the playoffs, with about a 4 percent chance of doing it as the NFC North champions. They had a 61 percent chance at this time last week.
With a win over Carolina, their playoff chances would improve to 56 percent. With a loss, they’d fall to 40 percent.
At ESPN , the Packers have a 41 percent chance of earning a playoff berth, down sharply from 56 percent last week. They have a 5 percent chance of winning the NFC North.
The Packers have a 65 percent chance of beating the Panthers, according to ESPN. It’s a big game; their playoff chances would improve to 49 percent with a win but plunge to 27 percent with a loss.
At Stick to the Model , Green Bay’s playoff chances are merely 37 percent. They were at 49 percent before the Detroit game.
With a win, they’d bounce back to 45 percent; with a loss, they’d plummet to 23 percent.
In the latest playoff odds at FanDuel Sportsbook , the Packers are eighth at +126. They are behind the 49ers, Vikings, Lions, Bears, Seahawks, Rams and Cowboys.
“It is what it is. You got to learn from it and move on,” coach Matt LaFleur said after the game. “You know, we’re going to have a team that I’m sure is gonna be pretty ticked off in their own right coming into Lambeau, and it’s going to be the team that can bounce back the best.”
The Packers are 3.5-point favorites against Carolina, for what it’s worth.
The Packers’ remaining opponents have a .538 winning percentage this season, according to Tankathon . That’s the eighth-toughest remaining strength of schedule, which is the bad news. The good news is the Vikings rank first, the Bears third and the Lions fourth due to the bruising NFC North gauntlet.
Green Bay’s remaining 10 games come against four teams with losing records: the Dolphins, Saints, Texans and Rams.
“Just get back to the drawing board, obviously, refocus, regroup and put all of our focus in getting our bodies back in preparing for Carolina,” quarterback Jordan Love said.

title: Latest Roughing-the-Passer Penalties Hit Comical, Crisis Levels for Packers
full_text:
DETROIT – With about 4 minutes to go in the third quarter on Sunday against the Lions, Green Bay Packers edge player Brenton Cox was flagged for roughing the passer.
And, in retrospect, comical in that dark humor sort of way.
Late in the play, Cox fought his way past Cade Mays. In a last-ditch effort to keep Cox away from his quarterback, Mays tried to push Cox past Jared Goff. Cox hit Goff with two hands in the midsection. Goff tipped over like Humpty Dumpty – Cox appeared to try to grab Goff to keep him upright – and a flag was thrown.
Brenton Cox Jr. Gets Called For Roughing The Passer. This Might Be The Most Ridiculous One I've Ever Seen, And That's After Last Week's Multiple Roughing The Passer Calls That Were Definitely Questionable. This One Is The Worst Of Them All. I Never Want To Call Something… pic.twitter.com/gEkQI1l2Ki
“I was trying” to hold up, Cox said. “But it’s like it’s a superstar quarterback. I’m trying to make a name for myself and they’re going to call it every time. I honestly felt the refs should know the difference between what’s intentional and what’s not, and what’s violent and what’s not. It’s a new game right now. You can’t get close.”
Goff’s third-and-10 pass fell incomplete, but Cox’s penalty gave the Lions a first down. They eventually drove to the Packers’ 6-yard line, where the drive stalled. So, while the penalty didn’t give the Lions points, it did bury the Packers in horrible field position.
Then, late in the fourth quarter with the score tied at 17, Goff hit tight end Sam LaPorta for 18 yards. The moment Goff threw the pass, he was hit by Karl Brooks. Brooks didn’t hit him late. He didn’t land on him with body weight. He didn’t hit Goff in the head.
But the moment Goff hit the turf, he pointed to the referee and got rewarded. Another 15 yards was tacked on in a critical moment.
Tom Brady on the roughing the passer call on Karl Brooks: “My goodness, what is that? “There is no way” “It’s definitely not roughing the passer” #GoPackGo 🧀 pic.twitter.com/syzzBcOgno
“My goodness, what is that?” wondered Fox broadcaster Tom Brady. “It’s definitely not roughing the passer.”
The penalty moved the ball to Green Bay’s 40-yard line and helped set up the game-winning field goal.
“I don’t even want to comment on any of the penalties,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “It is what it is. You got to play above it. I thought there were some tough calls, but it is what it is.”
Those two penalties were part of a day that had the Packers crying foul – and worse – about the officiating.
Incredibly, the Packers have been flagged eight times for roughing the passer this season. That’s the most in the league, according to NFL Penalties . Carolina, Cleveland and Kansas City are next with four, so the Packers have double the second-ranked figure.
On the other hand, Jordan Love, who has faced the second-most pressures (according to Pro Football Focus) and been hit the third-most times (official stats), hasn’t drawn a single roughing penalty.
“It is what it is. Another one of those things, it’s out of my control,” Love said. “Just go out there, focus on doing my job, playing the game and let the calls be the calls. But, yeah, it is what it is.”
Apparently, Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon is coaching his team like it’s the 1970s Raiders while Love has faced seven consecutive games against choir boys and Boy Scouts.
Added together, the Packers are down 8-0 in roughing-the-passer penalties. That is equal to the next three teams combined: The Browns and Chiefs (minus-3) and the Seahawks (minus-2) are the only teams worse than minus-1.
“Yeah, definitely, we talk all the time,” Love said of conversations with the officials. “Especially if you feel like it might be a roughing, you talk to them, have those conversations, tell them to look out for it, and they communicate back.
“I saw the replays on the ones we got called on, you know, it’s tough. We always tell the defense, how can we be better? And we always talk about lowering the strike zone, focusing on not landing with body weight on the guys. So, I think it’s tough, and … yeah.”
NFL Penalties has data going back to the 2009 season, with its season numbers including the playoffs. Only three teams over those past 17 seasons finished with more roughing penalties than the Packers have been deemed guilty of in seven games season.
The Bears last season were guilty of nine roughing penalties and finished minus-6. The Jets in 2020 were guilty of 14 and finished minus-12. The Ravens were guilty of 11 in 2019 but were only minus-4.
So, the Packers are breaking trail, 15 yards at a time.
“It just be bulls**** that’s going on, bullshit calls, and I can’t really tell you because sometimes we’re not seeing the same calls for our quarterback, we’re not seeing the same calls for our offensive guys,” safety Xavier McKinney said. “I just don’t really understand. It really don’t matter if it’s home or way, it’s kind of been consistent throughout the year. Obviously, it’s not to make it as an excuse but I just say it got to go both ways, man.”
The eight roughing penalties have given Green Bay’s opponents 102 yards. That’s more penalty yards than eight teams have total on defense. The Vikings, whose blitzing, attacking defense is why they are the only undefeated team in the league, have been flagged only once for roughing.
Four players are tied for the NFL lead with two roughing penalties. Green Bay holds three of those spots with Lukas Van Ness, Brooks and Cox.
LaFleur was in no mood to complain. As he said last week , he just wants it officiated both ways. That 8-0 disparity is anything but both ways.
“I can say what I really think,” LaFleur said after the game, “but I don’t think it does any good. So, it is what it is. You just got to overcome it.”
