title: Chargers' Post-Bye Week NFL Mock Draft, 5-Round Edition
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are emerging from their Week 7 bye with an 0-6 record and a firm grasp on the number one overall pick now that the Miami Dolphins have won a game. Miami's win leaves the Chargers as the lone winless team remaining in the NFL.
The Chargers, as an organization, have questions to answer moving forward and towards the November 10th trade deadline. Will they continue to maintain a plan of standing pat or will they decide to sell off tradeable assets and look to the future?
The Chargers and Dolphins are the favorites to land the number one overall pick. The two teams play each other late in the season in a Week 16 matchup that could easily be the deciding factor based on the current outlook of the season. Right now the Chargers have the number one pick and let's run through that scenario in a mock draft.
It’s not just the 200 yards and 4 TDs for Jeremiah Smith — it’s wild routes like these, at 6-4, 220, that make him such a special prospect pic.twitter.com/gnlWb2S5nX https://t.co/TyT6YVz5W9
This is the easiest pick that the entire NFL world would make without hesitation. The Chargers need a top receiving option to get defenses to back off the line of scrimmage and give Justin Herbert a viable option to throw to.
Smith is a 6'3 222lb monster of a wide receiver who is generating lofty comparisons. The bottom line is Smith is one of the best wide receiver prospects we have seen in years. Smith owns several Ohio State school receiving records and stands out from a school that has sent a receiver to the NFL via the first round for five consecutive years and six total.
In the event the draft order changes, this draft class has several top wide receiver prospects who could help immediately but Smith stands alone at the top of the class.
Fastest College Football Players of Week 8 2️⃣ 21.8 mph - Zabien Brown ( @zabien_brown ) CB Alabama #ReelSpeed 🔗 https://t.co/wwII6ki7cm pic.twitter.com/VPJazVtcHr
The Chargers have a thin cornerback room and could use an addition. Zabien Brown is a great blend of size, speed and instincts. He is not perfect with his technique but his talent is undeniable. If any coaching staff can get the most out of him and turn him into the lockdown outside corner he is capable of being, the Chargers defensive staff can get him to shine.
John Henry Daley 2.7 second sack time! https://t.co/ZNIKwcuT7y pic.twitter.com/bjfmMrgEqW
In all likelihood, the Chargers will be moving forward without Khalil Mack. Tuli Tuipulotu and Akheem Mesidor will be the edge anchors and Los Angeles will need another edge rusher to fill out the room with the amount of three-edge-rusher looks they use.
John Henry Daley is cut from the same cloth as Tuipulotu and Mesidor, a high effort menace who is capable of rushing from the inside but can also win quickly. Having a high pick in each round gives the Chargers a chance at players like this.
#BYU LB Cade Uluave had 3 pressures on the final drive; was a big reason why #GoIrish QB was under duress down the stretch The physical tools aren't outstanding but he checks boxes. Can rush / cover / shoot gaps vs the run. Green Dot guy. Reminds me of Henry To'o To'o at Alabama pic.twitter.com/aJHnHyMc04
The Chargers' linebacker room is incredibly thin heading into 2027 with several veterans playing out 2026 on expiring contracts. Even if the Chargers re-sign Daiyan Henley, they will need to add to the room.
BYU's Cade Uluave has been on my radar for years going back to his freshman season at Cal. Scouts from the Chargers were a consistent presence at Cal over the past few seasons and have already visited BYU games twice in 2026. It may mean nothing but the scouts will have had eyes on him for a long time as well.
Uluave is a modern linebacker who can cover, blitz and tackle. He is also highly regarded for his leadership and football character.
Texas Tech DT AJ Holmes Jr. having 5 sacks in 6.5 games at 6-3, 300 is disgusting pic.twitter.com/2Kt1MVH20K
The Chargers will be lucky if A.J Holmes Jr. is available at the top of day 3. The defensive line room has been stacking strong talent in back to back drafts and is led by veteran menace Teair Tart. Holmes is one of the top rated interior rushers in the nation and brings extra juice as a rusher.
Will be monitor #Cincinnati LG Evan Tengesdahl throughout the rest of the season. Big, physical interior lineman who has the athleticism to cut off D-linemen on perimeter runs and powerful to create displacement and stonewall pass rushers. Pocket cleaner, never gets too… pic.twitter.com/WUecXr5Ki1
I fully expect the Chargers to spend money in free agency in an attempt to solve their interior offensive line woes. However, they will also need to add more depth. Cincinnati's Evan Tengesdahl is mean and powerful interior blocker but with good movement skills. He still has some work to do as a pass protector but is a solid player with a lot to work with.

title: Chargers Bottom Out in Power Rankings…But Top NFL Draft Order
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are the worst team in the NFL . It’s a budding idea that has been whispered for a few weeks now and got confirmation while they sat on bye and morphed into the NFL’s only winless team.
With even the hapless-looking Tennessee Titans winning a game, the Chargers are now dead last in power rankings at 0-6. Any rankings without them at No. 32, frankly, aren’t worth the time of day.
Chargers fans, at least, got a win while this happened . Those fans, who probably checked out after 0-4 and turned to offseason mode already, just got to watch as the Chargers took a firm, lonely grip on the No. 1 overall pick.
So there’s that, at least. Silver linings and stuff, right?
About those power rankings.
Sporting News’ Vinnie Iyer put it best while plopping the Chargers at No. 32: “The Chargers have been hit with a bolt of poor energy under Jim Harbaugh and come out of the bye as the league's sole winless team. They need to stop playing like 53 Frankensteins who were just hit by lightning.”
Speaking of “bolts” of energy, the Chargers were hit with anything but via the arrival of Mike McDaniel. He tweaked some of Herbert’s mechanics and remolded the personnel in free agency and the draft to miserable results so far.
That makes the updated NFL draft order pretty shaky:
Shaky, because the popular idea is the Chargers going after Ohio State wideout Jeremiah Smith in the top five.
Sounds fun. The Chargers have spent too much time on first-rounder Quentin Johnston and his drop issues while names like Ladd McConkey fight injury woes and others like Tre Harris have yet to emerge.
But will it be McDaniel scheming up Smith in his offense? Will Jim Harbaugh even still be around at this point?
And knowing NFL coverage, especially in the offseason, how often will analysis call for the Chargers to take a risk on quarterback and make a big trade with Herbert?
So it goes for a team sitting 32nd in the rankings and first in the draft order. If nothing else, every day should be pretty interesting for Chargers fans…once the season ends.

title: Joe Hortiz's Trade Deadline Plan Faces a Major Bye-Week Test
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers had their bye week in Week 7. The Chargers needed a bye to regroup and hope to get some reinforcements back from injury. The reality is the Chargers are at a crossroads: they have significant injuries , their offense is still searching for an identity and they are 0-6.
The Chargers are currently in line to land the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 draft. Following the Week 7 schedule, the Chargers now are the last winless team left in the NFL with the Dolphins taking down the New York Jets for their first win of the season.
The season is essentially over for Los Angeles but questions for the future loom large. Will new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel shake up the lineup find the best offensive strategy for the available personnel or will the offense continue to be a trainwreck?
The Chargers have two games remaining before the November 10th trade deadline. If McDaniel does not get the train back on the tracks, does he survive the season? If the Chargers do not make significant changes during the bye week and show a different on-field product against the Rams in week eight, does Joe Hortiz finally cave and engage in trade talks?
The current reports indicate the Chargers are holding off trade calls and as Jeremy Fowler put it, are "still giving the impression they are standing pat."
Temperature check on a few teams entering trade deadline: -Many in league getting impression Colts will wait 1-2 weeks before determining trade course. Rallying off a few wins could change perspective. But...they need picks, too. -Bucs still in NFC South hunt, but a loss…
If the plan from the Chargers front office is to stand pat and continue to try to save the season, perhaps not for 2026 but to find some continuity heading into 2027, that plan faces a massive test against the Rams next week. The Chargers, at best, could end up 2-6 heading into the trade deadline. However, if they drop to 0-7, Joe Hortiz's phone will likely be ringing non-stop.
Currently, betting markets have the Chargers and Dolphins in a tight race for the number one overall pick. Kalshi currently has the odds at 35 percent for the Dolphins and 31 percent for the Chargers. Typically, regimes do not survive a catastrophic season that leads to landing the top pick in the draft.
The deadline math for general manager Joe Hortiz and the Chargers' front office isn't as simple as buyers vs. sellers. They have to deal with a high-stakes balancing act with little margin for error. The front office could sell off tradeable assets to build for the future and net draft capital. The risk in selling is leaving your franchise quarterback, Justin Herbert, with even less to work with.
If Los Angeles continues to stand pat and hold the line, and they essentially will be burning future capital on a lost season. But, if they decide to go full fire-sale, does that symbolic waving the white flag put everyone's job further in jeopardy. John Spanos, President of Football Operations and son of Chargers owner Dean Spanos, will likely push the decision one way or the other.
Looking back to when the Chargers fired former general manager Tom Telesco and head coach Brandon Staley, John Spanos said in the days after, "My opinion is everything starts with ownership. Ultimately, we're responsible for everything. What we've been doing has not been good enough." What direction the Chargers go at the deadline may ultimately be out of Joe Hortiz's hands. If they fall to 0-7 the plan of standing pat may collapse.

title: Rams Shake Up Practice Squad, Sign Linebacker Jon Rhattigan to Address Special Teams Struggles
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams made a handful of roster moves on Tuesday, with the hope that their newest addition will help them on special teams . The Rams signed linebacker Jon Rhattigan to their practice squad and terminated the contracts of cornerback Nyzier Fourqurean and linebacker Eli Neal.
Over the first seven weeks of the season, the Rams have been trying to figure out how to improve on special teams. Against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Rams gave up a 36-yard kickoff return and then a 42-yard kickoff return before opting to just kick the ball out of the back of the end zone.
“It was not good enough. We've talked about this a lot and it has to get fixed. It's not good enough and we cannot allow ourselves to do that,” said head coach Sean McVay. “I have to figure that out. It's one of those deals that’s driving me crazy. We have to figure it out and we haven't yet.”
It’s somewhat surprising that the Rams cut Neal after he’s been with the team for the last three years on and off the practice squad. Neal had been active in two games this year, but not since Week 3. The Rams will hope that Rhattigan can help their issues on the coverage unit.
Rhattigan was an undrafted free agent out of Army in 2021 and spent three seasons with the Seattle Seahawks. He was with the Bears this summer but was released during roster cuts. Rhattigan has played 1,270 special teams snaps in his career. In 2022 with the Seahawks, he had a 90.1 special teams grade via PFF. Last season, Rhattigan had 2 tackles on special teams, but was credited with six missed tackles.
The Rams signing Rhattigan is another sign that they are continuing to bring in players to try and fix their issues on special teams. This is likely something that the Rams will have to address in the offseason, but McVay understands it’s a problem and they are doing what they can at this point.
Also among the roster cuts was Fourqurean. This offseason, the Rams signed a pair of undrafted cornerbacks in Fourqurean and Al’Zillion Hamilton. Hamilton was part of the first roster cutdowns and was not brought back on the practice squad. Fourqurean has now been cut as well after performing well in the preseason. It is worth noting that the Rams signed cornerback Damarion Williams two weeks ago, and Williams may have surpassed Fourqurean on the depth chart.
As another note on the transaction wire, the Rams also had long snapper Jake McQuaide in for a visit. Earlier this offseason, the Rams signed Joe Cardona to be their long snapper, so McQuaide coming in for a visit is certainly interesting. McQuaide spent his first 10 years with the Rams and was brought back last year after the team cut Alex Ward.
It's clear that the Rams aren't satisfied with how things have gone on special teams, and Tuesday's roster moves are another example of their efforts to address those issues. Rhattigan may provide some help on the coverage unit, but it remains to be seen how much of an impact he’ll have.

title: Blake Corum Is the Key to the Rams Turning Their Season Around and Making a Playoff Run
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams lost to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6, it was rock bottom . The offense scored 16 points against a struggling Cardinals defense, and the Rams fell at home to the bottom-dweller of the NFC West
On Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Rams leaned on Blake Corum to spark the offense along with Kyren Williams and a steady run game. Corum and Williams combined for 192 yards rushing as the offense found its identity . They became the first running back duo since Marshall Faulk and Trung Candidate to each rush for over 90 yards in the same regular season game.
Throughout the McVay era, there have been times when the offense has gone through ruts. In 2018, the Rams lost two out of three games and didn’t look like themselves during that stretch. During the 2021 season, the Rams went through “No win November” and Stafford was plagued with turnovers. The offense turned the ball over seven times across three games.
In every case, the Rams simply got back to what they did best. The foundation of the McVay offense is built around the run game.
“Any good offense that we've had here that I've been a part of, you have to be able to do both,” said head coach Sean McVay after the game. “You have to be able to have balance, or you at least have to have the threat of if they overcommit to something, then you have to be able to make them pay.”
During Weeks 16 and 17 in 2018, C.J. Anderson had 43 carries for 299 yards. In the playoffs, the Rams beat the Cowboys on the back of Anderson and Todd Gurley rushing 39 times for 238 yards and three touchdowns.
When the Rams went through 'No Win November,' they leaned on Sony Michel after struggling to find consistency in the run game all year. Michel had 20 carries in Week 3 of the 2021 season. He didn’t have another game with 20 or more carries until Week 13.
Between Week 13 and 18, Michel had a league-high 129 carries and rushed for 540 yards, which ranked third. During that span, the Rams had just a +3.2 pass rate over expected compared to +5.5 during the losing streak.
With Williams on injured reserve in 2023, the Rams went 1-3 and fell to 4-6. Once Williams came back, he had 20 carries in five of the next six games, including 25 or more in Weeks 14 and 15 as the Rams went 5-1.
From Weeks 12-17, Williams ranked second in EPA per rush and led the NFL in rushing success rate. Williams had the most rushing attempts and yards during that span as well. The Rams had a +1.3 pass rate over expected over those six games.
That’s what the Rams needed to get back to last week. They needed to simplify things on offense. During the first six weeks of the season, Stafford led the NFL in passing attempts. The Rams ranked fifth in pass-rate over expected at +4.9 and it was at +7.7 between Weeks 3-6. In Week 7, the Rams had a +0.8 pass rate over expected. They were much more balanced .
“When you're able to do that, you're not in a bunch of bad spots on second down and on third down and a lot of things can come off of that,” McVay said. “I thought that was the first game that was reflected. We were able to really do some of the things that I've been in alignment with when we've been able to operate at a pretty decent clip offensively.”
While the Rams have a steady rushing attack with Kyren Williams, it lacks a creative dimension when he’s the only player involved. After Corum and Williams split carries in Week 2 against the New York Giants, the running game lacked that 1-2 punch.
Kyren Williams and Blake Corum's rushing charts shows exactly why they work well together. A lot more green/consistency from Williams, but Corum brings big-play ability. The answer to a dominant Rams' run game is using both in a 50-50 split. pic.twitter.com/TFVhtWlDac
From Weeks 2-6, Williams had 57 carries to Corum’s 25. Week 2 was also the last time that Corum had more than 10 carries in a game. On Sunday against the Raiders , Corum led the Rams with 17 carries to Williams’ 16. Again, they combined for 192 yards. Corum finished with 93 yards but had potential for more, as he had two touchdowns, including one from 43 yards, called back because of penalties.
“I thought he saw the holes well. I thought he pressed the line of scrimmage. It's a bummer the one long one came back. You see the explosiveness, though,” McVay said after the game. “It's something that we have to build on because this is a long journey. I thought this was a good step in the right direction, and you could feel that throughout the course of the week by the way the guys approached it.”
Over the last two seasons, when Williams and Corum each have 10 or more carries, the Rams average 0.03 EPA per rush with a 50.6 percent rushing success rate. When Williams has 10 or more carries and Corum does not, they average -0.07 EPA per rush with a 46.1 percent rushing success rate.
The best version of the Rams’ rushing attack is one that includes a heavy dose of Corum alongside Williams. Both players complement each other well, as Williams helps keep the offense on track while Corum has more burst and big-play ability.
Blake Corum: really good at football pic.twitter.com/NH2qHvjL4D
Getting Corum more involved and McVay committing to the run game are what will get the Rams back on track and back to the team that many expected coming into the season. In past years, the Rams have leaned on Stafford. However, they don’t need Stafford throwing 40 times per game when they have Corum and Williams.
The Rams have two running backs capable of making an impact, but that advantage means very little if only one is consistently involved. If the Rams are going to build on their win against the Raiders and turn their season around, Corum needs to remain a focal point of the offense.

title: Rams Face Mounting Trade Deadline Pressure as NFC West Rivals Make Major Moves
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams may have changed the course of their season with a win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, but they still have work to do to remain competitive. The NFC West remains one of the more competitive divisions in the NFL. With the Seattle Seahawks trading for All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson , and the San Francisco 49ers acquiring DeForest Buckner, the pressure is on for the Rams to make a corresponding move if they want to remain competitive with the Seahawks and 49ers.
While the 49ers may be the favorites to win the division, the battle for second place and a wild card spot in the playoffs is up for grabs. After the Seahawks beat the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football, it’s clear they believe they are in position to push for that spot and do what they can to try and repeat.
The Seahawks making this type of move at 4-3 is a testament to how competitive the NFC West is as a division. Since the beginning of 2025, the Seahawks are 22-3 when Anthony Bradford starts at guard. Bradford has helped activate some of the things they do in the run game and allowed them to be more balanced on offense. Adding Nelson allows the Seahawks to be dominant in the run game and keep the interior clean for quarterback Sam Darnold.
Despite the 49ers leading the division, they responded with a move of their own with Buckner. Buckner gives the 49ers a dominant run-stopping defensive lineman that they've been lacking. It keeps them firmly ahead in the NFC West.
While the 49ers lead the group, the Rams and Seahawks will be competing very closely for a final wild card spot, especially with how strong the NFC North is currently. Between the Rams, Seahawks, and 49ers, all three are consistently looking to improve and seek out ways they can one-up the other. There are only three playoff spots available and five teams competing for those spots.
While the Rams made moves for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie earlier in the summer, Garrett has yet to play and McDuffie has missed each of the last two games. Simply sticking with the status quo may not be enough to make a legitimate push for one of those playoff spots, especially with the Seahawks pushing more of their chips into the middle of the table.
At the end of the day, this is still a Rams roster with its flaws. With the injury to Davante Adams, the Rams have a need for a wide receiver. Even if Adams comes back, the Rams need an upgrade at their third wide receiver spot over Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield. If the Rams don’t make a move there, it could come back to haunt them in the same way that ignoring the cornerback position did last season.
Additionally, the Rams could use a defensive tackle as well. Poona Ford is out for the season and Kobie Turner is on injured reserve. The Rams have depth on the defensive line, but it’s hard to promote some of that depth into a full-time role and expect to get the same production for half a season.
The Rams have options here to explore with Brian Thomas Jr., Josh Downs, and others. It simply comes down to how big of a move the Rams want to make and what they feel like they can afford. Les Snead doesn’t necessarily need to make a blockbuster move, but the Rams do need to be aggressive and show they aren’t waving the white flag on this season despite some of the injuries.
This isn’t necessarily about the Rams making a trade simply because the Seahawks did. However, the Seahawks’ willingness to give up draft capital to improve their roster should still increase the urgency for the Rams to do the same. The Rams have already invested heavily in competing for a Super Bowl this season, and can’t afford to fall further behind while a division rival looks to do the same.
Last season, the Rams lost an opportunity to compete for a Super Bowl because they lost to the Seahawks when it mattered. At that time, it was the Seahawks making a move for Rashid Shaheed that helped push them over the edge. It was Shaheed that sparked the comeback in Week 16 with his punt return for a touchdown. The Rams can’t afford to stand pat and watch a division rival surpass them again in a season when they were supposed to compete for a Super Bowl.
It’s true that the Rams will get healthier. Garrett is nearing a return, McDuffie could be back this week, and Terrance Ferguson should be back soon as well. However, the Rams can’t treat those players coming back as midseason additions. The Seahawks have made their move. With the Rams' Super Bowl hopes still hanging in the balance, it's time for Snead to make his.

title: Rams Trade Deadline Big Board: Realistic Targets Ranked by Fit and Cost
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams needed to beat the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday to warrant making any move before the trade deadline. Had the Rams dropped to 2-5, an argument can be made that the Rams should have considered moving on from players they didn’t plan on re-signing. However, with the win, the Rams are right back in the hunt.
If the Rams were to make a trade, making a move for a wide receiver appears to be the most realistic. However, given some injuries at other positions, the Rams will likely keep their options open. They could trade for a defensive lineman if the right opportunity came up. As Max Klare redshirts during his rookie season, a tight end may not be out of the question either.
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline getting closer. Here are a few names to track on our Rams trade deadline big board.
The Fit: Brian Thomas Jr. has been a popular name floating around Rams trade circles . Thomas put up 1,282 yards as a rookie and 10 touchdowns, but only has 812 yards in the 20 games since. There’s no question that Thomas would fit a need at wide receiver as the Rams are without Davante Adams for the next 6-8 weeks. While Thomas would slide right into the Rams’ “X” wide receiver role, it’s fair to wonder where he would fit once Adams does return. Both players fill a similar role on offense. As much as Thomas would be a trade for the future, they also need a player who can provide consistent production as they chase a Super Bowl title.
The Cost: The most realistic price for Thomas is a second-round pick. That’s what the Houston Texans gave up for Marvin Harrison Jr. a few weeks ago, and Thomas has been more productive. The Rams also gave up a second-round pick for Sammy Watkins when they traded for him in 2017.It’s possible the Jaguars get desperate to move off of Thomas and view trading him to an NFC team as a more attractive option. If that’s the case, the Rams may be able to acquire Thomas for the equivalent of a third-round pick. Thomas would cost the Rams around $656,000 for the remainder of the season.
The Fit: If there is a wide receiver available who would be a perfect fit in the Rams’ offense, it’s Josh Downs . Outside of Puka Nacua, the Rams don’t have a wide receiver who can consistently create explosive plays. They are also lacking a reliable option on third down. Downs is a player who could contribute immediately, but also fit into the offense once Davante Adams comes back. He’s a good separator with the ability to beat man coverage. Downs is a smaller wide receiver and built more like Zay Flowers than Tutu Atwell. While he can win vertically, it’s also not his specialty. He’s much more productive in the intermediate area of the field.
Watch Josh Downs slot left here. 3rd down in the red zone, Chiefs rush 7 and man up behind. Solution: run quick hitters and get open fast. Downs COOKS Sneed off the line, and a better ball from Jones makes this a TD. #49ers pic.twitter.com/31xTOk9vJn
The Cost: Downs is on the last year of his rookie deal and could be available given that the Colts are at 2-5 and just fired their general manager. He fits much more in the Austin Corbett and Kevin Dotson tier of trade than a splashy move for a star player. With that said, Downs could be available for a fourth-round pick. If he doesn’t re-sign in the offseason, the Rams could potentially get a compensatory pick in return. He also only costs $2.4 million for the remainder of the year.
The Fit: The Rams should get Kobie Turner back within the next four to six weeks. Still, Poona Ford played an important role for the Rams’ defense and is out for the season. Ojomo is a run-stuffing defensive lineman with pass rush upside. He would fit right in next to Aaron Donald, Braden Fiske, and Kobie Turner and fit an immediate need.
Eagles DT Moro Ojomo with one of the best plays of the week to seal the game for the Eagles on the two-point conversion attempt. Jalen Carter gets popped, but Ojomo reads it perfectly and saves the game for Philly pic.twitter.com/d6cGHhKjBR
The Cost: Howie Roseman hasn’t been afraid to move on from players in lost seasons. Ojomo is likely going to earn a $100 million contract in free agency and that’s not a player the Eagles will be able to afford . It’s very possible that a fifth-round pick and a conditional fourth could get the deal done.
The Fit: Since the offseason, Vita Vea is a player who has been on the trade block. Vea asked for a trade back in July when negotiations on a long-term extension stalled. With Ford out for the season, the Rams could use a run-stopping defensive lineman and Vea fits that role perfectly. It may not be a flashy move, but as stopping the run gets more important in December, Vea could be the difference-maker the Rams need later in the season.
The Cost: Vea is not going to come cheap, but with the Buccaneers at 2-5, they could look to move on from an aging player in the last year of his contract. It’s likely they’ll ask for a third-round pick. While the Rams don’t have that in 2027, they could offer a Day 3 pick this year and a third-round pick in 2028. Vea would cost the Rams $1.4 million for the remainder of 2026.
The Fit: If the Rams make a trade, wide receiver seems like the most realistic position they would target. They need a reliable third wide receiver and an upgrade over Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell. It’s hard to see the Vikings trading away a player as they sit at 6-0, but Jennings has just four receptions on the year. He’s not a standard “X”, but fits into the offense when Adams returns. The Cost: Jennings is 29 and only has four receptions for 43 yards this season. If the Rams are looking for a low-value trade, Jennings makes a lot of sense. He could be had for a Day 3 pick swap and only has a cap hit of $2.2 million.
The Fit: Is it crazy to think that the Rams would consider trading for a kicker? Blake Grupe spent time with the Colts last season before the Rams signed him off the Jets’ practice squad. If the Colts can get value for their kicker, it might be something they consider. Trading for a kicker is rare, but the Rams’ special teams unit is just that bad.
The Cost: The Colts aren’t simply going to give their kicker away. Shrader is 19-for-21 on field goals this season and 6-for-7 on kicks of 50 or more yards. Would the Colts do it for a fifth-round pick? That’s a trade that ESPN’s Bill Barnwell suggested last week .
The Fit: It seems almost insane that the Rams would consider trading for a tight end. With that said, Terrance Ferguson has been hurt and Colby Parkinson has managed injuries all season as well. Given Max Klare was inactive and a healthy scratch last week, it’s clear he isn’t ready to contribute yet. Sanders also gives the Rams a potential long-term option at the position, with several of their tight ends set to hit free agency this offseason.
The Cost: Sanders wouldn’t cost the Rams more than a Day 3 pick and would count for just $656,000 against the cap this year. He’s a player the Rams could afford. It may not be a splashy move, but it also allows the Rams to continue leaning into 13 personnel.
The Fit: Again, wide receiver is going to be a position the Rams target heavily on the trade market. They are going to weigh their options. Jerry Jeudy and Calvin Ridley are both veteran options at the wide receiver position who could fit into that “X” role. Jeudy is slightly more versatile, which matters when Adams returns. However, with KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston emerging in Cleveland and the Titans at 1-6, both teams could look to move off of those two aging players.
The Cost: Jeudy has a very difficult contract to acquire. He would only cost $916,000 this season, but he has a $23 million cap in 2027, and because of his void years, it doesn’t make him easy to cut. Ridley is similar as well. title: Week 8 Consensus NFL Power Rankings: Rams Are Back on the Rise, but Doubts Remain
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams defeated the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, 35-21 . After dropping in the consensus power rankings last week, the Rams are climbing back up. They may not be back inside the top 10 yet, but if they can start to stack wins together, it won’t be long before they are back there.
Until the Rams can prove they can win consecutive games and play consistently week to week, it’s going to be hard to trust what they can do. However, after rushing for 192 yards against the Raiders, it’s hard not to like what we saw. They seem to be a team with an identity again.
Oh my goodness the Bengals' remaining schedule pic.twitter.com/f7Mp0meoWr
Last week, the Rams looked like they had hit rock bottom. With the win against the Raiders, it looked like they may have turned their season around. Let’s jump into this week’s consensus power rankings.
The Rams move up two places in ESPN’s power rankings this week . They haven’t quite earned enough confidence from analysts to get back into the top 10, but it’s hard not to like what we saw against the Raiders. If the Rams can continue to play like they did on Sunday, they’ll start to earn some trust back and move back up the rankings.
Arguably the most impressive part about the Rams’ win against the Raiders was how they ran the ball. While the Raiders don’t have a stout run defense, the Rams still operated the offense through their dynamic rushing duo of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. If the Rams are going to start to turn it around, that’s a gameplan they’ll need to stick to.
“There’s absolutely another gear from Blake Corum that we haven’t seen,” said Sports Illustrated’s Connor Orr . “And while it’s not the Sean McVay hidden weapon we’re waiting to see, it’s absolutely going to matter in January.”
After last week’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals, the Rams were close to dropping outside of the top 20 in The Athletic’s power rankings. Now, they’re back inside the top 15. Nothing is guaranteed with this Rams team, but they still have an opportunity to turn their season around. With games against the Chargers, Commanders, and Cardinals on deck, the Rams have a chance to go into their bye week at 6-4. If that’s where the Rams stand as they start to get healthy, they won’t be a team others want to play come December and January.
“Don’t look now, but the Rams could easily put together a four-game winning streak without batting an eyelash,” wrote The Athletic . “After dispatching the Raiders on Sunday, their next three games are against the Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals, who have a combined record of 3-15-1. There is plenty of time for the Rams to turn their season around.”
Nick Shook remains the lowest analyst on the Rams , but that’s not to say it isn’t fair. The Rams haven’t shown the ability to be consistent week to week. If the Rams can play like they did on Sunday over the next month, it will be easier to feel good about them going into December as they get healthy and fight for a playoff spot.
“Some might say this is too low for the Rams, but I’d like to remind everyone of where they stood after the Week 6 loss to the Cardinals. Their coach openly admitted they lacked an identity and were coming off an indefensible defeat that included a barrage of new injuries,” wrote Shook. “It was a much-needed bounce-back performance, but it’s not enough to convince me all of their issues are magically fixed.”
The key to the Rams finding their identity on Sunday against the Raiders was leaning into the run game . Corum and Williams combined for 192 yards. They were the first Rams running back duo since 2001 to have more than 90 yards rushing in the same game.
“If they can keep running the ball the way they did on Sunday, they can start stacking wins,” wrote Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio .
When the Rams lost their offensive identity in 2021, they leaned on Sony Michel to get out of their rut. If the Rams are going to be the team that many expected, it starts with remaining committed to the run game.
Following last week’s loss, it seemed as if everyone had lost faith in the Rams, and it was hard to blame them. However, getting back in the win column with their most complete win to date, they are the drug that you just can’t quit. The Rams moved up to No. 12 from No. 16 in Fox Sports’ rankings and could keep moving up.
“Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in,” wrote Ralph Vacchiano . “It wasn’t just because of their win over the Raiders on Sunday. It was the way they raced out to a 28-3 lead, with some outstanding passing by QB Matthew Stafford and a strong, two-pronged rushing attack from Kyren Williams and Blake Corum.”
For the first time this season, the Rams looked like the team that many expected coming into the year. That’s not to say that they played a perfect game, but they were a team with an actual identity. After Matthew Stafford led the NFL in passing attempts going into Week 7, the Rams had more rushing attempts than passing attempts. That may not happen every week, but it’s a game plan they need to stick with.
“The team we saw beat up the Raiders is the Dream Team we expected to see before the season. The run game is back,” wrote Pete Prisco .
The Chargers are the only winless team remaining in the NFL and are dead last in the consensus power rankings. That’s a good thing for the Rams, who are looking to get a second consecutive win for the first time this season. However, the Chargers are also coming off a bye week.
Heading into the bye week, the Chargers had enough problems that they likely would have needed an entire month off to figure it all out, and even then it might not have been enough. With that said, the Rams can’t afford to overlook them like they did the Cardinals last week.
There is only one undefeated team remaining in the NFL through seven weeks. It may be harsh to only have them at six, but the Vikings have their flaws. If they can get out of this tough stretch of their schedule and look good, I can feel confident putting them in the top five.
With Caleb Williams, the Bears look like one of the best teams in the NFL, but still have a lot to prove. All eyes will be on their game on Monday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks.

title: Rams Remain Noncommittal on Myles Garrett's Return to Practice Ahead of Week 8
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams remain hopeful that edge rusher Myles Garrett will return to practice sooner rather than later . As the Rams prepare for their Week 8 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers, Garrett is nearing a potential return. While the Rams haven’t established an official timeline, outside reports have consistently pointed to a six-week recovery.
After missing the Rams’ game against the Las Vegas Raiders, Garrett has officially missed six games and is now just over six weeks removed from knee surgery. A six-week timeline was always seen as a worst-case scenario for Garrett, and he has now reached that point. Still, McVay remained mum on Garrett’s potential return to practice this week.
“I'm not sure yet. I have not decided on those things,” McVay said. “Once I get with Reggie and talk about the approach for the week. Then I will follow their guidance based on where he's at and how he's feeling.”
Late last week , NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported that Garrett was likely to return to practice this week and could play in Week 8. McVay even said on Friday that Garrett returning to practice next week was a possibility, but that he’d wait to talk to Garrett and the team’s training staff to come to a decision.
It’s no real surprise that the Rams remain coy on Garrett’s injury, as that’s how they’ve handled it since the beginning . Garrett was initially held out of practice late in training camp due to knee swelling. While he played in Week 1, Garrett didn’t feel like himself and was placed on injured reserve the following week.
Before Garrett returns, the Rams will want to be sure that he is fully healthy and ready to practice. They’ve waited this long and will want to ensure that Garrett is at 100 percent when he gets back on the field.
McVay is scheduled to speak to the media again on Wednesday. At that time, McVay may have more information about Garrett’s status. If Garrett isn’t practicing by Thursday, it seems unlikely that he’ll return this week. When the Rams designated Keagen Trost to return from injured reserve, they opened his 21-day window on the Thursday before the game.
If Garrett does return to practice and ends up playing this week, it would provide a huge boost to the defense. While the defense has played well, it has struggled to generate consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks. The Rams rank 27th in sack rate this season.
With Garrett now more than six weeks removed from surgery, the focus shifts to when he will be cleared to practice and how quickly he can get back on the field. At 3-4, the Rams are entering an important stretch of their season and could certainly use Garrett back in the lineup as they look to build on their win against the Raiders.

title: Rams Week 7 Snap Counts: Blake Corum's Rise Changes Running Back Outlook
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams had to manage several injuries on Sunday against the Raiders , which meant increased roles for a handful of players. Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell were asked to step up in place of Adams at wide receiver. Ty Hamilton made his presence felt without Kobie Turner. However, one of the bigger developments of the week was how the Rams rotated at running back. Blake Corum took a significantly larger share of the offensive snaps, raising questions about Kyren Williams’ role moving forward.
The big story out of Week 7 for the Rams was the increased usage of running back Blake Corum . That was the third-highest snap share of his career and the second-highest this season. Corum saw 45.2 percent of the offensive snaps back in Week 2. That was also the last time that Corum had more than 10 carries in a game.
Corum had 17 carries to Kyren Williams’ 16. However, prior to the final drive, Corum actually had 17 carries to Williams’ 11. The Rams had a very balanced rushing attack and found ways to get both players involved. We’ll have to see if the Rams can keep that type of usage between the two players moving forward.
Heading into Sunday’s game against the Raiders, there were major questions about who would step up in place of Davante Adams. The answer was simply nobody . Konata Mumpfield had one catch for 15 yards and played 43 percent of the snaps on offense. Behind him was Tutu Atwell, who played 35 percent of the snaps and wasn’t targeted once.
The Rams increased their usage of 13 personnel, lining up with three tight ends on 52.3 percent of their offensive snaps. Throughout the game, the Rams rotated Mumpfield and Atwell while Jordan Whittington was very clearly behind them. With the trade deadline coming up, the Rams need to seriously consider trading for a wide receiver.
Without Kobie Turner, the Rams needed to figure out how to replace him defensively. It wasn’t just one player. The Rams have depth on the defensive line, and they took advantage of it by increasing several players' roles. Aaron Donald saw 73.5 percent of the defensive snaps, which was his highest for the season. Tyler Davis saw more than 40 percent of the defensive snaps for the first time this year.
Ty Hamilton and Larrell Murchison also saw slight increases in their roles. The Rams will hope to get Turner back in a few weeks. The Raiders struggled along the interior of their offensive line, and the Rams will face tougher tests going forward. However, Sunday was still a positive for what that group can do in Turner’s absence.

title: Rams Player Grades: Running Game Leads the Way in Week 7 Win Over Raiders
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams got one of their most complete wins of the season , defeating the Las Vegas Raiders, 35-21. It was a team effort led by the running game and a strong defensive performance. Here are this week’s position grades based on their performance against the Raiders.
Matthew Stafford was very efficient against the Raiders . He didn’t need to do anything special and played within the offense. That’s exactly what was needed from him on Sunday. Stafford had a passing success rate of 63.3 percent, which led the NFL in Week 7. While the Rams’ quarterback still isn’t pushing the ball down the field, he finished with three touchdowns and became the franchise leader in touchdown passes.
The engine of the Rams’ offense on Sunday against the Raiders was the running game . They rushed 33 times for 192 yards and had a touchdown. Blake Corum and Kyren Williams became the first Rams running back duo since Marshall Faulk and Trung Candidate in 2001 to each have 90 rushing yards in the same game. Williams did have a fumble, which continues to be an issue. However, outside of the fumble, Williams and Corum were fantastic.
There continues to be a significant drop-off at wide receiver behind Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. With Adams out, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell rotated as the second wide receiver. Mumpfield had one catch for 15 yards while Atwell had nothing. If the Rams make a trade at the deadline, it needs to be for a wide receiver.
With the Rams missing Adams, they leaned on the tight ends in the passing game. Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, and Tyler Higbee combined for 12 receptions. Parkinson did have a pass go off of his hands that resulted in an interception. However, Allen had two touchdowns in the red zone.
The offensive line was very good against the Raiders. The success that Corum and Williams had in the running game was a testament to the offensive line winning in the trenches . Stafford was also kept clean. With Alaric Jackson back in the lineup, the offensive line played much closer to what we’re accustomed to seeing from that group.
Without Kobie Turner, the defensive line played well. While Kirk Cousins had time, the Rams still sacked him twice.Ty Hamilton had one of the best games of his career and made his presence felt against the run. The Rams had a 26.7 percent stuff rate on defense, which was the fourth-highest in the NFL. Aaron Donald still doesn’t have a sack, but his pressure on the two-point conversion led to a bad throw. This group stepped up despite being short-handed.
Despite not having Nate Landman, the Rams’ linebackers had their best game of the season. Omar Speights was great in a full-time role, and Shaun Dolac filled in nicely. Speights did have two missed tackles, but also had two tackles for loss. Dolac was almost perfect alongside Speights and there’s an argument that he deserves a more extended look.
Jaylen Watson allowed two catches on 10 targets and has settled in nicely in the Rams’ defense. If he can stay healthy, Watson and McDuffie are a great cornerback duo. It’s going to be very difficult to throw against this Rams team. Josh Wallace filled in nicely again, and Emmanuel Forbes had a key pass breakup on fourth down. Where the Rams have struggled is at safety and with their tackling angles. Jaylen McCollough was credited with three missed tackles on Sunday.
Brandon McManus made his debut for the Rams on Sunday, but wasn’t tested. He went a perfect 5-for-5 on extra points. The Rams also recovered a crucial onside kick to put the game away. However, the kickoff coverage unit remains a liability. Each of the first two kickoff returns went over 35 yards. It’s simply not good enough.

title: 10 Takeaways From Rams' Win Over Raiders: Blake Corum Sparks a Much-Needed Victory
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams beat the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, 35-21, to improve to 3-4 on the season. It was the type of win that the Rams needed after a disappointing loss last week. They seemed to find their identity, leading to a complete team win. There’s a lot to talk about after that one. Let’s jump into this week’s 10 takeaways.
The Rams continue having slow starts on offense. To start the game, the Rams went three-and-out after three consecutive passes. While they scored on their next four drives, the Rams haven’t scored an opening drive touchdown all season. The Rams also came out flat in the second half. Instead of extending the lead and picking up where they left off, the Rams again went three-and-out. The Rams should be able to find success with their scripted plays at the beginning of each half. They need to find a way to start faster in games.
It wouldn’t be a Rams football game if we didn’t talk about special teams. The Rams didn’t have any back-breaking mistakes, but the win can’t hide the mistakes that did happen. On the opening kickoff, the Rams allowed a 36-yard return. The next return went for 42 yards. Later in the game, the Rams touched a kickoff that should have been a touchback and got the ball at the 20 instead of the 35. The Raiders also had a successful fake punt. In games with tight margins, these are mistakes that matter. Those mistakes didn’t come back to hurt the Rams on Sunday, but there is still room for improvement.
Two of the Rams’ best games running the ball this season have been games in which Blake Corum was used consistently alongside Kyren Williams. The answer to the Rams’ running game isn’t one or the other. McVay needs to find ways to get both players into a rhythm. They combined for 33 carries for 192 yards against the Raiders. Corum led the Rams’ first touchdown drive and then had two touchdowns called back because of penalties. Williams might be the engine, but Corum is the spark. He continues to provide the explosive plays that the Rams’ run game needs. Williams and Corum also became the first Rams' running back duo to have 90 or more yards in the same game since Marshall Faulk and Trung Candidate in 2001.
Kyren Williams and Blake Corum's rushing charts shows exactly why they work well together. A lot more green/consistency from Williams, but Corum brings big-play ability. The answer to a dominant Rams' run game is using both in a 50-50 split. pic.twitter.com/TFVhtWlDac
Coming into the game, Matthew Stafford led the NFL in passing attempts. While the Rams built an early double-digit lead, McVay also committed to the run earlier in the game, which opened things up in the passing game. The presence of the run game allowed the Rams to get to their play-action passing game and get the tight ends involved underneath with misdirection. This shouldn’t be the expected game script every week, but it shows how much a consistent, balanced offensive approach makes everything easier.
For much of the season, Matthew Stafford hasn’t been great. He’s been good in moments, but he’s lacked some consistency. Against the Raiders, Stafford was efficient and simply took what was available. In the first half, he went 17-for-19 for 148 yards and had three touchdowns. With his third touchdown, Stafford became the Rams’ all-time leader in passing touchdowns, surpassing Roman Gabriel. The game may have been different during Gabriel’s era, but Stafford still accomplished the feat in nearly half the time. This is the Stafford that the Rams need more consistently. The big games against the Bills are nice, but if Stafford can simply keep the offense on track, it will put the offense in a better spot going forward.
For as good as the offense was against the Raiders, the passing game still feels one-dimensional and constricted. Stafford averaged 4.9 air yards per attempt. It’s the second consecutive week he’s averaged fewer than five air yards per attempt. Prior to that, he hadn’t done so in 23 consecutive games. The Rams need a player who can stretch the field and create explosives in the passing game.
This wasn’t the Raiders offense of old that the Rams were going up against. Coming into the game, the Raiders ranked fifth in EPA per pass and sixth in passing success rate. At one point, the Rams were holding them to -0.96 EPA per pass and a zero percent success rate. The defense held the Raiders to 5-for-19 on conversion downs. They also got a stop on a two-point conversion to keep it a two-score game in the fourth quarter. The defense was dominant in the first half and did enough to close it out late in the game.
For much of the season, the Rams haven’t had an identity that they could fall back on. Some of that had to do with injuries, but they weren't the only reason. Against the Raiders, the Rams got back to the team they wanted to be coming into the year. They had a dynamic rushing attack that operated out of 13 personnel and leaned on the play-action passing game. When the Rams' offense went quiet for the entire third quarter, they were able to lean on their rushing attack to put the game away late. This is what the Rams need to lean on going forward.
While the Rams were impressive in Week 2, Jaxson Dart got injured early in that game. The Raiders may have been on a three-game losing streak, but two of those losses were by three points to the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills. Had the Rams played like they did last week, they likely would have lost. It may have gotten tense at the beginning of the fourth quarter, but this was a complete team win. The Rams played good, complementary football and now have a win that they can build on.
This was a turning point in the Rams’ season. There is still a lot of work to do and the Rams need to show that they can stack wins. However, they found an identity on offense that they can lean on and got a win against a solid team when they needed it. After last week, the Rams needed a win they could feel good about, and the way they beat the Raiders provided exactly that. It’s hard not to overreact to one win, but this was a step in the right direction. When we look back at the Rams’ season in two months, it’s possible this win is seen as where things began to change.

title: Monday Morning Rambling: Rams Rediscover Winning Formula Against Raiders
full_text:
Following last week’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals, the Los Angeles Rams had officially hit rock bottom as they dropped to 2-4. While a 2-5 start once seemed impossible for a Sean McVay-led football team, it was hard to have confidence in anything this Rams team did or predict what they’d look like on a weekly basis. After beating the Las Vegas Raiders, 35-21 on Sunday, the Rams may have finally figured out what kind of team they want to be .
Coming into the season, one of the main talking points was how the Rams were going to lean into the 13 personnel that they had so much success with in 2025. With two running backs, the Rams were going to more evenly split their carries to give the running game a consistently fresh feel to it.
However, through the first six weeks of the season, no quarterback threw more passes than Matthew Stafford. Prior to Sunday’s game against the Raiders, Kyren Williams had 80 rushing attempts to Blake Corum’s 47.
There was certainly some context for why the Rams were so pass-heavy, but the offense still needed to get back to the basics and take a more balanced approach. That’s exactly what they did against the Raiders, and the results spoke for themselves.
For the first time this season, the Rams had more rushing attempts than passing attempts. Corum led the Rams with 17 carries as he and Williams combined for 33 rushes for 192 yards and two touchdowns.
The Rams operated out of 13 personnel on 52.3 percent of their plays, the highest rate for any team in a game this season. With the balanced rushing attack, the Rams were able to lean more on play action. Their 56.7 percent play action rate was the highest for any team in a game this season.
With a more balanced approach and by leaning into the identity this team was meant to have, the Rams had a 63.1 percent offensive success rate. That is in the 99th percentile since 2016 and the fourth highest of the McVay era. It was the 25th highest in any game since 2016.
There’s little doubt that Matthew Stafford has regressed from last year. With that in mind, McVay made things simpler for his quarterback and allowed the running game to carry the load. It can certainly be argued that’s how it should’ve been all along.
During the 2021 season, McVay got used to Stafford being able to sling the ball all over the field without consequence. In the three-game stretch that became known as “No Win November,” Stafford threw the ball 127 times. Over the next six weeks, the Rams got back to the basics of leaning on the run game, with Sony Michel recording 18 or more carries in each game. The Rams went 5-1 during that stretch.
Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford are certainly a perfect match for each other. However, that can sometimes lead to McVay leaning on his quarterback’s arm too much. After dropping to 2-4, the Rams just needed to get back to the basics, and that’s exactly what they did. While they went three-and-out after three consecutive passes on the opening drive, it was much more balanced from that point forward. The Rams scored a touchdown on their next four drives. On those drives, the Rams ran the ball 16 times for 103 yards.
The Rams have shown the ability to win games this season. However, they have not been able to stack wins. After beating the Giants, the Rams blew a 16-point lead to the Broncos. Following the win against the Eagles, the Rams had a field goal blocked in overtime, preventing them from winning against the Bills.
If the Rams are going to recover from a 2-4 start, they need to start stacking wins. They won’t have any reason not to as they face the 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers next week, followed by the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals. If the Rams get Myles Garrett back within the next week or two, it’s possible that they finally start to hit their stride. With Garrett back, the vision of what the Rams wanted to be coming into the season might finally start to come together.
When all is said and done, we might look back on the Rams beating the Raiders as a turning point in the season. While it may have “only been the Raiders,” the Rams aren’t in a position to discount wins. The Rams played their most complete game to date and found their identity while doing so. That’s something they can build on.
At some point, the narrative around the Rams’ wide receiver depth is no longer that they aren’t being used, but that they just aren’t good enough. Without Davante Adams in the lineup, Konata Mumpfield was the only wide receiver outside of Puka Nacua to have a reception. He had just one catch for 15 yards. Last season, the Rams ignored their need at cornerback, and it cost them. If the Rams don’t add a wide receiver at the trade deadline , it could have the same impact once the playoffs come.
The Rams were without Nate Landman on Sunday as he missed the game with a concussion. Without Landman, the Rams had Omar Speights and Shaun Dolac at linebacker. Speights was the primary linebacker throughout the game, but Dolac played well in his limited snaps. The Rams’ linebackers played well, especially against the run. It’s hard to see the Rams benching Landman, but Dolac took advantage of his opportunity.
There might be something to a running back not being able to get in a rhythm with a consistent rotation. However, this is the Rams’ running game at its best . In games when both Corum and Williams have had 10 or more carries this season, the offense has delivered two of its best performances outside of Week 1 in Australia. Giving Corum a consistent role in the offense gives defenses something else to prepare for.
It’s certainly possible to hand out multiple game balls for the win against the Raiders. Matthew Stafford hit a milestone, becoming the franchise leader in touchdown passes. Davis Allen scored two touchdowns. Additionally, Jaylen Watson had a good game. However, Corum provided a spark for the offense, and had it not been for two penalties, he would have scored three touchdowns. He finished with 17 carries for 93 yards and showed why he should be used more alongside Williams.
The Rams ran the ball 33 times. Again, it’s the first time this season that the Rams have had more rushing attempts than passing attempts. That’s not how things are going to shake out every week as the Rams aren’t going to have a double-digit lead to work with. Still, it shows that when the offense is balanced, everything works together.
As mentioned earlier, it’s very possible that we look at this game against the Raiders as a turning point in the season. Now, the Rams have to start stacking wins. They should be able to do that against a Chargers team that has struggled to find its own identity, despite them coming off of their bye.
Through seven weeks, the Rams are 3-4 and sit in third place in the NFC West. They still have an opportunity to get to the bye week in a good spot. With that said, they need to show some consistency week to week. Sunday’s win was a good start, but they finally have an identity they can build on going forward.

title: Hondo’s Mailbag: Raiders Fans Demand Answers on Struggling OL
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) head to Gotham this weekend to take on the New York Jets (2-5) on Sunday.
The Silver and Black are headed back East for another 10 AM PT kickoff, and they will face their starting QB from last season, Geno Smith.
But before they get on the airplane and head out, they have a tough week of practice and some tough issues that must be addressed.
Kirk Cousins currently leads the NFL in touchdown passes with 16, and nearly 1,900 passing yards is good for third.  Still, the Raiders don’t have a running game, and their offensive line is, at best, suspect.
The fan base understands exactly what is going on with this Raiders rebuild that is currently underway, and because of the 3-0 hot start, they want more.
The NFL trade deadline is looming, and a win will certainly impact the Raiders' moves.  Additionally, a loss would, as well as some around the league feel, mean GM John Spytek has a lot to consider if the Raiders lose the next two games before the deadline.
I asked you all on my social media X account to tell me what you are looking to see most besides the win, and you didn’t disappoint.
Be able to run the ball. Our interior O-line has been ass all year...
The guard's play over the last three weeks hasn't been good, and last week was terrible.  I asked Klint Kubiak on Monday about G Bryve Cabeldue and rookie OL Trey Zuhn III getting the chance to earn reps on Sunday, and his answer was direct and clear, Yes.”
That is good news.  This is a rebuilding year, but the Raiders need to foster competition as best they can to create an even bigger point of emphasis and competition.
I have lost zero faith in C Tyler Linderbaum, who has had only truly bad games, but has had nearly zero help on his right and left.
The Kubiak system is rooted in, and finds it foundational, strength in running the ball; you can’t and won’t with guard play as bad as it has been this year.
Someone to tackle, someone not named Maxx to put pressure from the D line, the destruction of this vanilla wafer offense, and letting Washington Jr. carry the damn ball.
I am a little surprised that there isn’t more consternation about the defense.  The entire time I have covered the Silver and Black, the entirety of their time in Las Vegas, it has been stop Maxx Crosby and stop the Raiders' defense.
The Raiders have spent countless millions on high-priced free agents and even rookies, and no one has been able to do it except Malcolm Koonce for half a season in 2023.
The Raiders' defensive coaches have to do better, and many players have been pathetic in the tackle box.
These men are professionals, and sloppy technique reflects on them; the CBA limits practice, and even the physicality of practice, and that had a tremendous impact on the game.
There are many reasons things have gone wrong this year, and many are legitimate. Still, the poor tackling should embarrass all of them as highly paid professionals who have done it consistently, and they've done it several times.
For Gino to have 2 int. If it could be on the first pass of the game, like against Chargers last year, that would be awesome. Not too much right?
I understand Raider Nation’s bitterness towards Geno Smith because last year was a disaster.  I can also tell you that Geno wasn’t the number one reason for the failure in 2025, and isn’t even close to the top of the list.
While I think he is a good QB, he is not elite, and no one knows this defense better than how to bait him into mistakes; they saw it every day in practice last year.
While I think he will be highly motivated to punish the Raiders, every player left from last year’s team knows that the Raiders didn’t lose solely because of Geno.
That said, if the Raiders win, I would expect Geno to have a hand in it; that is the track record of his losses in this league. I like Geno, have never hidden it, and while I think his behavior toward the Raiders fans was unacceptable and warranted punishment from the team, it doesn’t change the fact that two news teams are facing off on Sunday.
Some fight in all three phases. Two of the last three games there was practically no fight. Dominated in those games.
Good call, Doc.  I can tell you I have been impressed by this team's lack of quit, but I've also been shocked by its lack of fight.
Some of these guys' play has been terrible on national TV.  I know these men; while they certainly don’t play for free, they're not men who don’t care.
At some time, you have to come back punching and fight back.  I want to see some gut fighters in these guys.  The raw emotion that fuels this game.
Hondo S. Carpenter Sr. is an award-winning sports journalist with decades of experience.
