title: Five Instant Overreactions to the Dolphins-Jets Matchup
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins grabbed their first win of the season against the New York Jets. Their 28 to 25 victory marks the first of Jeff Hafley's Miami tenure, which means it's time to overreact to this game.
After not holding a single lead over the course of their first five games, Miami never trailed against the Jets. They remained in control through an ugly second half, and started what could be one of the craziest stories in NFL history.
On a very real note, the Miami Dolphins grabbed a win that required every ounce of effort they could muster. From a stellar offensive first half closed out by some masterful clock management to a timely fourth-down conversion to seal the victory, Jeff Hafley’s unit never wavered and won several crucial momentum-swinging moments. This win adds an exclamation point to a first half of a season that has felt about as promising as 1-5 can feel.
Malik Willis played what was easily his best game as a member of the Miami Dolphins, going 14 of 21 passing for 208 yards and two touchdowns, and adding another 37 yards and a score on the ground. His decision-making was consistently positive, as he understood when to take off, when to move off of his progressions, and when to fire into some tight windows.
On Miami’s first scoring drive, Willis made multiple throws late in the progression, including the first of two touchdown passes to Caleb Douglas. Just as important, though, was what we didn’t see on the stat sheet: turnovers. Miami won the takeaway battle on Sunday, and while Geno Smith threw an early pick to Michael Taaffe, Willis kept the ball out of harm’s way.
Willis looked like a completely different player than what we saw against the Cincinnati Bengals, and if he can start to stack strong performances, his window as the Dolphins’ franchise quarterback will remain cracked open.
One of Miami’s most promising rookies made his triumphant return on Sunday, and Caleb Douglas’ impact on the health of the Dolphins’ passing game is palpable.
His two catches, both of which went for touchdowns, showcased an element Miami simply doesn’t have with any of their other weapons. In the first quarter, Douglas dusted cornerback Azareye'h Thomas, pressing into his toes and snapping off a gorgeous route to the inside. Then, when Miami’s offense struggled to remain explosive late in the game, Douglas hit Minkah Fitzpatrick with a mean stutter-step, and followed it up with a tightrope act that resulted in a 63-yard score.
Even when he wasn’t making plays, it's clear that Douglas’ size and talent put the rest of the Dolphins’ receiving weapons in a more natural spot. Greg Dulcich had one of his best games, and Malik Washington made multiple nice plays underneath. Douglas’ impact cannot be understated, and his presence was key in Miami grabbing their first win.
The Dolphins’ rookies have largely met expectations, and one who has far exceeded them is safety Michael Taaffe.
Taaffe grabbed his second interception of the season against the Jets, triggering down on a crossing route by Jeremy Ruckert. It was an excellent play, and one Taaffe continues to make this season, trusting his instincts to fly towards the football.
Even as a rookie, there are a couple of plays in each game where it seems like Taaffe knows what the offense is running before it happens. His football IQ has made an immediate impact on the back end, and in a year where the primary goal is assessing talent, the former fifth-round pick looks like a gem.
In what ended up as potentially the biggest play of the game, former Miami Dolphins kicker Jason Sanders missed a 40-yard field goal for the New York Jets, and for the first time all year, the Dolphins played what looked like a clean game in the third phase.
In the first game after Jeff Hafley not-so-subtly called out Riley Patterson for not being able to get the ball into the end zone, Patterson’s replacement, veteran Zane Gonzalez and punter Bradley Pinion took turns on kickoffs and had the distance to eliminate the Jets’ potential returns. Gonzalez also went four for four on extra points.
Pinion had a mediocre punt that was salvaged by a nice bounce, but overall, special teams wasn’t a glaring negative, and that’s the first time all season that I’ve been able to say that.
Tyler DeSena is currently a journalism student at the University of Central Florida. Prior to joining Dolphins On SI in 2026, DeSena worked with dolphinstalk.com, and created independent social media content on X, YouTube and TikTok.

title: Miami Dolphins Week 7 Instant Takeaways: Willis, Douglas Make Sure to End Winless Foolishness
full_text:
OK, everybody can forget about this idea — farfetched as it was — that the Miami Dolphins were going to finish the 2026 season at 0-7 and we can at least hit the pause button on this idea that the Malik Willis experiment already should be deemed a failure.
The Dolphins got that elusive first victory of the Jeff Hafley era Sunday and of course it was going to come against the New York Jets, just has it had in 2007 after Miami started off 0-7.
And while there were plenty of stars on this day — welcome back, Caleb Douglas — Willis absolutely was front and center.
His final passing numbers weren't necessarily overwhelming as he finished with 208 yards on 14 completions, but he provided exactly the kind of quarterback we saw during his stints with the Green Bay Packers that convinced Hafley and Jon-Eric Sullivan to bring him over.
It was the kind of performance that would make the Dolphins look to another position with their first-round pick in the 2027 NFL draft, a pick that still figures to be pretty high, and maybe we can stop debating — at least for a little while — whether it should be Drew Mestermaker or Arch Manning or Darian Mensah.
All along, we said Willis deserved the benefit of the doubt and a longer look before making definitive judgements about his viability as a starting quarterback, but if nothing else he bought himself more time with that performance — not that we would suggest he's cemented anything, either, just off one game.
As for the win and that silly notion the Dolphins could go 0-17, did anybody really think the Dolphins wouldn't be able to improve as the season moved along.
And, as we pointed out on numerous occasions, if the 2019 Dolphins could win five games after being outscored 163-26 (basically an average of 41-7) in their four games, yeah the 2026 Dolphins pretty safely were going to win a game here and there.
-- Douglas had only two catches in his return after missing three games with an ankle injury, but they both showed why he's the most exciting player on offense (outside of Willis) with De'Von Achane on IR. His first touchdown showed off his route-running ability as he faked the Jets cornerback out of his cleats with a quick jerky movement and then there was the fabulous YAC work on what became the game-winning touchdown. And how sweet was it that the Jets player he beat to turn a short reception into a long touchdown was none other than Minkah Fitzpatrick.
-- Major hats off to the running game for being able to close out the win after the Jets cut their lead with 3:24 left. It was five straight runs that produced two first downs, starting with a 14-yarder by Ollie Gordon II and punctuated by Malik Willis' sneak on fourth-and-1 where Gordon played a big role with his push of Willis. And even though it was risky, we tweeted before the call that the Dolphins should go for the win on that fourth-and-1 instead of going the conservative route and trying to pin the Jets deep. That's the kind of aggressiveness we want to see from Hafley moving forward.
-- Since we already mentioned Gordon, he continues to shine in the absence of De'Von Achane and looks like a feature back himself.
-- A couple of changes we noticed with the offense was that there weren't as man deep shots as in previous weeks, and that led to a better completion percentage for Willis. His decision-making was better, his scrambling again was a big factor, and he showed great awareness with his slide in bounds near the end of the first half to make sure the Jets wouldn't have much time left after they scored to make it 21-7.
-- It's pretty refreshing that we won't be talking about bad special teams play this week, isn't it?
-- It's actually ironic that the Dolphins ended up winning by three and the only missed field goal came from former Miami kicker Jason Sanders.
-- The Dolphins' new kicker Zane Gonzalez did a good job of putting the ball into the end zone on kickoffs, which limited the Jets' kickoff return opportunities and we'll take the defense starting at the 35.
-- The pass defense again wasn't great, but the secondary is the youngest unit on defense, so maybe it's to be expected to a certain degree. And that was a big-time veteran play by safety Michael Taaffe on his pick when he totally read the eyes of Geno Smith as he was scrambling.
-- Another big reason for the three-point win, of course, was the goal-line stand culminated by Chop Robinson's third-down sack when he absolutely didn't bite on Smith's play fake and Zayne Anderson took away Smith's short outlet. But it was Zach Sieler who made the big first-down tackle to start the whole thing, part of a really good performance by the D-tackle.
-- Yes, we have to factor in the quality (or lack thereof) of the opposition when dissecting this first Dolphins win, but then we also have to look at the quality of the teams against which they lost. So it works both ways. The Dolphins step up again in competition next week when they play host to the New England Patriots, but we'll continue to say the Dolphins will win a game or two this season that they're not supposed to win.
-- This game again the Jets was one of those that was deemed most winnable for the Dolphins, and that's how it played out. Now we don't have to hear anymore about going 0-17, we can table the draft talk for a bit because who knows exactly how high they'll wind up picking in the first round, and maybe most importantly we can just sit back and continue watching the development of the players before making premature determinations.

title: The Five Dolphins Players in the Spotlight in Week 7
full_text:
The MIami Dolphins will be back in action against the New York Jets on Sunday, and the mission will remain the same.
The Dolphins still are looking for their first victory of the season, but more importantly want to see progress and improvement, particularly after the disappointing showing in the last outing against the Cincinnati Bengals.
The matchup against the Jets, who also are in rebuilding mode though further ahead than the Dolphins, represents a good opportunity for Miami to get its first win of the season and end all talk of a winless season.
Most importantly, the Dolphins need for their young players to get better and organically that will give them a better chance to win as the season progresses.
With that in mind, here are the five players we'll be watching closely against the Jets:
QB Malik Willis — There might come a time when this no longer applies because it will have become apparent that the Dolphins need to look elsewhere to find a quarterback for the long run, but we're not there yet — even though a lot of fans already have given up on him. It's very obvious that Willis hasn't played well enough so far in 2026, but every game is a new opportunity and at some point the entire offense (hopefully) will start jelling a bit more.
WR Caleb Douglas — It's not often that the return of a rookie third-round pick is as anticipated as Douglas being back against the Jets, but this is where we are with the Dolphins. The clear lack of playmakers on offense was exacerbated by the loss of De'Von Achane to his season-ending knee injury and Douglas' performance in the Week 1 game against Las Vegas provided cause for excitement. Having said that, it's also probably not fair to expect big numbers from Douglas right away after he missed three games with an ankle injury, but there should be some kind of impact.
RB Ollie Gordon II — Gordon has averaged 94 yards in his two games since taking over as the starter, and now he'll be facing a run defense that's had some tough outings. Gordon could become the most important player on offense before this season is over.
LB Jacob Rodriguez — The second-round pick is off to a great start in his rookie season as a tackle machine, but he'll be challenged again in the pass game because the Jets have an uber athletic rookie first-round pick at tight end with Kenyon Sadiq, whose backup is another good young pass-catching tight end, Mason Taylor (son of Dolphins legend Jason Taylor). It won't be all on Rodriguez to limit the damage from the tight ends, but he'll be involved and will need to clamp down.
EDGE Chop Robinson — Jets quarterback Geno Smith has been very good this year at avoiding turnovers, but he'll also been criticized for taking too many sacks. This is where Robinson has to come in. Some of his analytics in the pass-rushing department are very good, but they haven't translated into enough impact plays. This is where he's got to make it happen.

title: Vikings Verdict: Judging J.J. McCarthy, RB Trade Targets & Other Overreactions Ahead of Week 8
full_text:
The Vikings are 6-0, but it hasn't stopped fans from casting doom up and down the roster . Despite the unblemished record, the play itself has often been lacking, and the team may need to make some dramatic changes sooner rather than later .
Is a blockbuster trade in the cards? Do the Vikings have a Justin Jefferson problem? Let's dive into those and more overreactions ahead of Week 8.
At 6-0, the Vikings could, and maybe should, be buyers at the upcoming trade deadline. And one position that makes a ton of sense is adding at running back. Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones Sr. are fine enough, but therein lies the issue.
Fine gets you some solid numbers, decent pass protection, and good reliability. What fine won't get you is a scared defense, explosive, game-changing plays, and someone to take over the game when and if Kyler Murray stumbles.
Trading for a top talent like Jonathan Taylor or Saquon Barkley, just to name a few, wouldn't come cheap, and the Vikings would have to dig deep into the stash of 2027 draft picks to acquire them. On the one hand, a second- or even first-round pick is a lot to give up for a veteran at a position that almost requires youth.
But on the other hand, when else will your team be 6-0 with a generational defense?
As the 32nd ranked team in offensive success rate, the Vikings offense is clearly still missing something. Getting better at running back won't solve everything, but there aren't many other feasible ways to improve this ailing offense by December.
After just two games, McCarthy really already has the media talking about how the Giants could be moving on from Jaxson Dart in favor of their newest signal caller. Truly. He's thrown for nearly 500 yards in just five quarters over the last two weeks for New York, and is either in some sort of brief flow state or the Vikings just let another franchise quarterback out the door.
It's truthfully way too early to have an opinion on McCarthy's future.
After all, his first career start against the Bears in 2025 saw him win Offensive Player of the Week, just to follow it up with two interceptions in a 22-6 beatdown against Atlanta the following week. His career sample size is still just too small. Still, at 23 and with obvious arm talent, the question of why the Vikings moved on so early and for so little in return is certainly an annoyance, at the very least.
McCarthy may not end up being the answer in New York either, but it's clear his ceiling is years away from being reached, and the Vikings bailing on their youngster so early is surely disappointing. It's hard to know what went on behind the scenes, but he probably should've gotten another stab at the starting job with Minnesota in 2027.
Jefferson is, and has been, known as one of the best receivers in the game, but the Vikings seem to be the last to know.
Despite all his talents, Jefferson is averaging just 6.2 targets per game, a far cry from the 11.1 or 11.5 numbers that other top players like Jaxson Smith-Njigba or Ceedee Lamb are seeing, respectively. Jefferson also has yet to eclipse 100 yards in a game this season, and even his 1,000-yard streak could very much be in danger if he misses another game or two.
Sure, the Vikings aren't airing the ball out 40 times per game, instead focusing on safe, smart, small-ball, but it's hard to forgive not targeting your best player. Clearly, other teams have figured out ways to scheme and then eventually throw to their top option. So what's the deal here?
It's possible that Murray and Jefferson are still working out chemistry issues, or that Jefferson still isn't 100% after spraining his ankle against Tampa Bay. Those are potentially valid, but for the most part, there's really no reason the Vikings shouldn't be looking Jefferson's way on nearly every dropback.
As great as it is to never turn the ball over by only throwing four-yard flat passes to tight ends and running backs, eventually the training wheels have to come off for a grown-up offense.

title: Rewarding Kyle Van Noy Should Be Among Vikings' Priorities After Week 7
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings signed edge rusher Kyle Van Noy this offseason to take pressure off Andrew Van Ginkel and Dallas Turner. However, he has more than exceeded expectations in Brian Flores' defense and deserves to be rewarded for his play.
Despite being 35 years old and in his 13th year as a pro, Van Noy is tied for the most tackles for loss among all Vikings defenders. He is tied with inside linebacker Blake Cashman at 7.5 and is showing no signs of slowing down.
As soon as general manager Nolan Teasley is able, Minnesota should lock him down for one more season by signing him to an extension. Keeping him with the Purple and Gold ensures the Vikings' strong edge-rush presence at a low cost.
Van Noy is averaging 19.2 defensive snaps per game, which is approximately 32 percent of the Vikings' total defensive snaps this year. In that limited role, he has still recorded 12 tackles, two quarterback hits, and 1.5 sacks.
What makes the Van Noy signing this offseason even more impressive is that Minnesota brought the two-time Super Bowl champion and former Pro Bowl edge rusher in on a one-year, $2.75 million deal to play for the 2026 NFL season.
Getting the type of production that Van Noy is experiencing this season at that cost is a huge bargain. His excellent play hasn't gone unnoticed by Pro Football Focus , which have him rated as the ninth-best edge rusher in the league out of 112 qualifying players with a grade of 85.1.
Although he can get after opposing quarterbacks at a solid rate, his real strength this year has been defending against the run. He has a PFF run defense grade of 86.3, which is the fourth-best of any edge rusher this season.
There's no reason not to lock Van Noy down for another season. He, Van Ginkel, and Turner have formed a dangerous trio of edge rushers who should return for the 2027 season. Plus, rewarding Van Noy for his play this season with a pay increase or bonuses would go a long way toward showing the veteran defender how much his contributions to Minnesota's defense are appreciated.
If Van Noy wants to play next season, it should be with the Vikings. And the team needs to make bringing him back a priority.

title: Myles Price's Injury Could Open Door for One Vikings Letdown to Save His Roster Spot
full_text:
Against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7, Minnesota Vikings wide receiver and return specialist Myles Price left the game and did not return. He took a big hit after catching a punt and was evaluated for a concussion.
Price has been an asset for the Vikings as a return specialist this season. In six games, he returned 18 kickoffs for 552 yards, and he leads the league with 250 punt return yards and a touchdown on 13 opportunities.
Price could be forced to miss time this season while going through concussion protocol in Minnesota. If that happens, the door could be open for a disappointing rookie to finally make an impact on the team this season.
Although wide receiver Tai Felton is listed as the backup return specialist on the Vikings' official website, that doesn't mean that dynamic rookie running back Demond Claiborne won't get an opportunity to showcase his return skills.
At Wake Forest, Claiborne returned 22 kickoffs for 579 yards and two touchdowns. His speed and elusiveness would make him a dangerous weapon on special teams to help win the field-position battle.
Claiborne doesn't have the same kind of experience on punt returns. In college, he fielded two punts, but did not record any return yardage. The only other player to return a punt for the Vikings in the last two years is Jeshaun Jones, who had only two returns for five yards in the 2025 season finale against the Green Bay Packers.
For Claiborne, something has to happen. The rookie running back was inactive in Week 7 against the Indianapolis Colts, while the team cut DeeJay Dallas, signed him to the practice squad, elevated him and played him for 20 total snaps between offense and special teams.
It feels like the Vikings are only keeping Claiborne on the 53-man roster out of fear of another team signing him if he is released to be signed to the practice squad. That roster spot seems to be held hostage at the moment, but finding a role for him as a kickoff return specialist would give him some value to the roster.
When one player goes down with an injury, others have to step up. In the case of Price's concussion, this is an opportunity for Claiborne to prove that the sixth-round draft pick in the 2026 NFL Draft can give the Vikings some production on the field.

title: Vikings Must Act Quickly If They Want to Trade for Colts' Jonathan Taylor
full_text:
As the Vikings continue to debate potential trade deadline plans , one potential partner has already put up their 'For Sale' sign.
The storefront is officially open in Indianapolis as the Colts' fire sale has begun . Indy made its first major trade Tuesday, sending star left guard Quenton Nelson to Seattle for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick  (h/t: ESPN ’s Adam Schefter).
Compensation update; The Seahawks are sending a 2027 third-round pick and 2028 fifth-round round pick to the Colts in exchange for Quenton Nelson. https://t.co/17B0bR47yV
The move signals a shift in priorities for a 2-5 Colts team coming off a defeat in Minnesota. With no first-round selection after last year’s Sauce Gardner trade, Indianapolis seems desperate to acquire whatever draft capital it can, and contenders will likely be circling for the chance to add any available talent.
One man who needs to be in the mix? Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley.
His target? Three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor.
With the Colts opening up their phone lines, the time to act is now.
The Vikings’ offense desperately needs a boost as they enter the most challenging stretch of their schedule.
While the defense and special teams are performing at an elite level, the offense is becoming a serious concern (h/t: Warren Sharp). Short of a midseason change at quarterback , the best way to get the offense on track is an explosive RB, and no rumored target fits that bill quite like Taylor.
the Minnesota Vikings are only undefeated team left on early downs this season, their offense: #32 with 29% success rate #32 with 18% of plays gain a 1st down #32 with 24.0% of plays gain 7+ yards 62% of its series reach 3rd down #1 most in the NFL
According to Spotrac , Taylor is under contract for two more years, with cap hits of $21.02 million and $22.98 million in 2027 and 2028 , respectively.
Rumors have circulated about Taylor’s potential availability in recent weeks, and the Vikings have consistently been linked to a possible deal. Speculation only increased after Nelson was traded to Seattle, but one NFL insider seemed to pump the brakes .
NFL insider Adam Schefter joined "The Pat McAfee Show" Tuesday afternoon, stating, “My understanding is that the owner (Carlie Irsay-Gordon) doesn’t want to trade Jonathan Taylor.”
"My understanding is that the Colts don't wanna trade Jonathan Taylor.. If I had to guess today I don't think that they will trade Jonathan Taylor" ~ @AdamSchefter #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/LJ7WY63hAa
Personally, I interpret this to mean one thing: up those offers.
The Colts are clearly heading toward a rebuild, so why hold on to a 27-year-old back who likely won't be at his peak by the time they finally build a semi-competitive roster? To me, it’s a call to action to GMs everywhere to get aggressive. It’s time for Teasley and the Vikings to play ball.
The Vikings may be the last undefeated team in the NFL, but that won’t last much longer if their offense doesn't get on track. With a November schedule consisting of games against the Lions, Bills, Packers, 49ers and a feisty Falcons team, the Vikings need help, and they need it now.
Explosive plays have been nearly nonexistent in the Vikings’ running game over the last two seasons, and a trade for Taylor would immediately fix that. He's recorded runs of 20-plus yards in five of seven appearances so far, including a season-high 38-yard score against the Vikings.
Why are the Vikings interested in running backs at the deadline? Lack of explosive runs. Here are the longest runs of each season since Kevin O’Connell took over as coach in 2022: - 2022: Dalvin Cook, 81 yards - 2023: Ty Chandler, 31 yards - 2024: Cam Akers, 58 yards - 2025:…
Even with two weeks left until the NFL trade deadline, acting soon on a Taylor trade is the right move. It may come at a premium, but Teasley and the Vikings cannot afford to risk another NFC contender picking up the star back.

title: Potential Vikings Defensive Concern May Have Emerged Ahead of Week 8 vs. Lions
full_text:
It isn't a secret that the Vikings' defense has been stellar this year. Heading into Week 8's NFC North clash with the rival Lions, the Purple and Gold are allowing the second-fewest yards (252.8), second-fewest passing yards (155.0) and fewest points allowed per game (12.3).
That said, even the best units face obstacles.
Week 7's win over the Colts might have highlighted a potential concern for the Vikings' defense in the coming weeks. Superstar running back Jonathan Taylor had 18 rushing attempts for 95 yards and a touchdown in Week 7, an average of 5.3 yards per attempt. It was the second most rushing yards they've allowed to a running back this season, as well as the second time in the last three games an opposing RB has gone for 90-plus yards.
The list of running backs Minnesota will face in the next few weeks is intimidating and will test the Vikings' defense as they attempt to continue their winning ways this season. This gauntlet starts on Sunday in Detroit.
Given the upcoming schedule, the last thing that the Vikings need is to find out that star RBs are their defense's kryptonite.
Here is a list of the running backs the Vikings will face in the coming weeks:
That list of running backs is full of star players who can change the course of a game at a moment's notice. Even with McCaffrey dealing with a thigh issue, he is a player who needs to be accounted for every time he touches the ball. That's without mentioning that he leads the NFL in rushing touchdowns, while Robinson is the yardage leader on the ground.
The run defense has been the most questionable part of defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit this season, but the Vikings still allow the tenth fewest rushing yards per game this season (97.8) and are bound to see that average increase after the next five weeks of opponents.
Minnesota is getting fantastic play from its defensive line this year. Jalen Redmond in particular has a Pro Football Focus grade of 81.7 , ranking him fourth among 126 qualifying defensive linemen. Another defender in the trenches who is playing well is Levi Drake Rodriguez, with a PFF grade of 62.2.
To this point, Taylor is the best running back the Vikings have faced this season, and he nearly broke 100 yards while finding the end zone on a 38-yard run. Minnesota will need to contain the opposing rushers over the next five weeks to prove its defense can compensate for an anemic offense against some of the top offenses in the league.
Their first test comes in the form of Gibbs and the Lions this weekend. The otherworldly RB has had success against the Vikings, converting 92 carries into 431 rushing yards and 18 catches into 121 receiving yards while scoring nine total TDs in six all-time matchups—including two 100-yard performances.
The Purple and Gold can't allow big runs against them if they hope to win the field-position battle against the explosive offenses coming up on the schedule. Stopping those superstar running backs needs to be the top priority if the Vikings hope to stay on top of the NFC North.
Otherwise, the Purple and Gold might have another need to address before the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10.

title: Biggest Vikings' Trade Deadline Needs Can't Be Ignored as Perfect Season Continues
full_text:
The 6-0 Vikings are in an incredibly unique spot as they sit atop the NFL as the league’s last unbeaten team .
While the defense and special teams have repeatedly showcased their championship-level pedigree, the offense has become a serious point of concern. Now, general manager Nolan Teasley must capitalize on the team’s hot start by adding additional talent to fill the gaps .
Teasley and head coach Kevin O’Connell have several potential routes to take, so let’s break down four trade scenarios that could give the Vikings the boost they need through the rest of the season and into the playoffs.
Let me start by giving Aaron Jones the flowers he rightly deserves. His 436 rushing yards through six games came without much help from his fellow backs, as Jordan Mason was placed on IR immediately after Week 1. Jones’s workload took a noticeable step back as Mason returned to the lineup on Sunday, ending the day with only eight carries for 26 yards.
But Jones continues to show his toughness, playing through a knee injury that he aggravated Sunday , leaving him day-to-day, according to ESPN' s Adam Schefter.
Vikings RB Aaron Jones’ knee injury that he suffered during Sunday’s win over the Colts is not considered to be significant at this time, and a source described him as “day to day.”
With depth at running back a major concern and the offense desperate for an explosive spark, a trade for a home-run-hitting back is possible, and Colts RB Jonathan Taylor may be the best-case acquisition.
Several factors come into play with a possible Taylor trade, and it seems a possible trade may be getting more expensive every day, with multiple contenders likely to check in. This would be an “all-in” move for Teasley and the Vikings, and may lead to some difficult decisions in the spring. But I don’t think many Vikings fans would mind the long-term implications if it led to a Lombardi this season.
Speaking of the Indy-to-Minnesota pipeline, right guard Will Fries has certainly disappointed since the former Colt signed with the Vikings in 2025 (h/t: Bring Me the News ’ Will Ragatz).
Will Fries gets knocked back by the DT for the Packers' second sack of the half. pic.twitter.com/0PzjYI4hGc
Fries's five-year, $ 88 million deal set high expectations that he simply has yet to meet in his time with the Vikings. He fractured his right leg in 2024 and seemingly has not been the same since. It's possible he never will be, and Minnesota needs to find a way to secure the offensive interior in the meantime, especially after the loss of left guard Donovan Jackson.
One name has emerged as a possible trade candidate for teams looking for help on the interior offensive line, and once again, he would come from Indianapolis.
Colts left guard Quenton Nelson has become a hot target as the Nov. 10 deadline approaches. With Nelson in the last year of his current deal and the Colts open for business, Nelson has “a lot of interest around the league,” according to NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. The 30-year-old guard is likely to land a massive contract this offseason, and the Vikings will have limited cap space, but adding the star lineman could do wonders for their offense, even if it’s just for this season
From The Aftermath on @nflnetwork : News and notes leading up to the NFL trade deadline, focusing in on the #Colts . pic.twitter.com/B3S9YjbSrT
What better way to make up for a struggling offense than by making your elite defense even better? This approach adds another talented pass rusher to defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit: current Charger Khalil Mack. The 35-year-old is well past his glory days, but his three sacks in LA’s first four games certainly turned heads. Since then, he has slowed significantly and has not found an opposing QB since Oct. 4.
While this isn't the blockbuster move many Vikings fans hoped for, Flores has already proven what he can do with veteran castaways in his all-out, aggressive scheme. As the season goes on, the team may need more pass-rush depth, and Mack’s experience and football IQ shouldn't be downplayed.
After six weeks and four full games together, O’Connell and Kyler Murray may simply not be a fit offensively. With a challenging schedule ahead and a defense too dominant to waste, could the Vikings make a switch? Would it even be possible?
It may just be worth making a call or two, especially on a certain former Viking.
The chances of the Raiders trading Kirk Cousins are slim, and according to head coach Klint Kubiak , it isn’t something they’re even considering (h/t: ESPN ’s Adam Schefter).
Raiders HC Klint Kubiak told reporters that Kirk Cousins is the team’s starting QB. “There is no controversy,” Kubiak said. Raiders play at the Jets on Sunday. pic.twitter.com/Y3M9DDMhkz
But what’s the harm in asking?
The Vikings' passing game has been a shadow of its former self since Sam Darnold’s departure after the 2024 season, and Cousins has proven capable of successfully executing many of O’Connell’s key concepts and play designs. His existing relationships with many former teammates could also go a long way, especially given Justin Jefferson's success with Cousins as his quarterback.
This one appears to be a long shot, but it's hard to imagine the idea hasn’t emerged in the halls of TCO Performance Center as the Vikings’ offense continues to struggle.

title: Breaking Down Vikings' Injury Report for Week 8 After Win Over the Colts (Who's Hurt and Who Could Return)
full_text:
Minnesota moved to 6-0 after getting past the listless Colts, and also came out of the game relatively healthy as an added bonus. A few Vikings did leave the game with injury, though, so there are a few names to watch this week ahead of a date with the Detroit Lions.
With various injuries on offense, defense and even one on special teams, here's who should be fine, and who might miss some time for Minnesota.
Price took a big hit on a punt return and was evaluated for a concussion. He was cleared to return to the game, but head coach Kevin O'Connell did say that Price was dealing with a stinger after the win. It didn't seem to affect the star returner, and there shouldn't be much concern heading into Week 8. Still, Price is one of those players that is darn-near irreplaceable for the Vikings if he did have to miss time.
Like Price, Addison was evaluated for a concussion before being cleared to play shortly after. Still, he wasn't able to do much in the contest, notching just two catches for 20 yards. Addison had already missed the Week 5 contest with a hamstring issue, but it appears he should have a clean bill of health to try and right the ship heading into the Lions matchup.
Jones has been battling a knee injury all season, and once again aggravated it late in the game against the Colts. O'Connell called the injury day-to-day after the game, but it wouldn't be too surprising if Jones needs a week off to let things heal. The Vikings have ridden Jones hard this season with Jordan Mason's own injury issues, and the toll on his body is adding up quickly.
If Jones can't shake this nagging knee issue, the Vikings could look to make a move for another runner at the trade deadline . Still, Jones has given his all this season, and it's hard to see him voluntarily coming off the field.
The Vikings' first-round pick exited the game with an apparent lower-body injury. And while his name didn't come up postgame as a possible serious injury, Banks' two previous foot injuries that forced him out of football for almost a year are certainly at the forefront of fans' minds. Banks didn't return after limping off the field , and his status will be something to monitor throughout the week.
Obviously injury concerns have been a big talking point with Banks, and if he does have to miss time, fellow rookie Domonique Orange could get some more run .
Luckily, the Vikings didn't appear to lose anyone to a long-term injury on Sunday. The key Vikings out for the season remained the same with Donovan Jackson, Josh Oliver, Jamal Adams and Tyler Batty all already lost for the year.

title: Vikings Week 7 Stock Report: Cashman Among Risers, Murray Falls After Gritty Win vs. Colts
full_text:
The Vikings are now the last undefeated team in the NFL , thanks to their elite special teams and suffocating defense. The offense, meanwhile, is still working out some wrinkles despite featuring some top-end talent.
After beating up on some bottom-feeder teams over the past few weeks, the real tests are just around the corner for Minnesota. So who is trending in the right direction, and who needs to step things up with the 4-2 Lions up next?
After a dominant performance against the Colts with 12 tackles and two sacks, Blake Cashman is playing some of the best football in the entire NFL right now. Heading into Week 8, he's first on the Vikings in tackles and tackles for loss, and second in sacks and passes defended. While not typically regarded as a household name, he's well on his way towards First-Team All-Pro recognition.
Cashman's contract is up after 2026 (like multiple other key starters), and the Vikings will have to shell out a pretty penny after what's shaping up to be his best season yet.
If Donovan Jackson wasn't already out for the year, Will Fries might very well be on the trade block. Since signing a monster contract to join Minnesota, Fries just hasn't figured things out in purple. Sunday's game was another sub-par performance, and Fries graded out as the fourth-worst offensive player by Pro Football Focus ' metrics with a 59.8.
The Vikings' interior was shaky all game, but while Joe Huber and Blake Brandel have inexperience on their side, Fries is running out of time to put things together.
Smith notched his 40th career interception in the win over Indy, and just one look at head coach Kevin O'Connell's post-game locker room speech tells the whole story of how important "The Hitman" is to the Vikings.
Harrison Smith hasn't played especially well this season, but Sunday's pick off of Daniel Jones (h/t NFL) to end the game was a step in the right direction. The Vikings still haven't found the perfect recipe at safety just yet, but it's clear Smith still has some savvy left.
HARRISON SMITH GETS THE INT! VIKINGS ARE 6-0 ‼️ pic.twitter.com/stul8J8hWe
For as flashy and mobile as Kyler Murray can be, he's also been very boring this year for Minnesota. That's been both good and bad, because while he has protected the ball and made smart throws, he's also been inaccurate at times and almost never pushes the ball downfield.
The Vikings are about to enter the teeth of their schedule with Detroit, Buffalo, Green Bay and San Francisco next month, and Murray isn't playing to the level the offense needs him to be yet after a hum-drum 150-yard performance this week.
Jake Golday played a season-high nine defensive snaps on Sunday, and his role looks to be expanding every week. His competition—Ivan Pace Jr.— has been trending the opposite direction , and if Golday can continue impressing during the week, he may carve out a respectable reserve role. The Vikings don't especially have a huge need for him right now, but the future starter is starting to get some valuable reps.
Yes, the Vikings are 6-0 and haven't lost a game in quite literally a calendar year, but it's also fair to question if Minnesota is winning in spite of their head coach on some level.
This is not a 'Fire Kevin O'Connell' post, as he has done a good job overall, but the handling of the J.J. McCarthy trade and leading an offense that is still struggling even in Week 7 deserve some criticism.
O'Connell is still the answer at head coach, but it's alarming, to say the least, that his offense will almost certainly be the reason the Vikings get booted from the playoffs.

title: Caleb Banks Injury Concerns Could Thrust Domonique Orange Into a Bigger Vikings' Role
full_text:
A major theme this season has been the Vikings' patience with their 2026 rookie class . While those rookies are growing and developing, the Purple and Gold have relied on their more experienced players on the roster to be major contributors.
That philosophy has had an interesting impact on first-round pick Caleb Banks and third-round pick Domonique Orange, who were selected to eventually replace last year's starters —Jonathan Allen and Javon Hargrave—after they were both released back in the offseason.
Former United Football League standout Jalen Redmond is having a fantastic season on Minnesota's defensive line and played 54 of Minnesota's 59 defensive snaps in Week 7. Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins had the next most defensive line snaps, playing 46 reps.
Banks and Orange played 12 and 13 defensive snaps, respectively, in Sunday's victory over the Colts . Since the Vikings are bringing them along slowly, the lower snap counts make sense from a development perspective.
However, Banks limped off the field against the Colts after being down and did not return to action. If he is forced to miss time with that injury, this could be an opportunity for "Big Citrus" to set more defensive work against the Lions in Week 8.
Orange has played 91 defensive snaps this year for Minnesota. Although he participates on special teams as well, he has four tackles this season, with one of those being for a loss against the Packers in the season opener. His 42.9 defense grade on Pro Football Focus is far from ideal , but three of his last four performances were higher than that mark. He's also averaged a run-defense grade of 57.4 in the last games after averaging 46.1 in the first two.
Assuming he doesn't play on Sunday, the 15.7 defensive snaps that Banks averages per game could be up for grabs.
Some of those could go to Orange, and if he can get about 25 defensive snaps against the Lions on Sunday, it could show how much he has developed since joining the team. That would be his career-high defensive snap count, besting his 24 reps against the Bears in Week 2.
The Lions run the fourth-most offensive players per game (66.3), so there should be more than enough opportunities to get on the field.
Developing Orange is even more important when looking at the long-term value of the defensive lineman. While staying on top of the NFC North or remaining undefeated is great, this team is in position to potentially be a scary playoff team, and having him as an asset to rotate into defensive coordinator Brian Flores's squad would be extremely valuable.
At only 22 years old, Orange should have a long NFL career in front of him. Getting him experience and evaluating his development in Week 8 could go a long way in preparing the young defender for a long and prosperous tenure with the Vikings.

title: Jakobe Thomas's Uphill Battle to Vikings Playing Time Became Steeper After Week 7
full_text:
It was extremely disappointing to see rookie defensive back Jakobe Thomas listed as one of the six players declared inactive for the Vikings' Week 7 victory over the Colts on Sunday .
Thomas' inactive designation follows the trend of him being sidelined for every game this season after joining the team as a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, meaning that he has never been active on game day since joining the team.
The 23-year-old safety has been patient in waiting for his opportunity to get on the field while others at his position struggled , but the solid play of his peers will make his case for playing time more difficult.
With Thomas inactive on the sideline, veteran Harrison Smith, versatile defender Josh Metellus, and fifth-year defensive back Theo Jackson all had good games against the Colts.
Smith had four tackles, half a sack, and the game-clinching interception. Meanwhile, Metellus finished second on the team in tackles, bringing down seven Colts ball carriers. Jackson tied for the third-most tackles on the team with five. They all graded well on Pro Football Focus , too :
Even fellow rookie S Jacob Thomas saw four defensive snaps, bringing his total to a modest 26 on the year.
These performances from Smith, Metellus, and Jackson take pressure off defensive coordinator Brian Flores and head coach Kevin O'Connell to make a change at safety. That will make Thomas's chances of being active in Week 8 on the road against the Lions, who average the second-most points (30.7) and total yards (397.3) per game this season.
Now, Thomas is in a position where he needs to continue working hard in practice to make a good impression on special teams coordinator Matt Daniels. Getting his foot in the door on special teams seems like the most logical way to earn a role on game day, even if it isn't the flashiest way to do it.
Interestingly, Thomas is one of only two rookies selected in the first 100 picks of the 2026 to be inactive for every game this season, with the other being Broncos defensive lineman Tyler Onyedim.
By now, Thomas has to be hungry to see some regular-season action. But the former Miami (FL) defensive back needs to continue to be patient until his opportunity comes. In the meantime, he can continue to learn a lot from players like Smith, Metellus and Jackson to be ready for when O'Connell, Flores & Co. give him the green light to be active on game day... eventually.

title: Patriots Host Feel-Good Halloween Costume Party for Pediatric Cancer Patients
full_text:
FOXBORO — For New England Patriots linebacker Benton Whitley, his Tuesday evening meant a little bit more. An off day from his time on the practice field, the 27-year-old — who grew up in Springfield and played his college ball at Holy Cross — traded in his pads for a Bullseye onesie.
He was one of 13 Patriots players who dressed up as Pixar characters for the team’s annual Halloween party for local pediatric cancer patients.
Nearly 40 children from Boston Children’s Hospital, Dana Farber Cancer Institute, Hasbro Children’s Hospital, Mass General Hospital and UMass Memorial Hospital made the trip for games, food and activities. A couple members of the MLS’s New England Revolution also came in costumes.
Whitley’s mother passed away in 2017 of cancer, so this event was extra important to him.
“This kind of hits close to home,” Whitley told Patriots On SI inside the Sports Illustrated Pavilion.
“I’m glad to do anything I can. … I feel like it just allows us to get out and meet some of the people who are supporting us in the stands, making our connection with the stadium and the community that much stronger.”
The Patriots entered the building set to cheers and a smoke machine. Some of them embraced the characters that they were dressed as. Linebacker Erick Hunter raised his fist proudly as Buzz Lightyear. Tight end Hunter Henry sped down the stairs like Lightning McQueen. Offensive tackle Walter Rouse, dressed as Russell from “Up,” had his own set of balloons.
Linebacker Robert Spillane , a father of two, came in his own Sully onesie and spoke about why he feels passionate about giving back.
“Young children who go through hardship, they deserve smiles,” Spillane told Patriots On SI. “They deserve opportunities to feel like kids. To go out there and just be a kid. And this is one of those nights where everyone’s dressed up, just having fun, enjoying the moment.”
The highlight of the day was when rookie tight end Tanner Arkin — dressed as Mr. Potato Head — faced off against a kid in Jenga. The game lasted for quite a while, drawing a massive crowd and cheers for both sides. Hunter grabbed the microphone to announce every move, and Rouse chimed in with some color commentary here and there.
Hunter might see himself with a future in broadcasting now.
“That wouldn’t be bad, I wouldn’t mind it,” Hunter told Patriots On SI. “I feel like I could do it. That was a good introduction right there.”
Whitley had some of his own tough battles, losing a game of cornhole.
“These kids are actually putting up a fight in the competition,” he laughed. “This is actually pretty cool.”
“This town ain't big enough for the two of us.” — Julian Ashby, probably pic.twitter.com/XMjdhpvrwr
Other players, like Julian Ashby , played checkers. Kids were also treated to decorating cookies, and designing tote bags and pumpkins. Players were happy to be stopped every which way for a picture or an autograph.
Between the white lines, the Patriots are sitting at 4-3 heading into a road Week 8 battle with the Miami Dolphins. But for one night a few days ahead of Halloween, the players were happy to make a difference off of the field.
“Seeing these kids come up to us with big smiles, realizing that we’re in costume, but we’re football players,” Spillane said. “That means something to them. Just seeing them smile today is what it’s all about.”
“New England is a special place,” Hunter said. “You can see why the way the organization is run is beautiful. It’s a beautiful place here.”

title: The Path to Production for Young Patriots WR Kyle Williams
full_text:
FOXBORO - Kyle Williams has seen increased playing time as injuries pile up in the New England Patriots' wide receiver room. However, that uptick hasn't translated into consistent on-field production, as Williams has recorded just six catches for 147 yards and a score through seven weeks.
Williams, the 69th pick in the 2025 NFL draft, entered 2026 with high expectations after a rookie season that showcased his game-breaking speed and deep-ball ability.
His development was a major storyline during summer training camp, even with a crowded WR room, as Williams reached the end zone in all three preseason matchups.
Tommy DeVito threw a dime and Kyle Williams never broke stride 😤 PHIvsNE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hkdcirz8nJ
Now, with Romeo Doubs (shoulder) and Mack Hollins (calf) sidelined on injured reserve , the Patriots need production from their remaining receivers more than ever, which raises an important question: How can New England get Williams more involved?
Williams' ability to stretch the field is well established. With his 4.40-second speed, he has the tools to threaten defenses over the top and create explosive downfield plays. It's what has made him such an enticing target on the boundary.
And while Williams has struggled on comeback routes (0/2 with one interception when targeted on routes returning to the line of scrimmage), the next step in his development could be finding ways to utilize that speed over the middle of the field.
Incorporating more crossing routes in the short and intermediate passing game could give Williams more opportunities to use his speed in open space. Instead of consistently asking him to beat defensive backs downfield, the Patriots could create easier opportunities for him to get the ball in his hands and make plays after the catch.
According to Pro Football Focus, Williams has caught all three of his targets between the numbers for 67 yards, an encouraging return that suggests there could be room to expand his role in that area of the field.
Increasing his opportunities in the middle of the field would also play into Williams' offseason training, as the wideout emphasized improving his lower-body strength to handle physical coverage, get off the line of scrimmage, and become more comfortable working across the middle.
“Play strength was definitely something that I wanted to emphasize,” Williams told the media. “I knew that I needed to get my lower half stronger and bulk up a little bit, coming across the middle, getting off press and all that type of stuff. So that was one of my biggest emphasis, mobility and just putting on a little weight.”
The Patriots invested a third-round pick in Williams for a reason. As opportunities open up in the receiving corps, finding creative ways to use his skill set could be the key to turning his increased playing time into reliable, consistent production.

title: True or False: Debunking Narratives Surrounding the 4-3 Patriots
full_text:
With three on the season, the New England Patriots have already accumulated the same amount of losses through seven weeks than they had in 17 weeks last year.
This New England team has far more holes this year than they had last year, which has created headlines across local and national media outlets. Here are some common threads with an analysis on the truth to each narrative:
One of the biggest struggles for the Patriots this season has been navigating a carousel of wide receiver injuries. New England has struggled to keep their new-look receiver room on the field. The Patriots have only been fully healthy at receiver for three quarters of play in 2026 — which came in Week 1 against Seattle.
They've placed A.J. Brown, Mack Hollins, and Romeo Doubs on the injured reserve, which is not only half of the rostered receivers, but their top-three receivers. With Brown's return in Week 6, the Patriots are limited to four wide receivers.
However, they've been able to manage an efficient passing game with just four active receivers. Josh McDaniels has intentionally created plays to utilize other weapons on the field. In last week's loss to Chicago, running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the Patriots' leading receiver. Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon have hauled in three touchdowns combined over the past three weeks.
With Hollins able to be activated as soon as Week 9 vs. the Packers, and Doubs able to return one week after that, stability will hopefully find the Patriots' receiving room soon.
Last Thursday, the Patriots rolled out their fifth and sixth-string guards to protect Drake Maye against the Bears defense. With guard being certainly their most injured position, many have taken the Patriots as buyers for another guard at the trade deadline.
With Quenton Nelson heading from Indianapolis to Seattle, the guard market is shaken up. While the Patriots will most likely show interest, acquiring a guard isn't a neccessity for this team.
The first reason in opposition of a trade is the likelihood that Ben Brown and Alijah Vera-Tucker return to play soon. Brown is still on the active roster after dealing with a knee injury, and Vera-Tucker can be activated in Week 12.
A larger reason to have faith in the offensive line is the dominance of both tackle positions. Will Campbell and Morgan Moses have provided elite protection for Maye. Additionally, Maye's strength in navigating the pocket comes from pressure up the middle. So long as the outside of the line is secure, pressure applied on Maye won't be an issue.
Second year running back TreVeyon Henderson has not started his sophomore season as excitingly he did his rookie year. Last year's leading rusher for New England has nearly a third less carries than Stevenson on the year, and saw half the amount of touches than his counterpart against Chicago.
In life, I struggle, I suffer, I’m tempted, I’m tested, sometimes I feel so weak. But when I am weak, I am strong. Because Christ, He is my hope, He is my strength, He is a firm foundation that never fails. Jesus is worthy of it all. May He be glorified always, not just on the… pic.twitter.com/uVWp8f8I6a
While Henderson has been the recepient of much criticism online, there are some caviats that factor into his on-field production. The Ohio State alum entered this season with an ankle injury suffered in training camp. In Week 6 against the Jets, Henderson sustained a new injury to the same ankle . The high ankle sprain that would usually land players on the injured reserve, didn't cause Henderson to miss anytime.
Considering his ability to play through the injury, his perfomance has certainly been impacted by it. Henderson is also the product of an offense that needs extra pass protection (see previous point) and Stevenson is better equipped to fill that need. The Patriots are still confident in their second-round pick from a year ago, and his 3.9 yards per carry, which are more than Stevenson, suggest that he'll remain an essential part of this offense.
New England's injury troubles have identified this team as one to utilize the trade deadline. They've had delve deep into their depth chart and practice squad to field a team in some weeks.
If the Colts are having a fire sale, Grover Stewart is the player I’m most interested in.
The trade deadline provides an opportunity for the Patriots to not be so reliant on their depth, and have temporary solutions to their holes. More specifically, New England could look at acquiring a linemen, cornerback, or linebacker.
However, if Mike Vrabel and Eliot Wolf choose to make a move, it will be for a temporary solution that addresses the teams depth. This means, fans shouldn't expect a big deal to be done with top trade deadline targets (such as RB Jonathan Taylor - IND, WR Quentin Johnston - LAC, or LB Nolan Smith - PHI).
The Patriots are a team that is still building their core. Draft picks are still a very essential resource for this young squad (especially considering the value they gave up for A.J. Brown). Unlike other high expectation teams like the Los Angeles Rams, the Patriots aren't in win-now mode, and don't have to overreact to three losses.
This current roster, while depleted, has shown that it compete with the best teams in the NFL.
Right now, the Patriots sit in second place in the AFC East, two wins behind the Buffalo Bills (5-1). In their Week 4 meeting, the Patriots got a leg up on the Bills, beating them in Buffalo, but Week 7's setback loss could put winning the division in jeopardy.
We certainly can't assume that Week 7 is the last loss the Patriots will take all season, but looking at Buffalo's remaining schedule, there are a lot of games that could go unfavorably for the Bills. Buffalo will travel to Minnesota (6-0), Denver (5-2), and Green Bay (4-3) and have to host Baltimore (4-3), Chicago (5-2) and Kansas City (5-1).
Noting that the Patriots and Bills are common opponents with each of these teams except for Baltimore, these six games could determine the AFC East. But none will be more influential than Week 13's game in Foxboro.
With New England having an easier strength of schedule remaining than the Bills , contention for a second straight AFC East title is more than possible.

title: Patriots Trade Deadline Tracker: Every Rumor for New England with 2 Weeks to Go
full_text:
The NFL's trade deadline was pushed back a week this year, so the New England Patriots and 31 other teams will have until Nov. 10 to try and get deals done this season.
The Patriots , currently sitting at 4-3 and in second place in the AFC East, could end up being active on the market. Injuries across the board and potential depth issues at other places could led Eliot Wolf and Mike Vrabel to try and improve the team somehow, someway.
Aleady in this calendar year, the Patriots have made a few trades. Back in March, they shipped away Garrett Bradbury and Marte Mapu before acquiring A.J. Brown in a block buster deal with the Philadelphia Eagles three months later. During the summer, Kayshon Boutte was dealth to the Houston Texans and during roster cuts, the Patriots also sent draft picks for Corey Kiner and Walter Rouse.
So could they end up making a deal mid-season? Here's all the rumors, quotes and storylines that are surrounding the Patriots as the trade deadline looms.
A few days after the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears , Vrabel spoke with reporters about how the team is stacking up prior to their Week 8 game with the Miami Dolphins. One of the questions posed was about if the Patriots will be active on the phones.
His answer left the door open for a deal being made, but the head coach also didn't officially dig a potential move into the sand. Like most coach-speak, Vrabel discussed how the Patriots would make moves to try and improve the overall roster in totality, and not try to single out a certain spot that needs upgrading.
"We're going to try to do everything we can to help the team," Vrabel said. "I don't know if we will or we won't. I would imagine that we'll try to do everything that we can to help us, within reason, and makes sense for us. I don't know how you want to interpret that, but I'm sure we'll listen and talk, just like everybody else does."
Some positions that the Patriots could end up attacking are running back, offensive guard (with a myriad of injuries hitting that group), interior defensive line and some backup cornerbacks.

title: Veteran OG Eligible to Return Off IR — Do Patriots Activate Him This Week?
full_text:
FOXBORO — Could the New England Patriots end up getting some help back this week against the Miami Dolphins? It's not out of the realm of possibilities.
Offensive guard Greg Van Roten , who has been on injured reserve for the last four game with a thigh injury, is eligible to return to the active roster this week. Speaking to reporters Monday afternoon, Mike Vrabel shared that the team has considered making that transaction this week.
"Probably won't see him today, but maybe this week, we'll see where that goes" the head coach said prior to practice. "I think him and (safety) Dell (Pettus) are eligible potentially to try and get back out there and kind of see where that goes, but we'll have to make a decision."
Van Roten is one of several offensive linemen who's gotten banged up this season. After Mike Onwenu broke his ankle in Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers, Van Roten stepped in to help fill that hole at right guard. He would practice as the starter all week in practice and start against the Jacksonville Jaguars the following game.
But Van Roten would get hurt in that game and be ruled out. He'd be replaced by converted tackle Walter Rouse, and was placed on IR two days later.
The Patriots have also seen Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Ben Brown (knee) get hurt in subsequent weeks. Last week against the Chicago Bears, the Patriots rolled with Rouse and Matt Pryor as their starting guards.
"I think the protection, I mean, I’m sure it could have been better. We just had some critical penalties," Vrabel said postgame. "Being able to handle the environment, third-and-short, whatever it may have been, and those are certainly unfortunate. That’s just beating ourselves. But I think I mean, I’m sure they played okay. I’m sure they played hard. Just without seeing it though it’s hard to say. But I know they competed."
Pryor has experience all over the offensive line and could earn a larger role if Van Roten doesn't return.
"Matt's done a nice job," Vrabel saaid. "Matt's come in, he's protected well. I think that he's still getting comfortable, but he's ... tough to get around. He's got heavy hands and he gives us a chance most of the time."
The Patriots could end up getting Brown back this week, as he suited up for practice as reporters were in the locker room. Should Van Roten return, he'll have three weeks to be activated to the 53-man roster or his season is over.
The Patriots will be back on the practice field in two days, which will be another opportunity for them to make a decision on the veteran guard. They also have one more week to make a decision on tackle Marcus Bryant, who's been designated to return off of IR with an ankle injury .

title: Patriots Release P Bryce Baringer from IR: Here's Why They Did It
full_text:
The New England Patriots are reportedly making a roster move on the special teams front.
As reported by NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Patriots are releasing veteran punter Bryce Baringer. The 27-year-old, who has been the team's top punter since being drafted in 2023, was currently on IR for an injury suffered in the preseason.
Baringer was the Patriots' sixth round pick in 2023 and won the job as a rookie. In the seasons that's followed, he punted in 51 games, tallying 219 total punts for 10,500 yards. He had not missed a game prior to his injury.
In the Patriots' second preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles, Baringer would leave the game and be replaced by rookie quarterback Behren Morton. He would be placed on IR as part of roster cuts, but without a designation to return.
All season, the Patriots have been struck by the injury bug — leaving a numbers crunch for them to deal with.
They're only permitted to have eight players return from IR in the middle of the season, and have already used two designations on wide receiver A.J. Brown and offensive tackle Marcus Bryant. Other players that are expected to contribute this year — including Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs, Alijah Vera-Tucker, Greg Van Roten and Dell Pettus — have all been put on IR and could return by the end of the season.
That means that the Patriots had to make a decision on Baringer , who was in the final year of his four-year rookie contract. Instead of letting him sit on the sidelines for the rest of the year, the Patriots do right by Baringer and releasing him. He's now free to sign with any other team.
Baringer was also one of several Patriots remaining who had played for Bill Belichick before he left after the 2023 season (Christian Gonzalez, DeMario Douglas, Marcus Jones, Rhamondre Stevenson, Brenden Schooler, Christian Elliss, Mike Onwenu, Hunter Henry, Christian Barmore and Jeremiah Pharms Jr. still remain with the organization).
Releasing Baringer leaves just Wishnowsky on the roster as the only punter. Wishnowsky, who signed with the Patriots' practice squad ahead of Week 1, has been the lone punter this season and has played relatively well.
Originally starting as a practice squad elevation, Wishnowsky was signed to the 53-man roster on Sept 22 . He's played in all seven games, punting the ball 22 times for 1,037 yards and three touchbacks.
Reports from Schultz and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport indicate that Baringer is fully healthy, meaning that the Patriots would have needed to move on from Wishnowsky if they wanted to bring Baringer up to the roster. It doesn't seem like Baringer would have lost the job had he not gotten injured, but it's hard to pull Wishnowsky out after he's been punting the ball well.
The Patriots have also reportedly made a move to their practice squad, re-signing edge rusher Jose Ramirez. They'll need to make room for him.

title: Calm Down Patriots Fans, A.J. Brown Will Be Just Fine — And Here's Why
full_text:
FOXBORO — A.J. Brown cost the New England Patriot s two draft picks, including a first rounder, this summer via trade. So far through three games, he hasn't lived up to that trade package — recording just nine receptions, 101 yards and no touchdowns.
Since returning from IR with his high-ankle sprain, Brown has only caught three passes against the New York Jets and Chicago Bears on 16 targets (including 10 in his return against New York). To put it bluntly, it hasn't worked out so far.
Head coach Mike Vrabel, speaking on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show, was asked about if he has any concerns for his top wideout as he looks to try and find more consistency on the field.
"No, I don’t have any concern," Vrabel said. "No."
Is it time to panic about Brown? Like Vrabel said, no. The former Pro Bowler will be able to figure it out and start stacking up some good days — but he'll need to do it soon. This week, the Patriots will play host to the Miami Dolphins, who won their first game of the season yesterday. It's a very winnable game for the Patriots and a real opportunity for Brown to make his mark.
During the summer, his budding connection with Drake Maye was one of the many highlights of training camp. Brown's ability to go up for balls and come down with them was going to be a godsend for this offense. It hasn't come to fruition yet.
Against the Jets, Brown caught three balls — while dropping several more. That performance alone got him plenty of grief online, but it was clear the rust was being shaken off (even though Brown won't say that).
"I thought that he dropped a few passes, and then the other night there was a contested catch that — I’ve seen him make those plays in the past, I’ve seen those plays get called for DPI, and I’ve seen those plays be good plays by the defense down the field," Vrabel said. "So, I don’t think anybody has to press here or anything else. I think we just have to get back into a rhythm offensively with the guys that we have."
Exactly. The Patriots offense, one that was a bit out of sorts against the Jets and very streaky one week later, needs to start firing on all cylinders. Injuries at the wide receiver position (Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs are both on IR) haven't helped, but that's why Brown is here.
But the reason to be confident in Brown is centered around his quarterback. Maye is playing some great football right now and has seemed to break out of his early season struggles. Now, instead of playing sloppy football, the 24-year-old is making play after play after play .
A lot of those plays have gone to Rhamondre Stevenson , Hunter Henry, Eli Raridon and DeMario Douglas — all players who haven't missed extended time with injuries. Brown could easily join that party.
His slow start won't last all season. Sooner or later, he'll break out and grab 100+ receiving yards and a touchdown. Maybe it's this week at home.

title: Most Important Patriots Postgame From Week 7 — And What They Mean Going Forward
full_text:
Sitting at 4-3, the New England Patriots aren't lighting the NFL on fire. But they've played well in their wins, and in their Thursday Night Football loss to the Chicago Bears , they also had enough chances to try and win the game.
Instead, a Superman effort from the Bears offense — mainly Caleb Williams and Luther Burden III — sent the Patriots home with a 30-24 defeat. It was a game that the Patriots could have pulled away in, but too many opportunities went to the wayside.
"I think it's hard to say, 'Shoulda. Woulda. Coulda.' I definitely think we — I'm proud of the guys for the effort," Drake Maye said. "I think we did some good things and we got a lot of stuff to clean up. And we got to get back from the rest this weekend and get back after we had another one on the road, a division game."
Here are some of the biggest postgame quotes from the Patriots , both from the podium and inside the locker room, after their primetime loss to Caleb Williams and the Bears.
For most of the game, the Patriots trailed. They got behind big in the first half, but Rhamondre Stevenson's heroics to close the opening frame got them within a score. But the Bears roared out of the locker room to another scoring drive. It continued to be back-and-forth, but the Patriots were just one step away for most of the game.
Mike Vrabel on the offense's productivity: "We moved it however we needed to move it and sometimes you are going to have days like that. I thought we'd be able to run it a little better. We didn't, but then our best players were putting the ball in good spots most of the time and making good decisions. That's how it goes, we'd have liked to run the ball a little bit better. But, it didn't happen tonight."
Drake Maye on his end zone interception: "Yeah, I mean, we hit the same thing, the same exact play, it was later in the game. So, I like my chances in there and just — yeah, it's frustrating. So I know that was a big turning point in the game and I know I let my team down."
Christian Gonzalez on dealing with an illness throughout the game: "I woke up and I though it was allergies, and it was a lot more. ... It ain't none at the end of the day."
Hunter Henry on rookie tight end Eli Raridon: "(He's) great, man. Just continuing to get better and growing that confidence. A lot of fun to play with."
A.J. Brown on how he saw Chicago's defense attack him: "I think they did a really good job. Early on, (offensive coordinator) Josh (McDaniels) tried to do a really good job of getting me involved and Drake just was taking what they were giving. They were trying to take me away early on, and that's just kind of how the game played."
Charles Woods on the difficulty of defending Caleb Williams: "Anytime a quarterback that's mobile as him gets out the pocket, they definitely put stress on DBs. Then we have to cover the second play."
The Patriots played two games in five days, and looked worn down — especially after all the injuries that struck. They certainly needed the three days off that they were given this weekend.
But now a new challenge emerges, and it's about bouncing back to play a winnable game against the Miami Dolphins. As it stands right now, the Dolphins sit in the cellar of the AFC East with a 0-5 record and really don't look like they have anything going for them long term.
After a loss against a Super Bowl-like team in Chicago, the Patriots can't afford to look past a team that should beat without any issues. It starts with Maye playing clean football again, the defense wrapping up and making the tackles they need to and the offense capitalizing on their opportunities.
We'll see in a week's time if the Patriots were able to flush the primetime loss and get back into the win column.

title: Patriots Legend Pokes Fun at Christian Gonzalez's Uniform Number
full_text:
There might not be a position for the New England Patriots that's so consistently good every single season more than the cornerback position. Ever since their days in the American Football League, the Patriots have always seemed to have a shutdown cornerback.
That trend has carried over to the present day, as Christian Gonzalez has cemented himsrlf as the latest addition to the shutdown cornerback lineage. But still, there's one thing that makes him stand out from the rest ... and it's drawn some jokes from another member of that cornerback fraternity.
Ty Law, arguably the greatest Patriots cornerback of all time and a Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee, kicked off the team's unofficial theme of the top cornerback wearing No. 24. Since Law donned the number as the Patriot's first round draft choice in 1995, Super Bowl champions Darrelle Revis (2014) and Stephon Gilmore (2017-2020) also wore it.
It's become part of the fabric of New England. Instead of retiring the number for Law, the Patriots have had it passed on. But Gonzalez — who certainly could stack up — blazed his own path, choosing No. 0 as his jersey in 2024.
That drew some jokes from Law this week.
On the fourth episode of "Forged in Foxborough," Law spoke about Gonzalez — who was seen signing his record-setting four-year, $135 million contract extension — and his choice of uniform numbers.
"Because of the success that I had with the number, 24, everybody's always gonna compare to me," said Law, who was inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame in 2014.
"Then you had Darrelle Revis. He come in, 24. Super Bowl. Then you got Stephon Gilmore, 24. We were all those type of corners and we just happened to all be wearing the same number. Christian Gonzalez, yeah, he broke the rule dammit, you supposed to be wearing 24 Christian."
Gonzalez's career has been filled with a lot of uniform numbers. After being assigned No. 50 during his first training camp, he donned No. 19 in the preseason. Then the regular season hit, and he wore No. 6 for the first few games of his career.
He would miss most of the season with a torn labrum, and then become the first Patriots player ever to wear No. 0 the following year. When Gonzalez was drafted in 2023, Joshuah Bledsoe was wearing No. 24. He'd be released the following summer and undrafted rookie Dell Pettus would end up taking it (he's still wearing it to this day).
"He's making his name on his own right being the same type of player," Law continued. "Outside of Christian not wearing 24, that's a bad boy. He's gon' start his own thing."
Gonzalez has been off to a great start to his 2026 season, playing in five games and racking up 15 tackles and five pass breakups. He's yet to grab his first interception, but limited stars Jaxon Smith-Njigba and D.K. Metcalf in his matchups against them.
He's been a major part of a Patriots defense that's been the best part of the team seven weeks in. His contract extension, the largest in franchise history, got done before Week 1 in Seattle — helping set the tone for how the team wants to lock down their homegrown talents.
"We're excited to have him for hopefully a long time," head coach Mike Vrabel said.
Law, Revis and Gilmore all won Super Bowls with the Patriots, and now it's up to Gonzalez to join that elite group — this time with his own uniform number.
