title: Steelers Two Biggest Strengths Can Carry Them - Hopefully
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- At 5-2, things are looking pretty good for the Pittsburgh Steelers. After a 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France, the team returns to the United States for a showdown against the Cleveland Browns.
As the Steelers try to jump to the top of the AFC North standings and exact revenge against the Browns for an earlier loss, the team is buzzing. The defense is a top-10 unit and the offense has a legitimate candidate for MVP.
Armed with a potent running attack and a stout defense, the Steelers could be set for a run in 2026. But that's only if they can address and correct a few key issues over the coming weeks.
No running back has exploded this season in the NFL like Jaylen Warren. He is currently seventh in the NFL in rushing yards with 561 on 102 carries. He's averaging 5.5 yards per carry, but he's doing most of his damage after contact. As a pass-catcher, he's just as dynamic, with 24 receptions and 294 yards.
There's no doubting that Warren is having an MVP-caliber season. The 27-year-old running back is putting together a career year and he's carrying the Steelers' offense along the way.
This is where things get tricky, however, for two reasons. The first is durability. Warren has proven to be durable over his five seasons in the NFL, but he's been banged up along the way. That's already been the case this season, as he's dealt with shoulder injuries early on.
Finding the right usage is key for Warren. The Steelers may have struck that balance in Week 7. With Rico Dowdle back on the field, they were able to steer some carries his way and keep Warren fresh all game long. If they can continue that one-two punch in the backfield, the run game will continue to fuel this team's success.
The passing game, however, is very much a work in progress. The game plan this year is basically forcing the ball to DK Metcalf. He has 58 targets, 25 more than the next-most targeted player (Jaylen Warren, of course), and the aerial attack continues to be one-dimensional. When Metcalf makes a big play, the pass game seems fine. When that doesn't happen, however, the passing game feels as inept as it did in 2025.
And defenses know that. They are forcing the Steelers to take deep shots on the outside, and it's not resulting in the productive plays the offense hopes for. The dink-and-dunk approach helped the Steelers win a few games so far, but it's not a recipe for long-term success. The Steelers have to improve this area of offense, or else the rest of it will suffer.
Week 7 was another strong performance from the defense, continuing an early-season trend for the Steelers. Under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, this group has gotten off to an impressive start. Through the first seven weeks, the defense ranks sixth in yards allowed per game, 11th in pass yards per game, seventh in rush yards allowed per game and fifth in points allowed per game. Their 18 team sacks are the 10th-most in the NFL so far, and they have the eighth-best turnover differential in the league.
By all accounts and statistics, this defense is better than it was last year.
There is one area that has not improved, however, and that is foot speed in the secondary. The defense played a great game against the Saints in Week 7, but the lack of speed and coverage skills led to many of the big plays New Orleans posted and the lone touchdown they recorded.
If the Saints picked up on it, what happens when a much better team does the same? It could create problems for Graham's defense that even his savviness cannot overcome.
Entering Week 8, the Steelers have the chance to sit atop the AFC North standings. They also have the chance to change the narrative in Pittsburgh, but they have to correct these two major concerns. Otherwise, this team could be setting themselves up for another repeat of recent history.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Former Steelers HC Mike Tomlin Doesn't Hold Back About Najee Harris Release
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin is having a blast in his post-coaching career. As an analyst for Football Night in America, he has been one of the most entertaining voices on television. It's something the Steelers are all too familiar with, as Tomlin was one of the most charismatic presences in the NFL during his 19-season run as Pittsburgh's head coach.
No longer tied to the Steelers or beholden to a contract the NFL pays, Tomlin has become unfiltered for the better. During his program's coverage of the Kansas City Chiefs and Seattle Seahawks Week 7 matchup, Tomlin addressed the New York Giants' improving run game. He dropped a classic Tomlin line when describing Giants head coach John Harbaugh's recent moves as "killing a mosquito with an axe," but it was his comments on former New York and Pittsburgh running back Najee Harris that really caught attention.
After Harris voiced his displeasure with the running scheme, the Giants released the former Steelers first-round pick. Tomlin, who coached the running back his first four years in the NFL, called out Harris and said the Giants sent a message after he spoke out.
"Najee Harris spoke out about a lack of rhythm in run/carry opportunities," he said. "And now he’s unemployed. Message sent. You can always ease up and be buddy-buddy. I just think it's important at the early stages to establish a rapport, and that's what he's (Giants HC John Harbaugh) doing."
"Killing a mosquito with an ax." Mike Tomlin had an all-time quote when describing the Giants' improvement in their run game this week. 🤣 pic.twitter.com/hOkCZLem8Y
The comments are equally hilarious and illuminating. In his first year with the Giants, Harbaugh is trying to institute his schemes and culture. It's very similar to the process the Steelers are undergoing with Mike McCarthy running the show.
Harbaugh took heat for the team's rushing struggles earlier in the season. Things came to a head when Cam Skattebo, the team's most impactful running back, was held without a rushing carry in Week 6.
The Giants received that spark in Week 7, however. Skattebo posted 124 yards and Devin Singletary posted an additional 41 yards, while Harris watched from home.
And Tomlin's comments could be taken as a shot directly at Harris, but I don't see it that way. Tomlin didn't criticize Harris's character or call him a bad teammate or anything like that. Instead, his comments were focused on what a head coach has to do to establish control of his locker room.
The truth is that it takes some shocking moves. Sometimes you have to release a running back for questioning the team's plans in the run game. Even if Harris held no ill intentions with his recent comments, Harbaugh made an example out of him.
You can't argue with the results. Maybe it was overkill, like killing a mosquito with an axe. But it also helped the Giants win and extend their record to 4-2-1 through the first seven games. Tomlin spoke the ugly part out loud during Sunday Night Football on NBC, something he frequently did as the Steelers' head coach for such a long time.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Should Call Colts About WR Trade
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers appear to be buyers as the NFL Trade Deadline nears. How could they not be after jumping out to a 5-2 record and a share of the AFC North lead?
The Steelers aren't perfect, however, and there remains plenty of work for the players, the coaching staff, as well as the general manager. At the top of general manager Omar Khan's priority list is upgrading a few key positions on both sides of the ball. On offense, no position is more precious or important than wide receiver. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers needs more options to get the passing game going and get to the place head coach Mike McCarthy envisioned.
Luckily for the Steelers, another AFC team is operating like they are going out of business. The Indianpolis Colts are heading for another rebuild, and the latest domino to fall was sending beloved offensive guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks for third-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft and a 2028 fifth-round draft choice. It's clear the Colts are willing to make a deal, and the Steelers need to strike while the iron is hot to upgrade their wide receiver position.
It's time the Steelers dialed up the Colts about a Josh Downs trade.
The Steelers have an obvious need for more talent at the wide receiver position , but it goes beyond just adding another player without regard to what skillset they provide. A player like Downs is an ideal fit for this team's offense for multiple reasons.
The first is the way he complements the current group. DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard have plenty of positive qualities, but one area the entire depth chart has struggled is creating separation. Both in short and deep, it's been a challenge for receivers to get open, forcing Rodgers to make his passes with pinpoint accuracy.
What the team needs is someone who can separate from a defender immediately off the line of scrimmage. Josh Downs is a player who can do just that. The 25-year-old pass-catcher has eclipsed 550 receiving yards in each of his first three NFL campaigns, but it's his ability to play in the slot that should have the Steelers so intrigued.
Primarily a slot pass-catcher in Indianapolis, Downs gives the Steelers a playmaker in the middle of the field and flexibility. It allows Bernard to flex around the line of scrimmage, while also giving Roman Wilson a spot on the outside when he returns from Injured Reserve.
The second, and perhaps more important reason, that Downs fits the Steelers' needs is his speed. The scouting reports are mixed about his upside, but no one disagrees about his foot speed. The Steelers would love to add that burst to their offensive attack, and they might finally be willing to cough up some draft capital to bring Downs in.
After trading Nelson, it sent a signal to the rest of the NFL. The Colts are trying to stockpile draft picks for their rebuilding process. If they took a day two and three pick for the team's top offensive lineman, they won't be charging a high price to offload one of their talented receivers.
Downs is now the top wide receiver on the trade block, and he's not happy with the Colts.
He's not a superstar player by any means, but he is a player with a history of producing. With more opportunity in Pittsburgh, he could give the Steelers a wide receiver group that Rodgers finally feels comfortable with and trusting in. As the Trade Deadline approaches, it's time for the Steelers to make a call and bring Downs to Pittsburgh.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Two New WR Trade Names Floated for Steelers
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers appear to be scouring the market for a considerable upgrade at wide receiver ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.
NFL insider Jason La Canfora anticipates that the Steelers, "will make a move or two by the trade deadline," and that the team's brass, "understands that adding another playmaker to this offense—even after making a bold trade for DK Metcalf from Seattle—is likely in order."
In terms of Pittsburgh's potential targets, La Canfora noted that one scout believes Ladd McConkey and Brian Thomas Jr. are both names worth noting over the next few weeks.
"After decades of operating as a conservative front office, the Steelers are wheeler-dealers now," La Canfora wrote. "One scout suggested to me that someone like Chargers wideout Ladd McConkey might be the kind of target Rodgers would enjoy throwing to to help sustain drives. Brian Thomas Jr. of the Jaguars is another name to keep an eye on."
Pittsburgh's run game is among the best in the NFL, courtesy of Jaylen Warren. He is seventh in rushing yards with 561 and fourth in scrimmage yards with 855 while Rico Dowdle is about as strong of a second option as there is in the league, evidenced by his 86 yards on 15 touches in the team's Week 7 win over the New Orleans Saints.
The passing game looks better than it has in several years under first-year head coach Mike McCarthy. Aaron Rodgers has turned back the clock a bit and has performed at a relatively high level, Germie Bernard has shown flashes of being a star in his rookie season, and DK Metcalf has recorded a combined 276 yards over his last four games after a slow start to the year.
The Steelers have dealt with a slew of injuries at the wide receiver position, however, with both Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) landing on the reserve/injured list over the last several weeks while Ben Skowronek (calf) has missed two games in a row as well.
Pittman Jr. in particular seems likely to remain out for a prolonged period of time beyond his required absence of four games while on IR, and Wilson isn't eligible to be activated until Week 11 at the earliest.
As a result, there's a clear need for another playmaker at receiver in Pittsburgh. For as good as Rodgers has looked relative to expectations too, he has completed just seven of his 36 attempts on passes of 20-plus yards (per SumerSports ).
Bringing in a receiver who can consistently separate and help generate explosive plays is a near necessity for the Steelers if they want to get into the playoffs and make some noise should they get there instead of losing an eighth-straight postseason contest.
Pittsburgh's defense is firmly a top-10 unit in the league. If the offense can follow suit and take some real steps forward in-season by adding another proven receiver, there's no telling the heights this team could potentially reach.
In five games this season for what's proven to be an anemic Chargers offense, McConkey has logged 200 yards on 13 catches.
Thomas Jr., meanwhile, continues to keep slipping down the depth chart in Jacksonville and has recorded 105 yards on nine receptions over six contests.
Of the two, McConkey is the higher-floor option for Pittsburgh. He's primarily a slot receiver, though he can certainly split out wide, and he's at his best in the short and intermediate areas of the field.
He's also proven to be a bit of a threat with the ball in his hands (340 yards after the catch since 2025, per SumerSports ), and he doesn't have many drops on his ledger.
McConkey isn't overly explosive, though, and would be more of a safety blanket for Rodgers rather than a big play waiting to happen.
The opposite is true with Thomas Jr. His stock has dropped a ton since his standout rookie campaign in 2024, during which he finished with 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns.
Since Liam Coen was hired as the Jaguars' head coach ahead of the 2025 season, Thomas Jr. has put up 812 yards and three touchdowns in 20 games.
Thomas Jr. is still a star-level talent, he just has not been nearly as productive as expected following his rookie year. He's 20th in yards after the catch with 728 since entering the league (per SumerSports) despite his relative struggles over the past two years, and his average depth of target of 12.66 yards across his career shows that he could be a real asset for the Steelers in terms of putting an emphasis on pushing the ball downfield.
If Pittsburgh is looking for a reliable receiver to pair with its current corps, McConkey is a better solution than Thomas Jr.
At the same time, Thomas Jr. comes with a super high ceiling and could benefit from a change of scenery with the Steelers , which may help unlock his potential.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Worst Offensive Lineman is Surprising
full_text:
There were certainly a couple of question marks about the Pittsburgh Steelers ' offensive line coming into the season, but Troy Fautanu wasn't one of them.
The 2024 first-round pick was super reliable for the Steelers last season after appearing in just one game as a rookie due to a knee injury, and the expectation was that he'd take further steps forward in 2026 while moving from right tackle to left tackle.
While there's been some flashes from Fautanu, his transition to left tackle hasn't been smooth to say the least, and he just turned in arguably his worst performance of the year in a 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris.
A vast majority of Fautanu's reps in pass protection vs. New Orleans were against Chase Young, which is bad news for most offensive tackles.
The 2020 AP Defensive Rookie of the Year, Young has found a home with the Saints and become one of the better pass rushers across the NFL.
Young certainly proved that to Fautanu, who allowed two sacks and four total pressures against him over 25 total reps in pass protection (per SumerSports ).
Fautanu shut out Anfernee Jennings, Cameron Jordan and Kaden Elliss over a combined nine reps between the three, but that wasn't nearly enough to negate his shortcomings against Young.
According to Pro Football Focus , Fautanu has given up 20 pressures and four sacks through seven games this season.
Considering he was credited with allowing just 31 pressures and three sacks for Pittsburgh over 17 games in 2025, it's easy to come away with the opinion that Fautanu has regressed upon moving positions and playing under a new coaching staff.
Per PFF, Fautanu had never allowed two sacks in a single game either before Young accomplished that feat against him.
At the same time, he deserves some grace given all of those previously mentioned factors. Fautanu did not give up a sack between Weeks 3 and 5, so there is reason to believe he could become a true stalwart at left tackle as long as he develops some consistency there.
As the rest of the offensive line has improved, though, especially once Brock Hoffman and Max Iheanachor were inserted into the starting lineup in Week 3, Fautanu has now regressed after the initial returns were pretty strong when that change was initially made by Pittsburgh.
There's a clear learning curve to switch sides of the line and it's possible the Steelers will just have to contend with some general volatility from Fautanu for the rest of the season.
He's far too talented to completely write off, and he's previously shown that he can produce at a high level. If Fautanu doesn't bounce back from his poor showing against the Saints and make some real strides over the back half of the season, though, then it may be time to have some real discussions about his future in Pittsburgh.

title: Steelers Injury Situation Finally Trending in Right Direction
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are finally trending in the right direction in more ways than one. The team won their fifth game of the season, taking down the New Orleans Saints in an international contest.
Now, the Steelers turn their focus to the Cleveland Browns in Week 8. The goal is to capture their sixth victory and even the season series against the Browns.
In that Week 8 contest, the Steelers will play a bit shorthanded. With multiple key players on the Injured Reserve, the team will have to dig deep to find that win. Thankfully, the team is improving week after week, and the schedule is only helping this team navigate their early-season injury troubles.
The Steelers had plenty of injury scares heading to Paris, France, for their Week 7 battle. A day before their flight departed, edge rusher T.J. Watt popped up on the team's injury report with a calf ailment. He was just the latest of multiple players dealing with various ailments of different severities.
Thakfully, those scares didn't continue after the game. Watt made it through unscathed, as did the rest of the lineup. Head coach Mike McCarthy confirmed in his weekly press conference that there were no other major injuries coming out of their international meeting.
The team also had one of their most positive injury developments in Week 7. Safety DeShon Elliott returned after almost a year due to a lower-body injury. He played in a limited number of snaps, but it was huge to get the star safety back in any capacity.
It was exactly what the Steelers needed.
The good news for the Steelers is that the schedule has been on their side. Over the past few weeks, the regular season schedule has been quite favorable for Pittsburgh. Taking on opponents like the Indianapolis Colts, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the New Orleans Saints, a trio of inferior competition allowed the Steelers to easily weather the storm of injuries.
Following this Week 8 game, the Steelers will walk into their bye week. It comes at a sorely needed time, with players like wide receiver Roman Wilson and defensive tackle Derrick Harmon nearing the end of the four required games missed on IR.
Wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. may also return this season, but reports from Pat McAfee Show corospondent Mark Kaboly say there's a chance Pittman Jr. misses the rest of the year.
For head coach Mike McCarthy, things are finally coming together. In his mind, the roster is in great shape. As they wait for a few pieces to return, McCarthy is confident that their mix of players gives the Steelers what they need for a run in 2026.
"We've got the right guys," he said during his weekly press conference .  "We've got a really great mix of veterans and young guys, and you're just seeing it come together."
And it's all coming together without critical pieces like Wilson and Harmon. Add in veterans Michael Pittman Jr. and Sebastian Joseph-Day and their unknown return timelines, and this team is trending in the right direction health-wise at the perfect time.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Missing Piece to Being Serious Contenders
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have once again gotten off to a strong start.
Entering a crucial Week 8 matchup with the Cleveland Browns, the Steelers are sitting at 5-2 and currently own the No. 6 seed in the AFC.
In the midst of a three-game win streak that it'll look to push to four before its Week 9 bye, it's not hard to feel optimistic about what stands ahead of Pittsburgh this season.
At the same time, if they want to be considered real contenders in the conference, the Steelers do have some clear needs that must be addressed.
Their biggest missing piece is evident, too, and it'll come as no surprise to anyone.
Pittsburgh was active in filling its hole at wide receiver this offseason by acquiring Michael Pittman Jr. from the Indianapolis Colts and selecting Germie Bernard in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft.
Bernard has certainly panned out thus far, recording 254 yards and a touchdown while making three starts. Pittman Jr., on the other hand, was placed on the reserve/injured list with a foot injury ahead of the Steelers' Week 5 game against the Indianapolis Colts and seems incredibly unlikely to return at the earliest possible date, which would be in Week 10 after he misses the required minimum of four games.
Roman Wilson (finger) also landed on IR in the lead-up to Week 6, and Ben Skowronek (calf) has missed two contests in a row as well.
DK Metcalf has bounced back after a rough start to the year, posting a combined 276 yards over his past four games, but he hasn't proven himself to be a true No. 1 receiver in a Pittsburgh uniform up to this point.
The Steelers' offense has been incredibly conservative during the 2024 and 2025 seasons with former offensive coordinator Arthur Smith calling the plays, and that has remained true under first-year head coach Mike McCarthy.
Through seven games, Aaron Rodgers ' average depth of target of 7.42 yards ranks No. 21 among 34 quarterbacks with at least 100 dropbacks this season (per SumerSports ).
His 61.6 percent completion rate and -0.13 EPA/pass both rank No. 25 under that same criteria, and his big time throw rate of 3.2 percent (per Pro Football Focus ) is tied for No. 22.
Rodgers has just seven completions over 36 attempts on passes of 20-plus yards (per SumerSports), which comes out to a 19.4 percent completion rate that comes in as the fifth-worst mark in the NFL.
The future Hall of Famer has played pretty well overall, but Pittsburgh is still severely lacking any semblance of an explosive passing game, which will hold it back long-term.
Getting Wilson back at some point should help in that regard, and he would make up a decent enough trio with Metcalf and Bernard. Still, the Steelers would really benefit from adding a dynamic playmaker at receiver who can separate and generate big plays consistently.
Finding a player who fits that bill at the trade deadline is easier said than done. With that being said, however, paying whatever it costs and taking a chance on someone like Brian Thomas Jr. is the exact type of high-reward move Pittsburgh has to seriously consider.
Thomas Jr. has taken a huge step back over the past two seasons since the Jacksonville Jaguars brought Liam Coen in as their head coach, but the 2024 first-round pick proved he has star-level talent after posting 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie.
Other options that could intrigue the Steelers include Quentin Johnston (Los Angeles Chargers), Jerry Jeudy (Cleveland Browns), Dontayvion Wicks (Philadelphia Eagles) and Stefon Diggs (Washington Commanders), though none of them offer as high of a ceiling as Thomas Jr. would.
It is hard to build an explosive passing game around a 42-year-old quarterback who's in the middle of his final season, though the Steelers have to make a concerted attempt to do just that.
They have a fantastic run game with Jaylen Warren leading the way as one of the top running backs in the league, and if they can start leaning on their pass game more by adding a legit receiver before the trade deadline, their offense has a chance to do some real damage moving forward.
If Pittsburgh is going to snap its seven-game losing streak in the postseason and make some noise as a contender in the AFC, doing so is an absolute necessity.
From the moment the Steelers put an end to the Joey Porter Jr. saga by trading him to the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4, there was always a possibility that cornerback would become an area of concern.
Jamel Dean is capable of being the team's No. 1 corner, though Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette are volatile options next to the former on the boundary. Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terell Smith were solid veteran additions as depth pieces, but neither should be expected to step in and play at a high level if called upon.
For that reason, a trade for a proven starter who can play opposite Dean would make sense for Pittsburgh.
The other position group that could potentially use reinforcements to help the Steelers become more of a complete team and have a chance of competing with the AFC's top squads is inside linebacker.
Payton Wilson has made some strides in his third NFL season , and Patrick Queen is coming off his best game in quite some time in Pittsburgh's Week 7 victory over the New Orleans Saints.
That tandem has fallen short often, however, and while Elandon Roberts may eventually factor into the team's plans while currently residing on the practice squad, a more consequential move to bring in a real difference-maker could pay dividends for the Steelers' defense.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers Sets New Record in Win Over Saints
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers were victorious in their Week 7 contest over the New Orleans Saints, defeating their NFC South opponent by a final score of 16-10. The Steelers return home with a 5-2 record and plenty of work to do before they meet the Cleveland Browns in Week 8.
The Steelers mustered a single touchdown in the win, but the offense showed signs of life. A 51-yard bomb from quarterback Aaron Rodgers to wide receiver DK Metcalf was the deep ball the offense has been trying to connect on for the past year and a half. Running back Jaylen Warren ran all over the Saints defense, putting up 137 total yards.
That pass to Metcalf carried more significance than helping the Steelers put points on the board. When the wideout hauled in that deep pass from Rodgers, it was the 95th time that the 42-year-old QB has thrown a completion of 50 yards or more. With that completion, he became the NFL's new all-time leader in that statistic.
What Rodgers and the Steelers care about the most is the explosive play he and Metcalf combined for. As nice as it is to have the recognition of being the first all-time on a list like 50+ yard completions, Rodgers is likely smiling about the breakthrough that the offense finally had.
The big knock on the Steelers, even throughout this current winning streak, is their offense lacks splash. And that is predominantly true, as Rodgers has found a way to succeed with the dink-and-dunk approach.
But on that deep pass to Metcalf, Rodgers used the bait of playing around the line of scrimmage to open up a shot downfield for his top receiver.
And hopefully, that pass unlocked something. Aside from Metcalf, the Steelers have rookie Germie Bernard trying to show his elusiveness in open space. Third-year pass-catcher Roman Wilson is currently on the Injured Reserve, but when he returns, the Steelers might have even more use for his speed on the outside.
That 51-yard pass to Metcalf was a record-setting one for Rodgers, but more importantly, it was a tone-setting pass for the offense in a crucial victory.
Aaron Rodgers is bound for the Hall of Fame. The Super Bowl winner and four-time MVP has put together one of the most illustrious careers of any NFL quarterback.
It's not like Rodgers needed another achievement to earn his place in Canton, Ohio, but this is yet another feather in the cap of the 42-year-old. He can add it to the long list of accolades to celebrate when he is enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Might Have Their Answer at LB
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers may have a long-term solution at inside linebacker.
The entire position group has largely underperformed since the beginning of the 2025 season, with both Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson being the biggest culprits.
That tandem has started to turn things around, however, and while Queen deserves his fair share of credit after how well he played in Pittsburgh's 16-10 Week 7 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, it's Wilson who has really taken the reins.
The 2024 second-round pick still isn't a finished product, but he's shown flashes of becoming a star in the middle of the Steelers ' defense.
Since training camp, Wilson has turned heads with how he's flown around the field and made plays in Patrick Graham's defense.
That's carried over to the regular season, and the strides he's made as a run defender has been evident as well. Wilson's not exactly polished in that aspect of his game, but it's still a far cry from how he performed in 2024 and 2025.
In a game where Pittsburgh held New Orleans to just 18 yards on 17 rushing attempts, Wilson was consistently around the ball and was paramount to the Steelers' success in shutting down the Saints' ground game.
The 26-year-old's biggest play of the game came in coverage, though. Tyler Shough had been carving up the Steelers' defense through the air, particularly underneath, and drove New Orleans down to Pittsburgh's 10-yard line while trailing 13-10 about halfway through the third quarter.
Wilson put an end to the Saints' 14-play drive, however, by jumping a throw to Chris Olave and returning it to the Steelers' 29-yard line.
Payton Wilson anticipates the pass perfectly and picks off Shough in the red zone PITvsNO on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7QIPlOfibh
New Orleans did not score for the rest of the game, and Wilson's clutch interception is one of the main reasons why Pittsburgh was able to come away with the win at the Stade de France.
Wilson's deficiencies against the run really held him back over the first two years of his NFL career, during which he was largely viewed as a good coverage linebacker and not much else.
He's ever-so-slightly starting to shift that narrative, though, given how he's improved as a run defender. On the flip side, Wilson has allowed the fourth-most receiving yards (258, per SumerSports ) among linebackers with at least 250 snaps this season.
The 26-year-old clearly has the tools to be a well above-average coverage defender, as evidenced by his interception off of Shough, though consistency is a bit of an issue for him as of now.
Furthermore, Wilson's missed tackle rate of 14.9 percent is the 10th-worst amongst linebackers with a minimum of 250 snaps (per SumerSports).
He's grown into an exciting player who's developing into a stronger run defender, and his standout athletic traits for the position provide him with a high ceiling.
Wilson still has to put all of the pieces together, namely in terms of continuing to grow against the run and being more steady in coverage, but there's reasons to believe he could stick around for a prolonged period of time in Pittsburgh.

title: One Change Has Sparked Steelers' Offense
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are 5-2 following their 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints. After a whirlwind of a weekend that saw the team fly to Paris, France, play a football game, and fly back to Pittsburgh, this team enters Week 8 exhausted but full of momentum.
Sitting at the top of the AFC North standings, the Steelers now shift focus to the Cleveland Browns, their Week 8 opponent and divisional rival. The Steelers will have to find a way to overcome a nasty Cleveland defense that has helped them also jump out to a 5-2 record.
It's a clash of strengths between these two foes. The Browns bring a top-rated defense, while the Steelers have found a new life on the offensive side of the ball under head coach Mike McCarthy. But comparing the offense this year to last season reveals a startling discovery. It turns out that the Steelers are not that much different this year in terms of offensive execution.
There is one clear difference, however. And that difference is running back Jaylen Warren.
One of the biggest criticisms of the Steelers' offense last season under Arthur Smith and Mike Tomlin was their lack of pass game. They weren't able to put up explosive plays in the air and despite Aaron Rodgers' best efforts, the passing game never became a threat. According to game data from SumerSports, the Steelers' Expected Points Added (EPA) on passing plays ranked 16th in the NFL and 19th in success rate. By contrast, their run game ranked 12th in EPA and 10th in success rate. Steelers analyst for Steelers Now Derrick Bell shared an interesting bit of statistics comparing the team's offenses in 2025 and 2026 through seven games that illustrates this exact point.
Comparing the 2025 and 2026 Steelers offenses through the first 7 games: 2025: EPA/play: 18th Success rate: 17th Dropback EPA: 19th Dropback success rate: 26th Rushing EPA: 7th Rushing success rate: 6th 2026: EPA/play: 20th Success rate: 22nd Dropback EPA: 27th Dropback success… https://t.co/5NNKMQjauC
This season, the Steelers' offense has made some splash plays in the passing game and Rodgers has had some strong individual performances along the way. Still, the numbers show that this team hasn't come that far in their aerial attack. So far this season, the Steelers rank 26th in overall EPA per play as well as per pass play. Their success rate in the pass game is a measly 41.8%, ranking 22nd in the NFL.
The Steelers find themselves amongst the likes of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Miami Dolphins, the Indianapolis Colts and the Tennessee Titans through Week 7 of the regular season.
Once again, the run game is the complete opposite. The run game is 7th in the NFL in EPA per rush play. The success rate leaves a bit to be desired, at just 42.5%, but that figure is tied for 12th in the league currently.
Those numbers in 2025 got Arthur Smith fired. In 2026 they are being celebrated as progress.
And when you watch Jaylen Warren play, it's easy to understand why this offense is being lauded. Yes, Rodgers has played well, throwing 13 touchdowns and just five interceptions over the first seven games. He's completed 61.6% of his pass attempts, and he's made some crucial plays with his legs.
But the star of the offense is Jaylen Warren. It's undeniable. And what Warren does at an elite level is gain yards after contact. SumerSports has tallied 28 impact plays for Warren so far, the second-most of any running back in the NFL this season.
The thing is, it's not because the play design or offensive line play has paved the way for free runs. It's been quite the opposite. Warren is averaging 1.61 yards before contact per rush attempt, which ranks 21st amongst all NFL backs with at least one touch in 2026.
Getting to Warren isn't that helpful, as most defenses have discovered. After contact, he just keeps moving. He's posted 397 yards after contact, the sixth-most amongst NFL running backs. Per rush attempt, he's gaining an additional 3.84 yards after the first tackle attempt, which stands 8th in the NFL.
And if you think Warren is elite after contact while running the ball, just put him in space and see what happens. He's one of the most utilized running backs in the passing game this season, with 24 receptions on 34 targets. His 294 receiving yards are the second-most in the NFL among backs, and his 344 yards after the catch ranks first across all running backs with at least 10 touches, according to data from SumerSports.
And as Warren goes, so too does the Steelers' offense. Right now, he's playing like an MVP candidate. If that continues, the Steelers will stay right in the mix of the AFC North race. If he falters, the Steelers will too. That's because the only change in Pittsburgh this season is the focus and emphasis on Jaylen Warren.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Do the Seahawks Target a RB After Trading for Quenton Nelson?
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks made a major trade for the fourth consecutive year as they traded for eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts . This move is an instant improvement to the entire Seahawks offense and their offensive line, which has taken a slight regression this season. Seattle gets one of the best offensive linemen in the league, but they might not be done.
The Seahawks might still be in the market for a new starting running back or a great backup running back. The move for Nelson comes as veteran running back Zach Charbonnet is participating in his second week of practice and rookie running back Jadarian Price returns from his chest injury . There are still some questions with the running game, leading to the possibility of a trade.
There are several running backs that the Seahawks could be looking at. They’ve been reportedly linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor , who is in the prime of his career. There are indications that the Seahawks could go all-in on their offense and get Nelson’s teammate of six and a half seasons.
Seattle could also be looking into Philadelphia Eagles’ Saquon Barkley, Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ Bucky Irving or Tennessee Titans’ Tony Pollard. Each one of these running backs has a reason to ask for a new environment. Taylor would likely be the easiest running back for the Seahawks to trade for.
The Seahawks have endured an inconsistent running game this season through seven games. Among some of the biggest reasons are injuries at the running back position, the lack of explosiveness in Emanuel Wilson and George Holani and rough offensive line play . Nelson’s addition solves one of the problems, but Taylor’s addition could solve the other.
While there are some key reasons why the Seahawks could trade for Taylor or another running back, there are also reasons why they shouldn’t. The front office already invested a first-round pick in Price and they might want to see what he could be as the franchise No. 1 back. Price has had a rough start to his career, but it is still early.
General manager John Schneider builds his team through a big trade, but he also loves to build the roster from the NFL Draft . This front office did a great job letting go of one of their third-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft and their fifth-round pick in the 2028 NFL Draft. This allows Schneider to find talented young players and have them contribute early.
Seattle has struggled significantly on offense this season, but they are still favorably ranked in or near the top ten of major offensive categories. Seattle averages 113.7 rushing yards per game behind an offense that has Wilson and Holani as the main rushers.
The offense could be a lot more dangerous once Charbonnet and Price return to the lineup. There are some risks to relying on them, but Nelson is one of the most efficient run-blockers ; the Seahawks’ run game could take a big leap.

title: What Happens to Emanuel Wilson as Seahawks RBs Return from Injury?
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson may have made his final start of the season against the Kansas City Chiefs , but he went out with a bang.
Wilson ran for 100 yards on 24 carries as the Seahawks dismantled the Chiefs 20-3 inside Lumen Field. It was his best game with the Seahawks so far, but with rookie Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet potentially returning from injury this week, Wilson may find his role diminishing. However, he might still have a chance to carve out some carries in the backfield.
"I saw a guy that just refused to get tackled," offensive lineman Grey Zabel said of Wilson via the team website. "He just kept running hard and when you got a guy like that you're going to exert as much effort as you possibly can to make sure he succeeds. What an unbelievable guy, teammate, person and kudos to him, the work that he puts in to have a game like that is truly cool to see."
The Seahawks want to make sure they are as healthy as possible by the end of the season. To do that, they will need to ramp up Price and Charbonnet slowly over time. Both have suffered big injuries, especially Charbonnet, who tore his ACL in the playoffs last January.
The goal for the Seahawks should be to have all three of them healthy and available come playoff time. The way to do that is by divvying up their carries as evenly as possible over time.
That doesn't mean all three of them will receive the same number of carries every week, but ensuring that nobody gets overworked between now and the end of the season is incredibly important.
Wilson has proven himself when given the opportunity. He hasn't always been perfect, but he has stepped up enough to warrant some kind of role moving forward, even if Price and Charbonnet are at full strength.
If the Seahawks have more, it might as well be merrier in Seattle, and it's something that the offense should consider moving forward.
Wilson and the Seahawks are back in action on Monday Night Football in Week 8 as they welcome the Chicago Bears to town. Kickoff is scheduled for 5:15 pm PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on ESPN or stream it on the ESPN app.

title: 3 Takeaways from Seahawks' Quenton Nelson Trade
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are making a splash by acquiring All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts.
The Seahawks are sending a third-round pick in 2027 and a fifth-round selection in 2028 for Nelson, who is a free agent at the end of the season as his four-year, $80 million contract is set to expire.
Some members of the Seattle Seahawks On SI staff chimed in with their reactions to the trade.
"The Seahawks continue to be big buyers in the NFL Trade Deadline. While trading for a running back might be a more glamorous move, an elite guard like Quenton Nelson would be the best move now and in the future." — Michael Hanich
While speculation on a trade for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor has been in the air, it appears that the team settled for Nelson instead. This might not be the trade many were expecting, but it helps Seattle improve one of the weaker spots on the roster.
"He was a Pro Bowler in each of his first eight NFL seasons and could make it nine-for-nine in 2026. The former Golden Domer is a three-time First Team All-Pro who turned 30 years old in March. Nelson has played and started 136 regular season games and the only time he's missed was four games in 2021. Quality guards age well in the NFL and this is an excellent addition for the reigning Super Bowl champions." — Russell Baxter
Very few offensive linemen have the resume that Quenton Nelson does, and now he is with the Seahawks for a chance at winning a second straight Super Bowl. Seattle has broken their ceiling again, and that is a very strong place to be at the midway point in the season.
"While Grey Zabel and Anthony Bradford have been playing well at the guard position, the Seahawks knew they needed to make a change after Charles Cross went down with a high ankle sprain that should keep him out for a couple of weeks. While the fit isn't perfect and Seattle could have gone in a different direction, they put their foot down and made it clear they wanted to make an improvement." — Jeremy Brener
It would have been very easy for the Seahawks to sit back, let things play out with Cross's injury, and rely on the depth they have. Still, the Seahawks are showing that they want to win another Super Bowl, which is why they went out and made this move. They will figure out the fit over the next several weeks, but it's safe to say that the Seahawks are better today than they were yesterday.

title: 3 Reasons Why Seahawks Fleeced Colts in Quenton Nelson Trade
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are adjusting their roster after their Week 7 win against the Kansas City Chiefs.
The team acquired eight-time Pro Bowl offensive lineman Quenton Nelson in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts , sending a third- and fifth-round pick in exchange for one of the best offensive linemen in the league.
Here's a look at three reasons why Seahawks general manager John Schneider should be praised for the deal.
The Seahawks are viewed as one of the top teams in the league, but this trade could put them back in pole position for the NFC contender race by boosting one of their weak spots on the offensive line.
The Seahawks are sending a message to the league that they want to contend for another Super Bowl this season. They didn't want to waste the opportunity after offensive tackle Charles Cross went down with an injury against the Chiefs that should keep him out for a few weeks. That is going to create a very competitive trade deadline as other teams try to jostle for position.
The Seahawks are currently on tap for 12 draft picks going into next year before the Nelson trade. Now that number slides down to 11, but the number of compensatory draft picks coming to the Seahawks gives them the ability to make this trade.
The Seahawks should get compensatory picks in next year's draft after losing Riq Woolen, Kenneth Walker III, Boye Mafe, and Coby Bryant to free agency. On top of that, assistant general manager Nolan Teasley is heading to the Minnesota Vikings, which gives them an additional draft pick thanks to the Rooney Rule.
Having all of these picks allows Schneider to be a lot more aggressive when it comes to trading, and it's possible that this might not be his only move.
When it comes to compensatory picks, the Seahawks should be able to get one if Nelson doesn't re-sign in free agency. Nelson is in the final season of a four-year, $80 million contract that he signed in 2022 with the Colts.
It remains to be seen if this trade is merely a rental or the start of the second half of a potential Hall of Fame career for Nelson. Regardless of where that puts the Seahawks, they are winning in the end.
If Nelson is only on the books this season, the Seahawks will likely get a third-round pick in 2028 for losing out on him in free agency. This means the Seahawks are pretty much sending a fifth-round pick to the Colts for one of the league's top offensive linemen, making this a massive fleece.

title: How Quenton Nelson Immediately Transforms Seahawks Offensive Line
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks made a pre-trade deadline splash by acquiring guard Quenton Nelson on Tuesday from the Indianapolis Colts, adding an eight-time Pro Bowler and three-time All-Pro to their offensive front.
It’s a massive deal, as the Seahawks haven’t had a former All-Pro offensive lineman since left tackle Duane Brown (2017-21). Brown was five years removed from his last All-Pro season when he joined the Seahawks, and Nelson, 30, last earned the honor in 2020. Seattle gave up only a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to land Nelson and bolster its offensive line. Nelson could be a game-changer for the Seahawks’ run game and pass protection.
The first order of business is where Nelson is going to play. He’s been a left guard his entire nine-year NFL career, and 2025 No. 18 overall pick Grey Zabel currently fills that spot.
There’s good news there, however. Zabel played right guard in college at North Dakota State, and it seems likely that he will be shifted there to allow Nelson to fill in at left guard. That means Anthony Bradford, who is currently starting at right guard, would be headed to the bench.
That is somewhat negative, as Bradford played extremely well in his return from injury against the Kansas City Chiefs. He’s a tone-setter for the offensive line, but his talent and upside don’t surpass Zabel or Nelson.
Zabel moving to center is also a possibility, allowing Nelson to slot at left guard and Bradford to stay at right guard. That would send Jalen Sundell to the bench, but that situation seems far more unlikely than the former.
We've agreed to a trade with the Colts for G Quenton Nelson, pending physical. Read more » https://t.co/WP3pFRGkF1 pic.twitter.com/9Z0TU5H98n
Then there’s the major upside. The Seahawks’ run game had struggled this season before their win over the Chiefs in Week 7, and Nelson immediately improved that area of the offense. Quarterback Sam Darnold also got better protection, as one of Bradford’s drawbacks has been his subpar pass blocking.
With left tackle Charles Cross potentially sidelined for multiple weeks , this gives the Seahawks a better offensive line in the short and long term when Cross returns.
Seattle will have to pay Nelson at the end of the season, as he’s in the final year of his current contract. That’s the only major drawback of the deal if he doesn’t re-sign. If he does re-sign, the Seahawks should have high-level guard play for at least the next three to four years.
This is a transformative move by Seahawks general manager John Schneider, and one that significantly increases the offense’s chance to succeed in pursuit of a second-straight Super Bowl title.

title: 3 Risers and Fallers After Seahawks' Week 7 Win vs Chiefs
full_text:
It was a rough stretch, but the Seattle Seahawks (4-3) managed to get out of it thanks to their mini-bye and dedication to getting better. The Seahawks took care of business in Week 7 with a dominant 20-3 win at home versus the Kansas City Chiefs. This was a statement win for the Seahawks as they showed they are still the team to beat despite three losses.
​It was also a statement for some players as they make their mark moving forward . There are three players that made big statements that should should earn themselves bigger roles or keep them on the roster as changes like trades could be made. There were, however, three players who were either disappointments or will play less of a role on the team.
​There was a lot of heat on starting quarterback Sam Darnold after the disaster that caused the Seahawks to lose to the Denver Broncos. While his turnover issues aren’t fully gone, Darnold was able to control the Seahawks’ offense and consistently drive the ball down the field . There is more for him to completely earn the confidence of the 12, but it feels he has the complete respect of the coaching staff and locker room after a bad series of games.
​The Seahawks’ run game has been a mess the last few games , with rookie running back Jadarian Price and veteran running back Zach Charbonnet out. This left Emanuel Wilson and George Holani, who are both power backs, carrying the run game. While a good portion of Wilson’s 100 yards came in the final quarter, he showed resilience and the consistency to likely stick around as the third-string running back ahead of Holani.
​The star of the night was the Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense . This unit continues to show why they are at the top of the NFL.  While most of the starters are used to being at the front, linebacker Tyrice Knight made his second consecutive start for the Seahawks. Knight continues to show he is capable of being a full-time starter by accounting for eight total tackles, four solo tackles and a tackle for loss.
32-year-old edge rusher Dante Fowler Jr. isn’t the pass rush veteran of the Seahawks. He continues to get fewer reps on the Dark Side Defense. He only had seven defensive reps while accounting for only one quarterback hit but had no special team snaps for the first time this season. He is becoming less of a playable pass rusher to the point that the Seahawks might look into the NFL Trade Deadline for a more capable pass rusher.
​Starting right guard Anthony Bradford made his way back to the lineup after missing five games with an injury. As a result, the Seahawks made Christian Haynes the primary backup while rookie right guard Beau Stephens was a healthy inactive. He wasn’t a bad option for the Seahawks, but there was no stability on the right side of the offensive line with the rotation of Haynes and Stephens. He may still be in the second-string unit, but Stephens is at the bottom of the totem pole.
​The Seahawks signed rookie running back Robert Henry Jr. off the Washington Commanders’ practice squad following Joe Mixon’s failed physical. Henry has been on the Seahawks’ 53-man roster for three weeks and was a healthy inactive. With veteran Zach Charbonnet and rookie Jadarian Price, it is not likely that Henry will remain on the 53-man roster or, potentially, the practice squad.

title: Instant Grade: Seahawks Trade For Colts' Quenton Nelson
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are boosting their offensive line by acquiring Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson in a blockbuster trade. ESPN insider Adam Schefter was the first to report the news.
"Trade: Colts have agreed to send eight-time Pro-Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks, per me and @rapsheet. Nelson is on an expiring contract and the Colts are opting to get back draft capital now before they could lose him in free agency. But an all-time Colt now moves on to the Seahawks," Schefter tweeted.
The Seahawks have been missing Anthony Bradford for multiple weeks due to hip and knee injuries, so they had not been at full strength. Now, Nelson gives them a big boost on the offensive line for a run game that has struggled to stay consistent throughout the season.
Nelson, 30, was the No. 6 overall pick by the Colts back in 2018, out of Notre Dame. Since joining the NFL, he has been one of the league's top interior offensive linemen and has consistently been a top performer. Nelson has not missed a game since the 2021 season and has played nearly 9,000 snaps in his career.
Throughout most of his career, Nelson has been blocking for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor , who joined the team in 2020. Since entering the league, Taylor has the second-highest rushing yards total of any player in the NFL, behind Derrick Henry. His 8,185 yards are not due only to his own talent but also to the strength of the offensive line blocking for him.
Nelson now gets to block for the likes of Jadarian Price, Zach Charbonnet and Emanuel Wilson as they try to build a rushing attack that rivals the one from last season, with Kenneth Walker III leading the way.
With Nelson on board, the Seahawks have a better chance to have a more well-rounded offense, which is a big step in the right direction.
Nelson is in the final season of a four-year, $80 million contract that he signed in 2022. It's a heavy price for the Seahawks, but this is proof that they are trying to push for a second straight Super Bowl victory.
Nelson could make his debut on Monday Night Football when the Seahawks host the Chicago Bears. Kickoff is scheduled for 5:15 pm PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on ESPN or stream it on the ESPN app.

title: Week 8 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Seahawks Soaring After Dominant Win vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks went into Week 7 with some questions to answer. They lost three of their previous four games and were set to face the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs.
Not only were the Chiefs unbeaten, but they were dominating thanks to former Seahawks star Kenneth Walker III. The Seahawks, however, proved to be up to the challenge , winning 20-3. They shut down Walker and Patrick Mahomes , reminding us all why they're the defending champions .
Now as we enter Week 8, let's see what their big victory does for them in our latest NFL power rankings roundup.
Connor Orr was impressed with the way the Seattle defense shut down the Chiefs this week, and he's not alone. He also praised the way offensive coordinator Brian Fleury made some adjustments to get Sam Darnold back on track.
"Like Tommy Rees and Michael Penix Jr., Brian Fleury made some critical adjustments to the new Sam Darnold reality and it paid off in a big way. Of course, completely removing the opponent’s run game and bringing the hammer with Emanuel Wilson doesn’t hurt, either," Orr wrote.
ESPN ranked Seattle fifth and they decided to highlight every team's best addition this year. For Seattle, it's running back Emanuel Wilson, which seems surprising at first. The run game hasn't been great, but Wilson has kept things moving as they wait for Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet to return.
"With the Seahawks reserving all their big offseason deals for in-house extensions, they made a few bargain signings in free agency, including Wilson on a one-year, $1.6 million deal. Their run game has not been a strength, with rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price missing the past four games and Zach Charbonnet having yet to make his 2026 debut, but Wilson has helped keep it afloat. He has rushed for 403 yards (3.6-yard average) and three touchdowns, with another touchdown through the air," Brady Henderson wrote.
Ranking: 7 | Last week: 10
Chad Graff and Josh Kendall of The Athletic moved Seattle from No. 10 to No. 7 after knocking off Kansas City. Like just about everyone else, they walked away from this game wildly impressed with head coach Mike Macdonald and defensive coordinator Aden Durde.
"Mike Macdonald and Aden Durde’s defense must be terrifying for opposing quarterbacks. The Vikings’ defense gets all the attention, and rightly so. But the Seahawks are right behind Minnesota in most metrics, and that unit was dominant against the Chiefs on Sunday night."
Gary Davenport said the Seahawks needed their win against the Chiefs. They were in the midst of a struggle and falling to 3-4 would have been devastating. Still, they have a tough task coming up in Week 8 against the Chicago Bears and we can learn even more about them based on how they perform in that one.
"The road doesn't get any easier in the short term. Next week brings a visit from maybe the NFL's best offense in Caleb Williams and the Bears," Davenport wrote. "After dropping three of four, though, Seattle needed a performance like this."
Pete Prisco was happy with the defense, but he was really impressed that Seattle's rushing attack showed up. If they can continue to move the ball on the ground, they could become a major threat once again.
"The defense was outstanding in the victory over the Chiefs, but the really good news was the running game came alive. That's a must for this team's offense to succeed," Prisco wrote.

title: The Seahawks Offensive Line Shows the Value of Anthony Bradford
full_text:
I’m about to say something that might sound like a negative statement, maybe even an insult, but it’s really not. What I’m about to say applies to the Seattle Seahawks, but also to most teams in the NFL right now. There’s no definitive right way to go about how to construct an offensive line. So here it is: The Seahawks have built a finesse offensive line.
Again, this isn’t a bad thing. It just means the team has decided that’s what they wanted to have. Charles Cross , Grey Zabel, Jalen Sundell, and (to a perhaps slightly-lesser extent) Abraham Lucas are players who excel in space and hitting blocks on smaller, more agile defenders. Ask them to blast their way through big bodies man-on-man, and it’s a little dicier.
It’s the kind of offensive line you want to have with this sort of running scheme. Outside zone runs don’t work without offensive linemen that can reach those landmarks to clear the way. Sometimes, however, even a finesse team needs a hard-nosed run right through the middle of a defense, and there’s one man the Seahawks look to when that’s on the menu.
I don’t know if Anthony Bradford is a ‘good’ player in the traditional sense. He commits a lot of penalties, allows a shockingly-high pressure rate for a right guard, and his whiffs frequently end up on lowlight reels across the NFL meme circuit. There is a reason why professional evaluators and sites like Pro Football Focus take such a dim view of his game.
But he’s the only starter on this line with a real nasty edge to him . He’s the only one big and strong enough to routinely dominate reps against the big uglies in the middle. He can take control of a rep and clear out a big hole, while also possessing the athletic ability to not be completely lost when asked to play on the move. That has clear value.
I couldn’t blame anyone for not being blown away by what the Seahawks did on the ground against the Kansas City Chiefs. 3.5 yards per carry on traditional runs to a back is typically not winning football. But consider that lead back Emanuel Wilson (who is the third string back on this team when health permits) was able to grind out 4.2 yards a crack.
Also consider how the Seahawks ran the ball for much of the night. There was a lot of jamming it up the middle into traffic, trying to grind out a few yards and not much more, just to keep the offense on schedule. When you run it like that, you need someone that can just clear your opponents out of the way. And Bradford is that. Something to keep in mind.

title: The Seahawks Have Improved Defensively From Last Season, Improbably
full_text:
By many metrics, the Seattle Seahawks had the best defense in the NFL in 2025 . But they were surely going to take a step back this year after the offseason they had. Coby Bryant and Riq Woolen both departed and were replaced by in-house pieces, and Boye Mafe was swapped out for post-June 1st free agent signing Dante Fowler Jr.
Leonard Williams, Jarran Reed, DeMarcus Lawrence, and Uchenna Nwosu were a year older. The defensive rookies the team brought in were not especially ballyhooed, and have contributed nothing so far. It’s a pretty obvious recipe for regression, a step back. But are they actually worse on the field through seven games? It doesn’t seem like it.
The Seahawks have allowed 17.9 points per game so far this year , a tiny step down from last year’s 17.2. Consider, however, how many of those points have been allowed on short fields, or no field at all. The defense has allowed touchdown drives of 21, 43, 18, and 11 yards, field goal drives of 26 and 8 yards, and two defensive scores.
To understand the significance of those short fields, Seattle is #1 by a wide margin in yards allowed per game (233.9), miles better than last year’s 285.6. They’re also historic in yards per play allowed at just 4.0, a massive improvement over the 4.7 number from 2025, and the best number any defense has produced this century. So far, it sure looks better to me.
If you go to advanced analytics, the argument gets even stronger. -0.118 EPA per play is second best in the league this year thanks to the Vikings getting off to a historic start, but it’s slightly better than their marks last year of -0.113. Their success rate allowed is significantly stronger, all the way down at 36.5% from 40.1% last year. Somehow, someway, they’re better.
Some have suggested this is partially a product of the schedule thus far. It’s not an entirely unfounded claim, but the thing that really catches my attention is how well this defense has played the last three weeks against Kyle Shanahan, Sean Payton, and Andy Reid. Three of the brightest offensive minds this century. That’s not something to ignore.
The Patriots are having some issues putting up points, but they’re a top ten team in yards and EPA. The 49ers and Chiefs are among the league’s best offenses so far. Even the Commanders and Cardinals are more below average than bad. Maybe the rest of the schedule is a little tougher offensively, especially with McVay looming twice, but that doesn’t tell the whole story.
Also, consider this team has played (essentially) two games without Nick Emmanwori, two without Drake Thomas , four without Ty Okada, and one without Julian Love. They’re here in part because they’re getting plus play out of players like Tyrice Knight, Rodney Thomas II, and Nehemiah Pritchett. For all we know, they’ll improve as we get deeper into the season.
The offense’s struggles have made it somewhat hard to notice, but it seems pretty definitive at this moment. This defense has experienced no drop-off from 2025, and is actually better so far. Maybe we won’t be saying this after encounters with the Bears, 49ers, Cowboys, and the Rams twice, but after the last few games, I would give them every benefit of the doubt.

title: Why the 49ers Still Believe in Eddy Pineiro
full_text:
Surprisingly, Eddy Pineiro didn't cost the San Francisco 49ers their first loss of the season against the Atlanta Falcons .
He's lucky the whole team played sloppily against Atlanta, so it didn't come down to him. He did, however, miss another extra point. Pineiro has the yips .
There's no denying that. With Pineiro kicking poorly this season, he's bound to be the reason the 49ers lose a game, maybe in the playoffs.
Now that the 49ers are on their Bye Week, they should explore kicker options. They cannot continue like this, but it seems they're okay with it, given John Lynch's latest comments.
"We don't have a kicker tryout. We have a lot of belief in Eddie," Lynch said to Bay Area radio station KNBR. "He has had a tough run early this year, but we extended Eddie for his body of work with us but then throughout the history of his career. He's going through a rough patch right now....We have belief in Eddie, and we're going to ride with him."
#49ers John Lynch on Eddy Piñeiro: "We don't have a kicker tryout. We have a lot of belief in Eddie. He has had a tough run early this year, but we extended Eddie for his body of work with us but then throughout the history of his career. He's going through a rough patch right… pic.twitter.com/QGH23qUJg4
Notice how Lynch mentioned that the 49ers extended Pineiro in the offseason. That plays a significant role in keeping him. Or, in this case, "believing" in him.
If there's one thing the 49ers don't like, it's admitting fault with a player they liked and added. Remember, it did take them a long time to cut ties with Jake Moody.
The 49ers didn't want to deal with the poor optics of cutting a third-round kicker so soon, even though the optics were bad from the moment they drafted Moody.
It's also the reluctance to pull the plug so soon on a player they just invested in. It makes sense from that standpoint, but it's only because Pineiro hasn't cost the 49ers games.
Once that happens, and it feels inevitable, that is when they will start to consider their options. I'm not sure how the 49ers can prevent that from happening.
Their one and only saving grace is the Bye Week. It allows Pineiro to get away, giving him a mental reset. He can come back after the Bye as if nothing had happened prior.
Anytime a kicker has the yips, it's mostly, if not all, mental. There's nothing the 49ers can do to significantly help him. If he can't get it together after the Bye Week, he never will.
Should his struggles continue, they would be foolish not to look at other kickers. Otherwise, they risk Pineiro being the reason their 2026 season comes to a disappointing end.

title: 49ers Acquiring DeForest Buckner Corrects a Past Mistake
full_text:
DeForest Buckner is returning to the San Francisco 49ers after they traded a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .
Earlier today, the Seattle Seahawks acquired All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson from the Colts. The 49ers needed to respond to Seattle's move by going after Buckner.
Sure enough, they make it happen and instantly bolster their defensive line. This was a no-brainer trade for the 49ers to execute.
It's more than just matching the Seahawks' trade for Nelson, which is obviously great. But the 49ers were desperate for a premier player on the defensive line .
With Nick Bosa struggling to stay healthy this season, the 49ers' pass rush has looked like it's 2025 version. It's been nearly nonexistent.
They caught fire in Weeks 5 and 6, thanks to an amazing collective effort, but it isn't a sustainable formula. Having an elite player who can dominate and draw attention was the missing piece in their defense.
That is why the 49ers needed Bosa back so badly. However, they couldn't solely rely on Bosa returning. Odds are he will miss time again with another injury whenever his calf is fine.
With Buckner, the 49ers get a player who will be significantly impactful against the run and as a pass rusher. Buckner has tallied 21 run stops, four sacks, and 17 pressures this season.
His presence will dramatically help Osa Odighizuwa, Gracen Halton, and Romello Height. And if Bosa returns and somehow stays healthy, the 49ers' defense goes from great to overpowered.
All the defense was missing was a monstrous defensive lineman. It didn't matter if it was Maxx Crosby, Khalil Mack, or whoever. They just needed an addition to make their pass rush lethal.
That said, Buckner was the right player for the 49ers to trade for over Crosby and Mack. He's been one of, if not the best, defensive tackles in the NFL in 2026.
He's been one of the best since 2019, which is what led the Colts to acquire him from the 49ers in the first place. Now that he's back, it feels like the 49ers are correcting a past mistake.
Buckner probably should've never been traded in the first place, even though there was sound logic behind it. He had been through tough times with the 49ers before they finally broke through in 2019.
Since that season, the 49ers have been Super Bowl contenders every season. Buckner deserves credit for getting the ball rolling for the 49ers.
And now, he's back where it all started, with the hope of finally helping the 49ers win their sixth Super Bowl.

title: 49ers 3 Biggest Disappointments At The Bye Week
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are sitting at 6-1 at the bye week , so there is not too much to get discouraged over. However, the team has had some disappointing developments. What are the biggest disappointments through the first seven weeks of the 2026 season?
Another year, more injury problems. The team cannot escape it. They signed Mike Evans despite injury concerns, and those have popped up. The same can be said with Deebo Samuel. Injuries are starting to become a known story for Nick Bosa as well.
Still, some have been more random. Rookie De’Zhaun Stribling has not been healthy. Marques Sigle and Upton Stout have missed time in the secondary. Both Alfred Collins and C.J. West got injured up front. The bye week is expected to help get the team healthy. At the same time, the expectation is for a new name to pop up in a week or two.
The 49ers went out of their way to improve the secondary depth this offseason. Now, they enter the bye week wondering if secondary help is another need. Nate Hobbs has not been healthy. With Stout and Sigle out, the depth got exposed.
Jack Jones has been an awful development this year. The team signed him cheaply, and while he started the past two years, he is unplayable in San Francisco right now.
Still, with Stout out, he has to either play on the outside so Deommodore Lenoir can slide into the slot, or they need to play safety Ashtyn Davis in the slot. Davis was picked on relentlessly in the Commanders' comeback in Week 6.
They have Ephesians Prysock as the only depth cornerback they have not tried. The 49ers almost have to play him after the bye week. If they want to run any dime formations moving forward, something has to change.
The 2025 draft class has not hit the ground running in year two. To be fair, injuries are not helping. Collins and West are out, and Mykel Williams just came back from injury. Nick Martin has been hurt all season, and now Upton Stout and Marques Sigle join him on the injured list.
Meanwhile, Jordan Watkins and Jordan James have been unable to climb the depth chart. Lastly is Connor Colby, who started hot but has fallen apart in recent weeks. They need this group to show a lot more.

title: Why the 49ers Should Extend Dre Greenlaw After This Season
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers bringing back Dre Greenlaw was always going to be one of the more popular moves they made this offseason.
The reasons behind that are obvious: he’s one of Kyle Shanahan’s favourite players , he has an excellent partnership with Fred Warner, and letting him go was a decision the 49ers likely came to regret internally.
Greenlaw spent one season with the Denver Broncos before returning on a one-year, prove-it deal, which, seven weeks into the new season, has shown he has proven it. And arguably exceeded many people's expectations, too.
Hear me out. Greenlaw's departure, in some ways, made sense. After his Achilles injury in the Super Bowl, he only played two games the following season, and that was somewhat justified given he only played eight games in Denver amid further injury problems.
Ten games in two seasons after rehabbing one of the worst injuries a player can suffer, alongside other injuries, made bringing him back on a one-year deal both sensible and understandable.
Now, the 49ers are heading into the bye week at 6-1 for the season, and Greenlaw has been healthy all season long. The only game he missed came in Week 6, following an altercation when things got a bit too heated against the Seattle Seahawks. He was ejected and received a one-game ban as a result.
Everybody knows how fiery Greenlaw is, and while that decision wasn't the best, even with Seahawks players swarming him, a one-game ban was the appropriate punishment.
With the negatives out of the way, the positives are that he's recorded 49 total tackles, 22 solo and 27 assists, alongside one forced fumble. No sacks, but the statistics are decent all the same.
It's natural to expect him to be slightly off given his injury history, but in some respects, he's exceeded all expectations. He has the second-highest snap count with 287, which is considerably less than the obvious name, but the 49ers are managing his workload well, and the returns are there.
In addition, Pro Football Focus ranks Greenlaw 14th of 75, with an overall defensive grade of 73.3. It's almost halfway through the season, and maintaining that level is the next requirement, but Greenlaw's return to San Francisco is exactly what it would have hoped for when the front office brought him back on a prove-it deal.
A multi-year extension should be on the table. Greenlaw's impact so far has warranted a prolonged second stint in San Francisco.

title: How 49ers Should Respond to Seahawks Acquiring Quenton Nelson
full_text:
Let the NFC West midseason arms race begin.
The Seattle Seahawks are acquiring All-Pro offensive guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .
Seattle bolsters their offensive line immediately. Their run and pass game will ascend with Nelson, making it tougher for the San Francisco 49ers in their next matchup.
The 49ers cannot sit back and watch the Seahawks make moves to improve their team. They must respond to Seattle acquiring Nelson, and I know just how they should do it.
Trading for DeForest Buckner is the perfect response to the Seahawks' acquisition of Nelson. It's been a move that has made too much sense for the 49ers in the last few weeks.
Buckner can significantly boost their defensive front, which desperately needs a premier player to lead their pass rush. It's been ineffective with Nick Bosa out with a calf injury .
Buckner would come in and immediately make a massive impact. And with the Seahawks getting Nelson, he's the perfect response because he can go head-to-head with Nelson as a defensive tackle.
It would also be hilarious for the 49ers to match the Seahawks' move by trading with the Colts since they were the ones who incited the 49ers to make a move.
This is the best way for the 49ers to stay on par with, if not ahead of, the Seahawks. What played a significant role in beating the Seahawks in Week 5 was their pass rush.
It surprisingly came alive, thanks to a collective effort. The 49ers sacked Sam Darnold five times and pressured him on nearly half of his dropbacks.
That is the key to beating the Seahawks. It's by making Darnold uncomfortable, which led him to make errant throws and decisions throughout the game.
The 49ers won't be able to replicate that again without a premier player. Bosa should be back after the Bye, but there's no telling when or if he'll get hurt again.
Relying on Bosa would be foolish for the 49ers. They need to pull the trigger on a trade for a defensive lineman, with Buckner as the most glaring move.
The Colts are in a fire sale. They are the easiest team to trade with right now. The 49ers could probably get Buckner for a third-round pick as well.
But if they need to give up a second-rounder, so be it. That costs nothing if it means increasing the chances of making the Super Bowl.
